### Diagrams (P5.26)

- **2026-10-11 — Diagram on React Flow and dagre, `@veljaos/ui/diagram` (P5.26, owner: "React Flow (MIT) with dagre (MIT), a BPMN-style notation drawn by us with tokens; no bpmn-js, no BPMN XML").** `packages/ui/src/diagram/`: `diagram.tsx` (the component and its state), `diagram-nodes.tsx` (a step, a lane, a connection, drawn inside React Flow), `diagram-parts.tsx` (run summary and attention, problems, the steps list, the three dialogs, the kinds' glyphs), `diagram-logic.ts` (pure, tested: `layoutDiagram`, `stepOrder`, `diagramKeyTarget`, `keyMoveDelta`, `addStepOperations`, `removeStepOperations`, `applyDiagramOperations`, `canConnect`, `connectionTargets`, `positionAfter`, `nextDiagramId`, `runCounts`, `problemsByTarget`, `drawnX`/`layoutX`), `diagram.css`.
  1. **A subpath of its own** (tsup entry `diagram`, `exports["./diagram"]`), as `@veljaos/ui/charts` and `@veljaos/ui/rich-text`: only `dist/diagram.js` names `@xyflow/react` and `@dagrejs/dagre` (checked in the build), so an application without diagrams never loads them. The root `@veljaos/ui` exports nothing of it. The consumer-check app renders an editing `Diagram` from the packed subpath (`apps/consumer-check/src/DiagramExample.tsx`, not a protected file; `check.mjs` is unchanged).
  2. **React Flow's style sheets are not shipped** — both `style.css` and `base.css` carry raw colours. `diagram/diagram.css` keeps only what positions and layers React Flow's parts (adapted from `base.css`, MIT, noted in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) with Liro tokens for every colour, imported into the base layer of `styles.css` so any utility wins (checked: no hex, rgb or hsl in the shipped rules). React Flow lays its canvas out in physical coordinates (`direction: ltr` on its root), so `left`/`top` in that file are the canvas's axes, not page layout; the diagram mirrors itself for right-to-left. The attribution is hidden (`proOptions.hideAttribution`) — see "Open" below.
  3. **The notation, drawn with tokens:** a task is a 176px box (radius md, 1.5px `border.control`, which keeps 3:1 against every surface, WCAG 1.4.11), at least 64px high, its name 13px medium centred and wrapping (never cut); a user task carries a person, an automatic (service) task a cog, a sub-process the BPMN + square. Events are 36px circles (start thin, end a 3px `text.primary` ring, timer and message a double ring with a clock or an envelope); decisions (exclusive) and parallel paths are 44px diamonds with X or +. An event's or a decision's name stands under it (start-to-end, 120px wide) or beside it at the end side (top-to-bottom). Connections are lines with rounded corners in `border.control` (3:1), an arrowhead, the default way out marked with the BPMN slash near its start, and a condition as an HTML label beside the last stretch before the arrow (so the branches of one decision never share a place). Lanes are labelled bands, every other one on `surface.hover`.
  4. **Layout:** without positions, dagre places the ranks along the flow — `layout="start-to-end"` (the default; mirrored in right-to-left: x is measured from the leading edge and drawn as `-(x + width)`) or `"top-to-bottom"`; ranks 64px apart, steps 40px; a condition gets its room. A step with a `position` keeps it (positions are in the layout's coordinates, so a stored diagram is the same in both directions). With lanes, each lane becomes a band in the order of `lanes` (start-to-end one under another under a 40px label row, top-to-bottom side by side); its steps keep their place along the flow. **Two passes:** React Flow measures the steps after they are drawn; the layout runs again with the measured sizes, then the view is fitted (24px around, never above 100%; with the overview, room under it) — `data-ready` says when, and the canvas stays hidden only until that first fit. It is drawn once the fonts are ready (as the charts); a later font refits in place. **Found by the pictures:** a font arriving during Playwright's full-page capture hid the canvas for a moment (edges and labels inherit the hidden state, React Flow's nodes set their own visibility), so the hiding is for the first fit only and readiness does not depend on the font generation.
  5. **Keyboard (view, run and edit):** every step is a Tab stop, in the flow's order (`stepOrder`), named by its kind, name, lane, state and problems ("User task: Director approves. Lane: Management"), described by the instructions. The arrow along the flow (forward in the reading direction, or down) goes to the connection out of a step and on to the step it leads to; the opposite arrow back; the other two arrows move between the connections out of one step (a decision's branches, ordered as drawn); Home and End go to the first and last step (`diagramKeyTarget`, tested in both directions and both layouts). Connections take the focus (tabindex −1), named "Connection from A to B. Condition. Default". React Flow's own keyboard handling, delete, selection and pan keys are off (`disableKeyboardA11y`, the key codes `null`); its role "application" stays, with the diagram's name. A focused step outside the view is brought into it.
  6. **Edit** (`mode="edit"`, never on a phone): a palette of the kinds at the start (click adds after the chosen step; drag places it — pointer events, a lifted chip with `shadow-lg`, touch after a 250ms press, never HTML drag and drop); with a step chosen, the bar above offers "Add step after…" (a menu of kinds), "Connect to…" (a dialog listing the steps it may lead to, with an optional condition), "Rename…" and "Remove"; with a connection chosen, "Label…" (the condition, and for a decision's way out "Default way out, when no condition holds") and "Remove". Added after a step with exactly one way out, the new step goes in between (that connection's condition and default mark move to the first half). Connecting also by dragging between the handles (a 2px point on the shape, a 10px dot, a 24px target; blue only while connecting — the focus colour, D17). A step moves by dragging or, chosen with Enter, by the arrow keys (8px, Shift 40px, measured from the leading edge, `keyMoveDelta`), Escape lets go; F2 renames, Delete removes, a double click renames. A chosen step or connection is `surface.selected` with a 2px `border.selected` (neutral). **Every change is reported** through `onChange` as operations (`add-step`, `remove-step`, `rename-step`, `move-step`, `add-connection`, `remove-connection`, `label-connection`, `set-default-connection`); nothing is saved — `applyDiagramOperations` is what an application does with them. New ids from `newId` (default "step-1", "connection-1", the first free). Every change is announced in a polite status region. **Every drag has another way** (WCAG 2.5.7): palette by click, connection by "Connect to…", move by the keys.
  7. **Problems** (`problems`, the application's validation messages): a step or connection with a problem is drawn in `status.danger.fg` (2px) with a danger badge (its count when more than one), and the list above the canvas ("3 problems", danger tone) names each with its target and a "Go to" (named "Go to <step>") that brings the step into view, gives it the keyboard and, in edit, chooses it.
  8. **Run** (`mode="run"`, `run`): each step's state from the application as an icon, words and a status tone — done (success), running (neutral, 2px `text.primary` outline), waiting (warning), failed (danger, its reason under it), skipped and not reached (dashed, muted) — never blue for a state (D17). The connections the run went along (`run.path`) are drawn strong in `text.primary`, the others dashed. Above the canvas: the run's status (the application's label and tone), "5 of 11 steps done" and "1 failed" (counts through `format.number`), and the application's line; under it, each step with actions (a failed step's Skip and Retry, the main last) in a danger or neutral block with its name, state and reason — **not inside the canvas**, where they would shrink with the zoom below 24px (found by axe's target-size rule on a phone); the buttons are named "Retry: <step>". `onStepAction(stepId, key)`.
  9. **Phones** (below 48em, or `screen="phone"`; the prop is not `layout`, which names the direction): view and run as on a desktop, the diagram fitted to the width (zoom with the buttons); edit shows "Open this diagram on a larger screen to change it." and the diagram as in view. **The steps list** ("Show steps as a list", `defaultView="steps"` restores it): the steps in the flow's order with kind, lane, state, reason, actions, problems and "Next: Manager approves (Up to 100.000,00 RSD), Director approves (…)" (an `Intl.ListFormat` of the locale) — the diagram's text alternative everywhere.
  10. **States:** `loading` (a skeleton in the canvas's place, `aria-busy`), no steps ("No steps yet"; in edit, the palette and "Add the first step from the palette."), `error` (the message and Retry), as the charts.
  - Messages (new, at the end of `messages.ts` under "P5.26 ── Diagram"): the kinds (`diagram.start` … `diagram.parallel`; "Automatic task", "Decision", "Parallel paths" in words a business user reads), the states, `diagram.stepName`, `inLane`, `connectionName`, `defaultFlow`, `defaultWay`, the instructions, zoom, list, problems, `goTo`, `goToButton`, `next`, `nextStep`, `runSummary`, `failedCount`, `stepState`, `stepAction`, empty / loading / error / retry, `editOnLargerScreen`, the palette, the edit actions, the dialogs and the announcements.

### Legal information (P5.27)

- **2026-10-11 — Legal information: the decisions the owner left open (P5.27, owner's request of
  2026-10-11).** Laws, by-laws, court decisions, opinions and a company's internal acts, on the
  invoice's DocumentPage layout, with nothing new where a component fits. Built on one shared
  model (`components/legal-model.ts`: act, versions, amendments, headings and articles with
  paragraphs, items and inline references, footnotes, related acts, practice, notes); every text,
  date, status and reference is the application's, the library presents it. No new dependency.
  1. **The table of contents is a start-side Drawer on every width** (LegalContents), opened by
     "Contents" in the act's toolbar: one pattern for desktop and phone; the side panel keeps the
     act's relations (versions, history, hierarchy, references, practice, notes), and a contents
     tree of 300 articles would crowd it.
  2. **Compare is inline, one column, on every width** (LegalCompare): the same view on a phone
     and a desktop, the act keeps its reading width, and assistive technology reads one sequence.
     Insertions are `ins` (underlined, with "Added:" for assistive technology), deletions `del`
     (struck through, "Deleted:"), with a visible legend and a badge per article: never colour
     alone.
  3. **The library may compute a word diff** between two texts it is given (`wordDiff`, pure,
     unit-tested, no dependency) and **transliterate Serbian Cyrillic to Latin**, one to one
     (`transliterateCyrillicToLatin`); Latin to Cyrillic is the application's text, since that
     direction is not one to one.
  4. **A long act is windowed** (LegalText `maxHeight`, the trees' row window), and **the search
     in the act runs on the data, not on the DOM**, so it counts and finds articles that are not
     drawn (the 320-article story).
  5. **The version picker is a SelectField of the application's versions**, named by their days
     (not a date field that resolves a version): a choice names exactly one text.
  6. **Invented data only:** the gazette itself is invented ("Illustrative Gazette"), so no real
     gazette number is ever attached to invented text; every act page of the examples says
     "Illustrative"; no text is taken from a legal database. Statuses in the examples: In force
     success, Partly in force warning, Not yet in force neutral, No longer in force danger, Final
     (a decision or an opinion) success — never blue.
  7. **The examples are joined:** the act pages (group O) show LegalText with LegalContents in the
     toolbar; "Compare versions" and "Compare with…" open a comparison page (two SelectFields for
     the earlier and the later version, LegalCompare under them; every pair of the law's four
     versions and the rulebook's two); the search's results (group P) link to the act pages'
     routes.

- **2026-10-11 — LegalText (P5.27 b).**
  1. **The text as given:** `nodes` (headings and articles of `legal-model.ts`) and `footnotes`;
     the library decides nothing legal. Reading width at most 70ch at the start side. Headings
     are real headings from `headingLevel` (default 2) down by depth — the number of headings
     above, not the data's `level`, so an act that skips a level keeps a valid outline; an
     article's label and title are its heading (label sm secondary above the title md, or the
     label md alone). Paragraphs with their label, items and sub-items as nested lists 24px in,
     emphasis, footnote marks linking to the footnotes under the text. Every block
     TEXT_DIRECTION; labels ("1)", "(1)") TEXT_ISOLATE.
  2. **Article actions:** "Copy link to Article 5" (28px, desktop) calls `onCopyLink(article)`;
     **without it** the library copies the article's `href`, made absolute against the page
     (`new URL(href, location.href)`), with `navigator.clipboard` and confirms with
     `notice.success(messages['legal.linkCopied'])` (error: `legal.copyFailed`) — the
     application mounts the Toaster. The article's label is a toggle button (`aria-pressed`,
     at least 24px high) when `onArticleSelect` is given: selected = surface.selected with the
     border.selected bar (SELECTED_BAR) and `data-liro-surface="selected"` (D17). The
     application's actions (`articleActions(article)`: a note, a bookmark) stand in a "⋯" menu
     (with Select / Clear selection). **Phones:** one "Actions for Article 5" menu holds Copy
     link, Select and the application's actions.
  3. **Change marks** under the heading, xs: each change `messages['legal.change'](label, date)`
     ("Amended by No. 47/2018 · applies from 01.07.2018.") in text.secondary with a History icon;
     an article not yet in force "Applies from 01.01.2027." in status.premium.fg, medium, with a
     CalendarClock icon. Never blue. **A deleted article** shows its words (`deleted`, data) in
     text.secondary; when it still carries its earlier text, "Show text" (`aria-expanded`) opens
     it muted behind a 2px border.default line at the start; `defaultShownDeleted` opens it at
     first (a restored state). A search hit in its earlier text opens it, so every hit counted is shown.
  4. **References** are links through `linkComponent` (text.link, underlined). With
     `resolveTarget(target)` a 24px preview button (Eye, "Preview of Article 4") follows each
     link and opens the target article in a Popover (label · title, paragraphs, items, "Open
     Article 4"); "This text is not available here." when the application has no text. Not
     modal: Escape returns the focus to the button, Tab leaves it, nothing traps the focus. Its
     side is chosen once from where the button stands (`previewSide`, below unless the room
     below is under 320px and there is more above; `avoidCollisions` off), so the picture never
     flips. The button sits in the line (−4px block margin), so the line height does not change.
     `defaultPreview` (an `href`) opens the first reference to it at first, without taking the
     focus. **Not done:** opening on hover or on the link's focus (the brief allowed the button
     instead; one way for every input).
  5. **Search in the act** runs on the data (`legalSearchIndex` once per text, `searchLegalIndex`
     per query; from 2 characters): case-, Latin-accent- and Serbian-script-insensitive (the
     query and the text are folded: lower case, Cyrillic as Latin, accents of Latin letters
     removed, đ as d; Japanese voiced kana and Arabic marks kept), in reading order, places in
     the drawn text, so it finds articles that are not drawn. Searched: headings' and articles'
     labels and titles, deletion words, paragraphs, items; not footnotes. Hits are `mark` on
     status.warning.bg (as CommandPalette's), the current one also underlined 2px and
     `aria-current` (more than colour). The field (`role="search"`, "Search in the text",
     `dir="auto"`), previous / next (36px, disabled without hits), "3 of 12" / "No matches"
     (`aria-live="polite"`). Enter next, Shift+Enter previous, going round. Typing and stepping
     bring the current hit into view (`scrollIntoView` center; in a long act the window scrolls
     to its article first). A restored search (`defaultSearch`, `defaultHit`) does not scroll
     (stable pictures). Controlled through `search` / `onSearchChange`; `showSearch={false}`
     hides it.
  6. **Serbian:** `lang` sr-Cyrl… with `script` / `defaultScript` 'latin' shows every text of
     the act (labels, titles, deletion and change words, paragraphs, footnotes, previews) in
     Latin through `transliterateCyrillicToLatin`, and the text's `lang` becomes sr-Latn. The
     switch (the neutral segmented control, "Latin" / "Cyrillic") stands at the toolbar's end
     when the act is Cyrillic, or Latin with `onScriptChange` (Latin to Cyrillic is the
     application's text).
  7. **Long acts:** with `maxHeight` the text scrolls in its own region (focusable, named by
     `label`) and draws only the entries in view — the trees' row window (`useTreeWindow`,
     tree-window.ts, so `virtual-rows.ts`'s rules: 600px overscan, the focused entry kept drawn,
     spacers), each entry measured once drawn (estimate `LEGAL_ENTRY_ESTIMATE` 160px). Without
     `maxHeight` every entry is drawn (short acts, the page scrolls). The 320-article story draws
     fewer than 40 articles.
  8. `ref.revealNode(id)` brings a heading or article into view (drawing it first) and focuses
     its heading (`tabIndex -1`); entries keep a scroll margin under the shell's sticky top.

## The owner's review of Phase 5 part 2 (P5.28)

- **2026-10-13 — How P5.28 was done (owner's brief).** The owner's Storybook review of Phase 5 part 2 (BUILD-PLAN P5.28: A 1–12 across the library, B 13–18 screens, C 19–22 bigger pieces, D 23–27 floor plans), in one branch. Each finding was fixed as a class — the library, its stories and the examples searched for the same fault, every occurrence fixed — and each general rule is written below and in AGENTS.md (D11, D19–D28). Helpers worked on independent parts (dates and grids; phones; one-record dialogs, toned actions and moves; the documents; POS; the dialogs left in other helpers' files; the follow-up of the sticky headers) and their branches were merged into `bp/P5.28-owner-review`. The floor plans (items 23–27) have entries of their own.

### Phones (P5.28 items 1, 5, 11, 13)

- **2026-10-13 — A phone frame is a phone's screen (P5.28 items 1, 5 and 11).** `PhoneFrame` (`packages/ui/src/components/story-frames.tsx`, stories only) is now the screen of a phone, not a clipping box: the frame (390 × 844, `data-liro-phone-frame`) has the transform that makes it the containing block of every fixed element inside it, and `overflow: clip`; inside it a scroll container (`data-liro-phone-page`, full height, scrollbar not drawn, `overscroll-behavior: contain`) holds the page. The page scrolls inside the frame as on a phone — the sticky header and the sticky bottom bars stay in place, a long page can be read to its end — while fixed elements (backdrops, dialogs, sheets, the toaster) stay on the frame, because their containing block is the frame, outside the scrolling. A picture (the visual tests, a full-page screenshot) is still the frame's first screen, 390 × 844. **Cause of "Move early to… darkens only the top band" (item 5), found:** the frame had `overflow: hidden`; a hidden overflow can still be scrolled by the browser, and a dialog's focus brought an element into view by scrolling the whole frame, so the fixed backdrop — positioned in the frame — moved up with it and left the lower part of the screen undimmed (measured: the backdrop 109px above the frame in "Invoice, phone" after "Search…"). `overflow: clip` cannot be scrolled; the page scrolls in its own container. The automated check (below) asserts that every backdrop covers the whole screen. A frame's page that scrolls but has nothing to focus (printouts) gets `tabindex="0"` from the frame itself (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`); stories need no change.
- **2026-10-13 — The screen context (P5.28).** The frame tells the components inside that they are on a phone through an internal context (`packages/ui/src/provider/screen.ts`, not exported): `usePhone()` (and `useBelowMd()`) answer true inside a frame whatever the window's width, and every floating content — select lists, popovers, menus and submenus, tooltips — takes the frame as Radix's collision boundary, so it keeps inside the frame as it keeps inside the viewport on a real phone. Before, a component in a phone frame inside a wide window drew its desktop layout unless the story passed `layout="phone"`, and its floating lists measured the window, so they ran off the frame. In an application nothing sets the context: the viewport is the screen.
- **2026-10-13 — Floating content never runs off the screen (P5.28 item 1).** Rules in the primitives, for every user at once: a select list, popover, menu, submenu and tooltip keep 8px inside the screen (`collisionPadding` 8, Mantine's default) and are never wider than the room there (`max-width` = Radix's available width); a long option, menu item or tooltip wraps (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`; the tooltip is one line as wide as its text up to that width). On a phone a popover or menu always moves to stay on the screen, even where a component chose a fixed side for a stable desktop picture (`avoidCollisions={false}`: LegalText's reference preview, CalendarView's day list, the legal search's sort menu). Width limits written in `vw` (`max-w-[calc(100vw-32px)]` in ListPage's view menu and the notifications panel, `calc(100vw-2rem)` in LookupField's list) measured the window, not the frame; they now follow the popover's own limit.
- **2026-10-13 — Dialogs on phones are bottom sheets (P5.28 items 1 and 5).** On a phone (`usePhone`) every Dialog, ConfirmDialog (and its presets) and any dialog built on the dialog or alert-dialog primitive is a sheet across the screen's full width on its bottom edge: as high as its content up to the screen's height less 40px (the page above shows it is a sheet over the page), radius lg on its top corners, sliding up 200ms, the bottom safe area as padding (`PHONE_DIALOG` in `primitives/classes.ts`). Its size ('wide') does not apply on a phone. The desktop dialog's `5dvh` / `90dvh` / `90vw` are now percentages of its containing block — the same on a page, and the frame (not the window) in a story. Drawers were already full width on a phone (`max-w-full`); LookupDialog and the company switcher stay full-screen sheets.
- **2026-10-13 — PeriodField on a phone (P5.28 item 1).** The popover (190px of presets beside a month) ran off a phone's screen ("Work-injury register, phone"). On a phone the field opens a sheet on the screen's bottom edge, titled by the field's label, with the close button: the presets first, in two columns of the same buttons ("Clear" under a line across both), then "Custom range" with one month across the sheet's full width (Calendar `fullWidth`: the seven columns share the width, the days keep their 36px height). The desktop popover is unchanged.
- **2026-10-13 — ActionGroup's measuring copy is clipped (P5.28 item 1).** ActionGroup lays every action out once, invisibly and unwrapped, to measure what fits. The copy (absolutely positioned, as wide as all actions) made a phone page scroll sideways (816px in a 390px frame on every legal act page). It now stands in a box of no height that clips it; the measuring is unchanged.
- **2026-10-13 — Long texts that made a phone page scroll sideways (P5.28 item 1, found by the check).** FilterBar's pills: a pill's text is cut with an ellipsis, but the list of pills, a flex item, kept the width of its longest pill (1,175px in "FilterBar / Long text, phone width"); the list and the pill's text may now shrink. Breadcrumbs: every crumb is one line; the current page's crumb (the last, never a link) longer than the row is now cut with an ellipsis (705px in "Navigation / Long text, phone width"); the links before it stay whole, so their focus ring is never clipped.
- **2026-10-13 — The phone check (P5.28 items 1 and 5).** `apps/storybook/tests/phone-overflow.spec.ts` (protected: a new test file under `apps/storybook/tests/`). Every story whose name says it is drawn on a phone (`/phone|handheld|mobile/i`: "…, phone", "Phone width", "Long text, phone width", the handheld examples) is opened in a window 456 × 900 (a phone's 390px with the story's margin and a phone-width story's own padding; below 48em, so the components lay themselves out as on a phone), light theme, left to right and right to left. The screen is the story's PhoneFrame, or the window when it draws none (the "Long text, phone width" stories with a 390px column). Checked as drawn and then with every trigger opened one at a time — `aria-haspopup` (selects, menus, popovers, dialog triggers), comboboxes (a press, then ArrowDown), and buttons whose name ends in "…" (the convention of a button that opens a dialog) — and, in a dialog or sheet that opens, its own triggers (a select inside a dialog); a trigger repeated down a page (an article's or a row's menu) twice at most, 40 per screen: the page does not scroll sideways; every open overlay lies inside the screen and nothing inside it is wider than its box (a cut option; an ellipsis on purpose is allowed); every backdrop covers the whole screen. It runs with the story tests (`test:stories` in `apps/storybook/package.json`), so CI shards it with them; no workflow change. It adds about 330 phone stories × 2 directions (measured locally on a shared 4-core machine: about 30 minutes with 4 workers for all 660 tests, 8–30s each; about 41 tests per shard in CI's 16 shards).
- **2026-10-13 — LookupDialog on a phone: compact rows (P5.28 item 13).** On a phone the results are one compact row each — the title (default `getRowLabel`), `mobile.subtitle` ("code · kind") and `mobile.badge` at the end (the price) — and under it only the columns `mobile.details` names, **default none** (DataTable's default, every column, made each result a full detail card over the line form). The examples pass the price as the badge (Invoice draft, the specification; the bank statement's open items: number; partner · due date; open amount).

### Locale (P5.28 item 2)

- **2026-10-13 — Day and month names, dates and the week's first day come only from the provider's locale (P5.28 item 2).** The owner saw an English interface with "Januar, Ned Pon Uto", "sre 7", "utorak, 6. oktobar 2026." and weeks from Sunday. **Root cause:** the examples' `ExampleProvider` (and screens-G's `Tenant`, and `shift-planner.test`) passed the story's locale ("en") with a whole Serbian `format` (`createFormat('sr-Latn-RS')`): `format` replaced `monthName`, `weekdayName` and `dateLong` with Serbian ones, while the week's first day came from "en" (Sunday). No component hardcodes a locale: the calendar primitive, CalendarView, ResourceSchedule, Timetable, SlotPicker, ShiftPlanner, MyShifts, AttendanceGrid, DateField, DateRangeField, MonthField and PeriodField all take their names from `format` and their week from `weekStartsOn` (checked, every one; PeriodField's year names come from `format.businessYear`). **The rule:** month and weekday names, long dates and the week's first day come only from the provider's `locale` (the week from its region, or the provider's `weekStartsOn`, the tenant's setting); `format` may replace how _digits_ are written, never the words. **New helper `numericFormat(locale, timeZone?)`** (exported, unit-tested): the numbers, amounts, percentages and numeric dates and times of another locale without its words (no `monthName`, `weekdayName`, `dateLong`, `businessYear`). An English interface for a Serbian company is `locale="en-RS"` with `format={numericFormat('sr-Latn-RS')}`: "12.345,60 RSD", "06.10.2026.", "09:42", "Tuesday, October 6, 2026", weeks from Monday (the region RS). **The examples** now do exactly that: `ExampleProvider` uses `tenantLocale(story locale)` ("en" → "en-RS", "ar" → "ar-RS"; a locale with a region keeps it) and the tenant's digits; `EXAMPLE_FORMAT` (story-frames) builds the long dates the example checks expect; screens-G's `Tenant` passes `numericFormat('sr-Latn-RS', 'Europe/Belgrade')` and no longer forces `weekStartsOn={1}` (the locale's region gives Monday); `ScheduleFrame` (the scheduling stories) takes the week from `tenantLocale` instead of forcing Monday on an "en" locale. The tests with the same fault (`pos.test.tsx`, `job-progress.test.tsx`) use `locale="en-RS"` with `format={numericFormat('sr-Latn-RS')}`. Stories (static): "Internal/Primitives/Calendar": English (United States) from Sunday, English for a Serbian company (en-RS) from Monday, Serbian (sr-Latn) from Monday with Serbian names and control labels; "Components/Scheduling/CalendarView": Month, English (United States) from Sunday; Month, Serbian (sr-Latn) from Monday with Serbian texts from `messages`.

### Long selects (P5.28 item 3)

- **2026-10-13 — A long select is searched (P5.28 item 3).** `SelectField` with 11 options or more (`SEARCHABLE_FROM`, the owner's "more than about 10") is searched by typing, as Mantine's Select `searchable`: a text box showing the chosen label with the chevron at its end; a press or ArrowDown shows every option, typing filters them (ignoring case and accents, in the page's locale — `filterChoices`), the keys of ComboboxField choose (WAI-ARIA combobox: the focus stays in the box, `aria-activedescendant`), groups keep their headings (`role="group"`). Leaving the box puts the chosen label back; an emptied box clears the choice only when the field is `clearable`. `searchable` overrides the count either way. A list searched on the server stays ComboboxField. Chosen over making every application switch to ComboboxField: the value stays a string, the options and groups stay the same, and the pupil picker of AttendanceGrid's phone layout (30+ pupils) and every other long SelectField change with no code. ComboboxField, MultiSelectField and SelectField's searched list open their list on a press (before, only typing or ArrowDown opened it).
- **2026-10-13 — A long list keeps its active option in view (P5.28 item 3).** ComboboxField, MultiSelectField, SelectField's searched list (and LookupField's own list is unchanged) keep the focus in the text box, so the browser did not scroll the list as ArrowDown moved past its 220px: the active option went out of sight. The list now scrolls itself (only the list, never the page) to keep the active option in view. A searched SelectField opens with its chosen option active, as Mantine's.

### Sticky headers (P5.28 item 4)

- **2026-10-13 — Sticky table headers stick below the shell; the first column stays at the start (P5.28 item 4).** A wide grid scrolls sideways in its own region (`overflow-x: auto`), and such a region is a scroll container: a `position: sticky` header inside it sticks to the region, never to the page, so on a long page it scrolled away under the AppShell's header (School, gradebook: the dates row disappeared). SectionCard's `overflow-hidden` and any `overflow-x-auto` wrapper do the same. CSS cannot make one element sticky to the page and scroll sideways in a box at once, so **one small mechanism** (`components/sticky-head.ts`, internal): the header cells carry `STICKY_HEAD` (`sticky top-0` inside their region, then `translate-y` by `--liro-head-shift`), and `useStickyHead(regionRef)` keeps `--liro-head-shift` on the region equal to how far the region's top has gone above the page's sticky edge — the bottom of the shell's sticky top (`--liro-shell-top`, published by AppShell) or the top of the scrolling container — clamped so the header never leaves its region (`headShift`, unit-tested). It listens to every scroll (document, capture: the window, a phone frame, an application's container), resize and the region's size, once a frame; the scrolling container is the nearest ancestor that scrolls vertically, else the page; the shell's height counts only when the shell scrolls in that container. **The rule for every table, grid and schedule with a header row:** (1) the header cells `STICKY_HEAD` (on an opaque surface), the header group `data-sticky-head`; (2) the first column (row headers: people, names, resources) `sticky start-0` on an opaque surface; the corner cell both, marked `data-sticky-start`; layers inside the region: body 0, first column 5, header 10, corner 20; (3) the region `STICKY_CLEARANCE`: a cell the keyboard reaches is scrolled clear of the shell, the header and the first column (scroll margins from `--liro-shell-top`, `--liro-head-height`, `--liro-start-width`, kept by the hook; WCAG 2.4.11); (4) anything else sticky at the top of a page (a phone's totals card) uses `top-[var(--liro-shell-top,0px)]`, never `top-0`. **Applied:** AttendanceGrid (timesheet, attendance, gradebook: the days row and the corner; people already sticky), ShiftPlanner (the days row and the corner get the raised surface; people already sticky, now under the header), ResourceSchedule (the days and hours rows as one sticky header; names already sticky), DataTable (`stickyHeader` now follows the page, no `maxHeight` needed; **in a card** — `inCard`, where the surface is known to be raised — the selection column and the first column stay at the start, rows get the raised surface so the sticky cells inherit hover and selection; totals' first cell too), EditableGrid (the header row always, its lines redrawn as shadows because the grid's collapsed borders stay where the cells were; in a card the first column, with its end line redrawn; on phones the totals card now sticks at `--liro-shell-top`, it slid under the shell), CalendarView (the day and week views' days row and the month's weekday row). RoomRack has no header row (rooms are tiles under floor headings; nothing sticky), Timetable's few periods need none. Stories that act (a picture cannot scroll): "Thirty … under the shell, interaction" in AttendanceGrid, ShiftPlanner, ResourceSchedule, DataTable and EditableGrid (plus EditableGrid's phone one), checking that the header (and the corner) stands right below a 56px shell bar after the page scrolled 300–400px past the grid's top, and that the first column stays while the grid scrolls sideways; and "Examples / School, gradebook, header under the shell, interaction" in the real AppShell. The examples' class 7/2 now has 30 pupils (the owner's gradebook), Luka still the fourth.
- **2026-10-13 — The statutory grid on the shared sticky mechanism (P5.28 item 4).** The grid's box is always a sideways scroller (`overflow-x-auto`, `STICKY_CLEARANCE`), the `thead` carries `STICKY_HEAD` and `data-sticky-head`, `useStickyHead` moves it below the shell while the **page** scrolls, the corner cell is `sticky start-0` with `data-sticky-start`, the rows' number and label cells (`th scope="row"`) `sticky start-0 z-[5]` on surface.raised. The region is named and focusable only while it overflows (`role="region"`, the part's title, `tabIndex=0`, `data-overflowing`); the tables use `border-separate` (collapsed borders do not move with a sticky header); group headings stay at the start while scrolling sideways (`--liro-grid-width`); the parts draw their own card, without SectionCard's `overflow-hidden`. **Replaced:** the first version's bounded region (at most the viewport's height under the shell, scrolling both ways, its header sticky at the region's own top, used when the grid did not fit its card). Why: with a bounded region a long part had two vertical scrollbars (the page's and the grid's), the wheel stopped scrolling the page inside the grid, and the header stuck to the region instead of the shell — the shared mechanism keeps one page scroll and the header under the shell whether the grid fits or not, which is what the owner asked for ("like the gradebook"). **`STICKY_HEAD` on the `thead`, not on each cell:** the form has two header rows (a group over its sub-columns); moving the group keeps them together (cells at `top-0` would put the second row on the first if the region ever scrolled down). The grid's own controls (entered fields, pencils, source buttons) get the same scroll margins as the cells (a field reached by the keyboard under the header is scrolled clear of it, WCAG 2.4.11); on phones (one card per row, nothing sticky) a focused field is scrolled clear of the shell. Stories: "Narrow, scrolls sideways"; (interaction) "Thirty-two rows under the shell, interaction" (desktop, a narrow card: the header and corner stay right below a 56px shell after the page scrolled 400px past the grid's top, a field under the header is scrolled clear when focused, the number and label column stays while the grid scrolls sideways) and "Thirty-two rows under the shell, phone, interaction" (390 × 720 frame: no sideways scroll, 32 row cards, a field focused under the shell is scrolled clear). The 32-row part is an illustrative input-tax record in the story file.
- **2026-10-13 — Every DataTable's header stays below the shell by default (P5.28 item 4, accepted by the lead).** `stickyHeader` now defaults to **true** (was false): every DataTable on a page — ListPage's and RegisterPage's tables, ClockRecordList, WorkingTimeBalance, ImportWizard's columns table, the examples' document lines, members, roles, invitations, absences — keeps its header below the shell while the page scrolls, with no prop to remember; this fixes the class at once. At rest nothing moves (the shift is 0). `stickyHeader={false}` remains for a table whose header must not move (none in the library). ListPage and RegisterPage therefore pass nothing (a ListPage default through context was considered and dropped: the default covers every table, not only those in a list card). DataTable's corner cells now carry `data-sticky-start` (with a selection column, both), so the keyboard's scroll margin clears the sticky first column in a card; the hook measures the cover from the region's start edge to the farthest marked cell (`startCover`, tested), so a selection column before the first column counts. Alpha breaking only in that the header now sticks (no API change). DataTable's first column outside a card (ClockRecordList, WorkingTimeBalance, the bank journal, the specification sheet) stays unsticky: sticky only `inCard`, where the surface is known.
- **2026-10-13 — PortalShell publishes `--liro-shell-top` (P5.28 item 4).** As AppShell's: a ResizeObserver on the sticky header writes its height on the shell root, so a table's header, a phone's totals or anything sticky in a portal's page stands below the portal's header. Checked in "Patient portal" and "Patient portal, phone".
- **2026-10-13 — TreeTable's header below the shell (P5.28 item 4).** The header row was sticky only when windowed (`maxHeight`); now always `STICKY_HEAD` with `useStickyHead`, the header rowgroup `data-sticky-head`, the region `STICKY_CLEARANCE` plus a scroll margin on the focusable rows (`[role=row][tabindex]`). The tree column is **not** sticky at the start: TreeTable has no card mode, so its surface is not known (the rows are transparent, the hover and selection on the row), and no consumer is wider than its box. Story: "Seventy rows under the shell, interaction".
- **2026-10-13 — Where nothing sticks (P5.28 item 4, searched).** PermissionMatrix: its header and row headers are transparent (it sits on whatever card holds it), a sticky header needs an opaque surface, and a role's areas are a short list (a dozen). KanbanBoard's column headers: a sticky header per column would float past the end of a short column, and columns are areas, not a table's header row. Timetable (a handful of periods), the rotation preview in ShiftPlanner's "Apply rotation…" dialog, DocumentTotals and the charts' "Show as table" (no long body), print tables (paper repeats the `thead`). - **2026-10-14 — Sticky header cells on a layer of their own (P5.28 item 4, found by the visual tests).** With DataTable's header sticky by default, Examples / Customers gave two pictures of its header text, one in about 25 runs: Chromium decides from frame to frame whether a sticky cell gets a compositing layer, and text on a layer is antialiased differently. Without the cells' translate it happened one run in four; with `will-change-transform` on `STICKY_HEAD` the cells always have a layer and 72 runs in a row gave the same picture. Every picture with a sticky table header changed once for it.
- **2026-10-14 — A layout measured from text measures again when the fonts arrive (P5.28, the class of DataTable's widths).** FloorPlan's label fit (item 24) was measured once after drawing and on resize; a web font arriving after the first measurement changes the labels' sizes but not the plan's, so the restaurant's labels fitted differently from run to run. It now measures again on `document.fonts.ready` and `loadingdone`, as DataTable's widths and ActionGroup's overflow already did. The combobox's list keeps its active option in view by layout positions (`offsetTop`), not the screen's: a list still opening (scaled or sliding in) gave a different scroll on each run. **A list that sets its own scroll turns the browser's scroll anchoring off** (`overflow-anchor: none`): SelectField "Many options, phone, open" was drawn scrolled to its end in two runs of three, because Chromium's scroll anchoring moved the list during the relayout of a full-page screenshot (reproduced: 17 of 24 loads; none of 12 with anchoring off; no script set the scroll). The same holds for the combobox list, LookupField's list, the company switcher's list and TreeView's window.

- **2026-10-13 — Moves others rely on are confirmed, and messages are a choice (P5.28 item 9, the owner: "Today Health, clinic schedule commits a drag at once with 'Appointment moved. The patient gets a message.'").**
  1. **`ChangeConfirmDialog`** (components/change-confirm-dialog.tsx): a drag, a "Move to…" or a "Transfer…" of an appointment, a shift, a reservation, a seat, a room or a bed only PROPOSES the change; the application opens this dialog and applies it on Save. Title the action, `subject` the record (item 6); `changes`: one line per field, old → new (the old value text.secondary, the new medium, "Before:" / "After:" for assistive technology, the arrow mirrored in right to left, "—" for none, never 0); `affected`: who it concerns, in the application's words; `warning`: the application's own check as a warning Alert (the dialog decides nothing); `notify`: one checkbox per message the application can send ("Notify Jovana Nikolić by SMS", a description of what and where), each checked as the application sets it (`defaultChecked`, default unchecked), so nobody is messaged without it being shown and chosen; with any checked the button says "Save and notify" (`changeConfirmLabel`), and `onConfirm({ notify })` receives the checked ids. Cancel, then Save (primary, last); Cancel changes nothing. A returned promise keeps it working (Save busy, Cancel disabled, not dismissible). **Pending changes** (several changes before deciding: a seating plan, a week of shifts) stay on the page as pending and are saved through the same dialog, one line per change with the record in the line's label (the "Pending changes" story). Pure helpers `initialNotify`, `toggleNotify`, `changeConfirmLabel` (tested). Applied: the clinic schedule (a drag proposes; doctor and time old → new; the patient's SMS checked by the clinic; Save moves it, the toast says whether a message went), the store's swap approval (the shift from → to, the shift given back, each person's "Notify …", the application's warning). The doctor's calendar has no move (CalendarView only opens an event) and the patient's own booking is confirmed by her Book: nothing to change there. Reservations, seating, room and bed moves reuse `ChangeConfirmDialog` as is — the moved guests or patient as `subject`, table / seat / room / bed and time as `changes`, the guests or the ward as `notify`, a clash from the application as `warning`; a seating plan edited in several steps keeps them pending and saves them with one dialog.
  2. **A move in ResourceSchedule only proposes.** The schedule reports `onMove` and draws the booking where the application has it; a drag, the keys or "Move to…" never move it by themselves. Where the booking is something others rely on (an appointment, a reservation, a stay) the application confirms it with ChangeConfirmDialog before changing `bookings` or messaging anyone. The component's own stories now do the same (their harness asks "Move booking" / the booking with doctor or room and time old → new and an unchecked "Notify …"; Save moves it; the readout says "message sent" or "no message"); new story "Move asked".
  3. **Messages on publishing and other confirmations are a choice.** `ConfirmDialog` (and `DeleteConfirmDialog`) gained `notify?: readonly NotifyOption[]` and `notifyConfirmLabel`: the messages the application can send with the action stand as "Notify …" checkboxes under the text (the same `NotifyChoices` group as ChangeConfirmDialog's, "Messages to send"), each checked as the application sets it and reset each time the dialog opens; while one is checked the button says `notifyConfirmLabel`; `onConfirm` receives `{ notify }` with the checked ids (empty without `notify`). A callback without a parameter still fits, so existing callers are unchanged. ReasonConfirmDialog and IrreversibleConfirmDialog do not take it. ShiftPlanner: `publishNotify` (the application's messages) and `onPublish({ notify })` (backward compatible: a callback without a parameter still fits; without `publishNotify` publishing messages nobody and `notify` is empty); the button says "Publish and notify" / "Publish changes and notify" while a message is checked (`shifts.publishAndNotify`, `shifts.publishChangesAndNotify`); `defaultPublishOpen` pictures the confirmation. ShiftPlanner's own edits are already pending until Publish (the pending-changes form of the rule). The store offers "Notify 8 people in the app" (checked) and "Send an SMS to the 2 people whose shifts changed" (not checked); the emergency department "Notify 12 people in the app" (checked). Chosen: one ConfirmDialog prop rather than a second dialog, because publishing is a confirmation of an action, not a change old → new.

### One "now" marker (P5.28 item 10)

- **2026-10-13 — One "now" marker (P5.28 item 10).** CalendarView had none, the clinic schedule none, and Timetable outlined the running period and put a "Now" chip in it (it pushed the lesson down and looked like a button). Now one internal `NowMarker` (`components/now-marker.tsx`): a 2px line in border.selected with an 8px dot of the same colour at its start (the leading edge of a horizontal line, the top of a vertical one) — neutral, never blue (D17) and never a status colour. It is an image named "Now, 09:40" (`messages['schedule.now']`, the time through `format.time`). CalendarView (day and week; across today's column; its slot `aria-current="time"`), ResourceSchedule (desktop: down across the rows, under the names and the header; phone: across the track) and Timetable (across today's running period at its place in the period; the cell keeps `aria-current="time"`, no outline, no chip) draw it. The time comes from the application: a new `now` prop on CalendarView and ResourceSchedule ("HH:mm" of the provider's today, or an instant shown in the provider's time zone, or a local "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm"), Timetable's `now` reads the same forms; never `Date.now`, so pictures are stable (`nowMoment`, `nowOnAxis`, `nowWithin`, unit-tested). `timetable.now` is replaced by `schedule.now`. The clinic examples (schedule and doctor's calendar) are seen on the day of Jovana's appointment (`CLINIC.day`, 14.10.2026, as their today) at 09:40.

### Official forms (P5.28 item 19)

- **2026-10-13 — StatutoryFormPage is the form's real grid (P5.28 item 19, the owner: "as the real form grid, like PP PDV, POPDV and the input-VAT records on ePorezi").** Replaces P5.20's one-table-per-section model (`StatutoryField` with `value` / `previous` is removed; alpha breaking). The model lives in `templates/statutory-logic.ts` (pure, tested in `statutory-logic.test.ts`):
  1. **Parts** (`StatutorySection`: `key`, `title`, `description`, `columns`, `items`) are cards, each with **its own columns** (`StatutoryColumn`: `id`, `label`, optional `group`). Neighbouring columns with the same `group` share one header above their own (two header rows, `statutoryHeaderRows`); a column without a group spans both rows; a one-column part ("Износ / вредност") has one header row.
  2. **Nested numbered groups** (`StatutoryGroup`: `key`, `number`, `title`, `items`) to any depth (Part 1 → 1.1 → 1.1.1). Every part and group is **collapsible** (a disclosure button with `aria-expanded`; a part's in its h2); a collapsed group's rows are **not drawn** (`statutoryGridLines`). `defaultCollapsed` (keys) for the first view. "Go to" opens the part and the groups around its target first (`findStatutoryPlace` → `path`), then scrolls to and focuses the row or cell.
  3. **Rows** (`StatutoryRow`: `id`, `number`, `label`, `cells` by column id, `total`). **A column without a cell does not apply: its place is blank** — never 0, never a disabled field (the owner: "1.3 and 1.4 have Base only, 1.1.5 has VAT only"). In the grid the empty cell carries `data-cell-kind="absent"`; on phones it is left out.
  4. **Three kinds of cells** (`StatutoryCell.kind`): `entered` — the application's field (`field`, a MoneyField with its label hidden and named by `statutoryCellLabel`, e.g. "1.1.2 · Општа стопа 20% · Основица"), plain text when `readOnly`; `computed` — read-only text (a total); `source` — read-only, the value a link-coloured button (dotted underline) that opens its documents in an end Drawer (`sources`, `sourceName` such as "Електронске фактуре из СЕФ-а" heads the list). A computed or source cell with `editor` can be typed over (P5.20's override: pencil, Cancel / Save, "Changed manually" with who, when, the computed value and "Use computed value"); the row shows the badge with the cell's column and the way back (in a one-column part without the column's name).
  5. **Ids:** a cell is `statutoryCellId(row, column)` ("1.1.2/base20"); rules' `fields`, the `editing` state, `onSaveOverride` and `onUseComputed` use row or cell ids. A rule shows under its row when it names the row or any of its cells (`statutoryRowRules`, failures first); "Go to" names the row's number.
  6. **The previous period is a comparison, never a replacement of the columns:** with `previousLabel` a switch "Compare with August 2026" (`compare` / `defaultCompare` / `onCompareChange`) shows each cell's `previous` under its value, xs secondary, its period named for assistive technology ("August 2026:"), and the note "September 2026, with August 2026 under each amount" beside the switch. Two extra columns per rate were rejected: four rate columns would become eight.
  7. **Language of the form (D15):** `lang` ("sr-Cyrl") puts `lang` on the form's own texts — part and group titles, row labels, column headers, the phone's value labels — when it differs from the page's (`useLangAttribute`); the application's UI texts (checks, buttons) stay in the page's language.
  8. **Phones** (`layout="phone"` / `usePhone()`): each part a card on surface.sunken, its group headings as disclosure buttons, **one card per row** (number and label, its checks and overrides), each value labelled with its group and column ("Општа стопа 20% · Основица"), an entered cell's field full width under its label. No table on phones.
  9. Kept from P5.20: LifecycleBar, PageHeader with back / status / actions, the checks' summary Alert (compact with a title only), `notice`, the drill-down Drawer, overrides, `readOnly`. The header and first column follow the sticky rule (above, "The statutory grid on the shared sticky mechanism"). Messages: `statutory.compareWith`, `statutory.comparing`, `statutory.previousValue` (`statutory.fieldValue` and `value.change` now receive "1.1.1 · Општа стопа 20% · ПДВ").
- **2026-10-13 — The illustrative VAT return (P5.28 item 19).** `templates/statutory-story-data.ts` (story data, not exported) builds one illustrative PP PDV / POPDV-like form for the template's stories and the VAT return example (group E): Part 1 "Промет добара и услуга и обрачунати ПДВ" (rates over Base and VAT; 1.1 with 1.1.1 from SEF, 1.1.2–1.1.4 entered, 1.1.5 VAT only, 1.1.6 total; 1.2 advances; 1.3 Base only, entered; 1.4 one base from SEF, reverse charge), Part 2 one column (2.1 computed 0,00, 2.2 from SEF, 2.3 total), Part 3 input tax (3.1.1 from SEF with Ivana's override of its VAT, 3.1.2 entered, 3.1.3 VAT only, 3.1.4 total; 3.2 and 3.3 VAT only), Part 4 one column (4.1, 4.2, 4.3 payable). Labelled "illustrative … not the authority's" in the subtitle and the docs; numbers like 1.1.5 are structure only. The application's arithmetic is played in paras (BigInt), so typing an entered cell updates its totals. One check fails while 3.1.1's VAT is overridden: "3.1.4 must equal 3.1.1 + 3.1.2 − 3.1.3 · Difference: 64.400,00 RSD". In the examples' data, `data-E.ts`'s `VAT_RETURN` is replaced by `vatFormValues` (with `SEPTEMBER_10`, `SEPTEMBER_ADVANCES`, `SEPTEMBER_REVERSE_CHARGE`, `VAT_INPUT_OVERRIDE`); `register-story-data.ts`'s `VAT_VALUES` is removed (its `SALES_20` / `PURCHASES_20` feed the template's stories).

PrintGradeReport and PrintFinding: the person's details as key/value rows in two columns (the finding's `subjectTitle` over them, no frame), the summary as rows. **PrintLegalAct:** the `note` is plain grey text (was a bordered box); its article headings stay centred (the convention of printed acts, as P5.27 decided).
- _[Moved to liro-folio, P5.95]_ **2026-10-13 — Electronic signature fields with their place in the PDF (P5.28 item 20).** Signature lines only where a signature is really required (a certificate, a report card, a finding), never on a business document. Each is a **`PrintSignatureField`** (`id` — stable, the same on every print —, `label`, `name`, `detail`, `image` once signed): the label xs grey, a **64 × 18mm** place on a thin border.strong line (`data-signature-field="<id>"`), the name and the detail under it; never split between pages. `PrintSignature.key` became `id` (alpha breaking). **The place on paper:** PrintPage measures every `[data-signature-field]` of its sheet after layout and on every resize (ResizeObserver), in millimetres as shares of the sheet's own width (the screen's `zoom` cancels out), and converts it with **`signatureFieldPlacement(id, box, area)`** (tested): the page body runs from the top margin and the repeated header (`area.top`, measured) to the bottom margin and the footer's room (`area.bottom`); the screen's long sheet is cut into pages of that height; a field that would cross a page's end starts the next page (`break-inside: avoid`); the result is the page (from 1) and the rectangle in **PDF points, origin at the page's bottom-left** (A4 595.28 × 841.89pt; `PT_PER_MM` = 72 / 25.4, two decimals). It is written on the element (`data-pdf-page`, `data-pdf-rect="x y width height"`) and reported through **`onSignatureFields(fields)`** on PrintPage and every template (only when it changes). Exact for a field on the first page (the certificate, a one-page finding) and wherever the content before it breaks between lines; a row or heading kept whole on paper moves what follows a few millimetres down, so a tool placing a signature on a later page should treat the rectangle as the field's place and look there. **Signing on screen:** with `onSign` an empty field is a "Sign here" button (`messages['print.signHere']`, link colour, a dashed border.default box, described by the field's label, left off the paper) that reports the field's id; the application signs and passes the visible signature back as `image`. Margins in `mm`, `cm`, `in`, `pt` or `px` are read by `lengthToMm`. Messages: `print.amountDue`, `print.signHere`.
- **2026-10-13 — Illustrative codes in stories (P5.28 items 20 and 21).** The application makes the real IPS QR image from the payment's data, and the fiscal receipt's code from the processor's answer; stories need only a stable picture in the slot. `illustrativeCode(text, label)` (`templates/print-story-data.ts`, not exported) draws a 29 × 29 QR-like SVG for the printouts (finder patterns and timing lines of a real code, the rest from a hash of the text) named "… (illustrative)"; `StoryCode` (`components/story-code.tsx`, not exported) is the POS stories' and examples' stand-in drawn from the text. Neither **scans**. No dependency was added.
- _[Moved to liro-folio, P5.95]_ **2026-10-13 — A fiscal receipt keeps its own layout (P5.28 item 20's class, the lead).** The printouts' simplicity (D27) covers the A4 templates: the business document, the certificate, the report card, the finding and the act. `ReceiptPreview` is the picture of a fiscal device's receipt, whose parts and order follow the fiscal journal (the banner and end lines between double rules, the kind between rules, the boxed marker of a receipt that is not a real sale); it stays black and grey with its dashed rules, as a thermal printer prints it. Changing it would make the preview differ from the paper the device prints.

### POS and Serbian fiscalisation (P5.28 items 21, 22)

- **2026-10-13 — Fiscal sale flows as data (P5.28 item 21).** The Serbian fiscal system (the electronic fiscal device and the processor of fiscal receipts) is the reference, but nothing of it lives in a component (D1, D2, D5): the kinds of a receipt, the ways to pay, the buyer's ID kinds, the counters, the markers, the rules ("a wire transfer needs the buyer's tax number", "a refund paid out in cash is signed by the buyer") and every printed word are the application's data. The stories and the examples carry an **illustrative** English rendering (`packages/ui/src/components/sale-story-data.ts`, `apps/storybook/src/examples/data-I-fiscal.ts`): invented processor numbers (`ZK7Q2M4P-ZK7Q2M4P-2318`), invented tax and personal numbers, the counter's suffixes written after the system's two letters. The receipt's legally prescribed lines are printed in the application's language ("FISCAL RECEIPT", "THIS IS NOT A FISCAL RECEIPT", "END OF FISCAL RECEIPT" in the English examples). The components compute nothing (D4): the remaining amount, the change, a refund's amount, the advances deducted, promotions, discounts, shares and the day's totals arrive as decimal strings. Today's look is kept.
- **2026-10-13 — The kind of a receipt: type × transaction (P5.28 item 21a).** `ReceiptKindPicker`: two groups of 44px pressed buttons (the neutral selection, never blue), the application's types (Normal, Advance, Proforma, Copy, Training) and transactions (Sale, Refund); a kind that cannot be chosen here stays focusable with its reason ("Copy: open the receipt in the journal to copy it."); the chosen kind's description and **marker** (`ReceiptKindOption.marker`) in a warning Alert. A kind that is not a real sale is marked three times, all with the application's words: the picker, the cart (`CartPanel` `kindLabel` under the title, `marker` as a warning Alert above the lines) and the receipt (`ReceiptPreview` `marker`, printed boxed and bold under the facts and again above the footer; the repeat is `aria-hidden`). **Training** adds a persistent warning `Banner` in `PosShell`'s new `banners` slot (role status, "Leave training" neutral). Choosing Refund in the picker starts from the original receipt (the application's rule in the example).
- **2026-10-13 — Several ways to pay on one receipt (P5.28 item 21b).** `PaymentDialog` takes the application's own ways to pay: `methods` may hold `PaymentOption`s `{ id, label, kind, icon?, unavailableReason?, note?, referenceLabel? }` beside the P5.10 names; `kind` is `cash` (quick amounts, keypad, change), `card` (a terminal's states), `qr` (an instant payment: the application's code shown large — `qrCode` — with the same four states as a card, its own words) or `plain` (an amount and, when asked, a reference: a cheque number, a voucher's code). Up to four ways stay a segmented row; more wrap as a grid of 44px pressed buttons (minmax 8.5rem; the neutral selection). **With `onAddPart` several ways pay one sale:** every panel takes "Amount of this payment" (the keypad) and "Add this payment"; a card or a code adds its part when the application says it is approved; the parts paid (`paid`, each with an optional `detail` and, with `onRemovePart`, a 44px remove button) and the remaining amount stand on top; "Exact amount" is the remaining amount once parts are paid (no arithmetic: the application's figure). A way that cannot be used yet (`unavailableReason`, e.g. a deferred payment without the buyer) can still be chosen: its panel shows the reason in a warning Alert, and the application's `extra` content (the BuyerField) under it. `doneContent` takes the issued receipt (ReceiptResult). The old `split` view and the P5.10 API stay as they were; `onAddPart` now reports `(method: string, amount)` and `method` / `onMethodChange` take strings (an option's id). The example offers the seven ways of the system: cash, card, instant payment, cheque, voucher (single-purpose; a multi-purpose one is "Other cashless" — the application's note), wire transfer (deferred, buyer required), other cashless.
- **2026-10-13 — The buyer (P5.28 item 21c).** `BuyerField`: a `fieldset` named by its legend (" \*" when the application's rule requires it, the rule as the description), the ID's kind and the ID side by side in a FormGrid (36rem), the ID left to right in every language; an optional second field with its kind when the application gives `optionalTypes`; a kind's `hint` ("9 digits") under the ID; the application's checks as `errors`. **More than ten kinds become a searchable ComboboxField** (`BUYER_TYPES_SEARCHABLE_FROM` 11, item 3's rule); the example's fifteen kinds are searchable. The corporate card is the buyer (the company's tax number) with the card's last digits in the optional field, paid by card.
- **2026-10-13 — Refunds: find, choose, carry over (P5.28 item 21d).** `ReceiptFinder`: the ScanField first ("Scan the receipt's code"; the camera through `onCameraScan`), then "Or search by number, date or total" (a FormGrid of three fields, Search neutral); the application searches and answers with `FoundReceipt`s as rows (CandidateList's look: number left to right, date and time, the kind, a detail, the total; chosen = the neutral selection; a receipt refunded in full stays focusable with its reason); skeletons while searching, the no-results EmptyState, the error in a danger Alert. `LineQuantityPicker` (one pattern for a partial refund, a split bill, paying part and moving items): "All lines" tri-state, a checkbox per line (ticked = the whole quantity available), a QuantityStepper 0 … available, "of 3 pc", the application's note ("1 of 4 refunded already"), a line that cannot be chosen with its reason, and the application's figure for what is chosen (`chosenTotal`, settling). The refund in the cart is "Normal · Refund", read-only lines, "To pay out", "Pay out 240,00 RSD"; its receipt carries the original's number and time (facts), the buyer, and a **signature line only where the application's rule asks** (`ReceiptPreview` `signature`; the example: paid out in cash). Logic `sale-logic.ts` (tested): `isChosen`, `chosenLineIds`, `toggleLine`, `chooseAllLines`, `allLinesChosen`, `exceedsAvailable` — quantities compared exactly as decimal strings.
- **2026-10-13 — Advances (P5.28 item 21e).** `AdvanceList`: a buyer's open advances (number left to right, the day paid, the state as a badge in the application's tone, the note, "Open" and "of … paid"), choosable with `onSelectionChange` (checkbox "Deduct advance …", the neutral selection), a refund button per advance (`onRefund`, "Refund advance …"), the application's "Deducted" figure; loading, empty, error. In the example the buyer's advances stand in the cart's `details`; one deducted, the rest "To pay" (`CartPanel` `totalLabel`). Taking an advance is a sale of the Advance kind (buyer, amount, what it is for); refunding one asks first (ConfirmDialog: the action as the title, the advance bold on its own line, item 6).
- **2026-10-13 — Cancel, copy, without compensation, corporate card (P5.28 item 21f).** Not components but the application's flows on the components: cancelling a receipt issued by mistake is a ReasonConfirmDialog (the application's reasons) that issues a refund of the whole receipt with its number and time; a copy is the receipt printed as the Copy kind with the marker; a sale without compensation is an option of the kind dialog (the application's rule: paid only as Other cashless, printed "WITHOUT COMPENSATION"); a corporate card is the buyer plus the card.
- **2026-10-13 — The result, the journal, the daily report (P5.28 item 21g).** `ReceiptResult`: the outcome (a success check "Receipt issued", or with `tone="waiting"` a neutral CloudUpload "Receipt issued, waiting to be sent" — never blue), the application's facts (processor number and time, the counter) as rows left to right, the code on a raised tile beside them from 30rem (container query; under them on phones), the link (left to right, new tab), and **delivery**: a row per way (print, e-mail, SMS / link), its own address field (e-mail / telephone, left to right), a neutral action named by the way ("Send by e-mail"), and its state in words with an icon (a spinner "Sending…", sent, failed in danger with the application's words); `onDeliver(id, address)`. `ReceiptPreview` prints the fiscal parts as data: `banner` and `end` between double rules (no more "=====" text in data), `kindLine` between dashed rules, `marker`, a `recap` table (columns and rows from the application; amount columns written by `format`), `issuedFacts` after it, `signature`. The journal is a DataTable inside PosShell (the list in the product area, the chosen receipt as printed in the cart area; on phones the receipt first and "Receipts" opens the list): time, number, kind, total, state; Copy, Refund…, Cancel receipt… The daily report is a ReceiptPreview (sales, refunds, net, by way of paying, the tax per label; the kinds that are not in the totals named in the footer).
- **2026-10-13 — Offline and its queue (P5.28 item 21h).** `PosShell` `queueState` ('sending' default, a neutral badge; 'failed', a danger "Not sent" badge — `pos.queueFailed`) and `queueAction` (the example: "Show receipts" opens the journal of the receipts not sent). A receipt issued offline has the till's local number and "Waiting to be sent" in the journal; refused ones say why, with "Send again" in a danger Banner (its action neutral, item 7).
- **2026-10-13 — An online sale (P5.28 item 21i).** A back-office page of the web-shop order WEB-1042: the order, and "Fiscal receipt" — ReceiptResult "Issued and e-mailed" with the processor's facts, the code, the link and the e-mail sent; "Show receipt" opens it as printed.
- **2026-10-13 — Open tabs on tables (P5.28 item 22).** A table's tab is the application's record and outlives the screen: the examples keep it above the screens (`useExampleState`, `apps/storybook/src/examples/example-state.tsx`, provided by ExampleApp) — the waiter adds items, goes back to the terrace (the plan shows the tab's time and what it still has to pay) and comes back to the same tab. On the tab (`screens-K-tabs.tsx`, one screen for Kafić Kod Mike and Bistro Dunav): each line's state in words (`CartPanel` line `state`: "Sent to the bar · 18:15", "Not sent yet" in the warning tone, "Paid"), its note (`note`), an edit button (`onEditLine`: the application's dialog — quantity, a note for the kitchen or the bar, a discount from the venue's list, Remove line); "Send order (n)" (primary, secondary weight) sends the unsent lines to their stations ("Sent: 2 to the bar, 1 to the kitchen."); the promotions from the venue's data (Espresso 3 for 2; a juice hour; the bistro's dessert of the day) and the waiter's discounts as the line's discount text and total rows; a discount on the whole order; **Split the bill** (equally: People, the application's shares, "Pay one share") or **Pay part** (by items: LineQuantityPicker, the application's amount); **Move…** the whole tab or some items to another table (free, or an open tab that is joined; more than ten tables a searchable combobox); **Bill** closes it with the fiscal receipt (ReceiptResult) and "Close table". The bistro's table panel gains "Tab" (and the tab's rest to pay); every figure is computed in `data-K-tabs.ts`.
- **2026-10-13 — What the application keeps outlives the screen (class of P5.28 item 22).** In the examples, records the user changes on a screen and expects to find again are kept above the screens with `useExampleState(key, initial)`: the tabs, the till's sale and journal, the open advances, the pick list and the stock count (the count is reached from the pick list and returns to it). Pictures still start from their route's state.
- **2026-10-13 — A scrolling area without controls takes the focus (P5.28, found by the tests).** A read-only CartPanel (a refund's lines, a cart without `onQuantityChange`, `onRemove`, `onEditLine`) makes its scrolling list one tab stop (`tabIndex` 0, a group named by the cart's title, the focus ring) so the keyboard can scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1; axe `scrollable-region-focusable`); the till's journal does the same for the printed receipt it shows. A dialog whose steps change (the refund: find, then lines) keeps its step while it closes, so its content does not change under the closing animation.

### Floor plans and places (P5.28 items 23–27, 17, 18; 6, 8, 9 for places)

- **2026-10-13 — No walls, doors or windows (P5.28 item 23, the owner: "they confuse; simplicity
  first").** `FloorItemKind` loses `wall`, `door` and `window` (a breaking alpha change: an
  application that passed them gets a type error). A plan is its areas — plain labelled regions,
  dashed outline on surface.sunken, the name at the top start — and the things people choose or
  choose around: tables, seats, rooms, places, the bar, a counter, a stage. Decided by me: `bar`,
  `counter` and `stage` stay as labelled furniture (a stage, a dance floor, a piano, a lift, a
  rack's sign); `FIXTURE_KINDS` is now `['stage', 'counter']` (drawn, chosen only in edit mode;
  the stage's border is solid now, dashed was the door's look). A real building plan, when the
  application has one, is the `background` image (P5.25a). Removed from every story and example:
  the restaurant's windows, wall and doors (Restoran Kej, Bistro Dunav), the café's railing and
  door, the wedding's and the gala's doors, the warehouse's dock doors (Receiving and Dispatch are
  the areas along the docks); the palettes' "Wall" is a "Service counter"; the hotel floor's
  corridor is an area, not a stage.
- **2026-10-13 — A label on the plan is never cut (P5.28 item 24, the owner: "'2 guests ·
  19:...'").** An item writes its number (`shortLabel`) with the state's icon, then a short
  second line, `planDetail` (new on `FloorItem`: the guests, "2 guests"); `detail` (the time and
  the guests, "2 guests · since 18:40") is no longer written on the plan — it is in the list, the
  item's name and the application's panel or drawer. Nothing is cut with "…": after every
  drawing and every change of the plan's width (ResizeObserver) the plan measures each label
  (`labelFit`, `labelRoom`: the item's box less 2px padding, a round item's inner 78%, less the
  level bar) and writes `data-fit` — 'all' (both lines), 'name' (the second line left out),
  'number' (the icons left out too), 'none' (nothing written; the list and the name say it).
  SeatingChart's tables write "8 of 10" as their second line. The examples give the guests as
  `planDetail` (Bistro Dunav, Restoran Kej) or what the tab still has to pay (Kafić Kod Mike).
- **2026-10-13 — One area at a time (P5.28 item 26).** FloorPlan with two or more areas that hold
  items shows an area switcher in its toolbar: "All areas" and each area — a segmented control
  up to four areas (`AREA_SEGMENTS_UP_TO`; two on a phone), a select beyond (SelectField, searched
  by typing from 11, item 3's rule) — decided by me: one control that stays one line, rather than
  chips that wrap into rows at 6+ areas. One area is drawn alone: the plan is cropped to the
  area's box (`planFrame`) and fitted to the width (on a wide screen no taller than
  min(70vh, 44rem)); its items are those of the area or, with no area of their own, whose centre
  lies in it (`inArea`); the list shows that area's group only. `area` / `defaultArea` /
  `onAreaChange` (null = all), `areaChoices` (the application's ids and order; default every
  area that holds an item, so a corridor or a nurses' station is drawn but not offered; `[]`
  hides the switcher). "Go to" a warning on an item of another area returns to all areas. In
  edit mode a palette item is added at the centre of what is drawn and in the area shown.
- **2026-10-13 — Takeaway and delivery are order channels, not areas (P5.28 item 26).** No
  example drew them as plan areas; the rule is recorded and shown: Bistro Dunav's floor is one of
  three page-level tabs — Dine-in (the plan), Takeaway (2), Delivery (1) — the takeaway and
  delivery orders as cards with their state and the next step ("Mark as ready", "Handed over",
  "Out for delivery", "Delivered"), kept above the screens (`useExampleState('bistro.orders')`).
- **2026-10-13 — Phones open on the list; no editing on a phone (P5.28 item 27).** On a phone
  FloorPlan opens on the list (as before), now a card per item (rounded, bordered, 8px apart) by
  area, with the state badge, `detail` (the guests and the time), note, capacity. The plan, when
  opened, fits the screen's width with no sideways scrolling: the 24px minimum width is not
  applied on a phone — the list on the same page is the equivalent control of the small targets
  (WCAG 2.5.8's exception) — and one area at a time draws it larger. With `editing` on a phone
  the plan is not editable: no palette, no "Move to…", no dragging; a neutral note says

- **2026-10-13 — Moving guests lists the free tables (P5.28 item 25, the owner: "'Move guests
  from Table 8' does not work: the 'To table' select is empty").** Cause: table 8's party of six
  had no free table with six seats, and the select showed nothing. Now "Move to table…" opens one
  ChangeConfirmDialog: title "Move guests", the table and party bold under it ("Table 8 ·
