## Admin, Superadmin and Helpdesk (P5.29, P5.30)

### Administration and the platform's status (P5.29 a, b)

- **2026-10-14 — HealthList: one component for monitored things (P5.29 a, b).** The library had nothing for "is it working, and since when?": StatusTimeline is one process's states in order, SetupChecklist steps done once, SessionList devices, KeyValueList values without a state, and JobProgress one job. HealthList (`components/health-list.tsx`, logic in `health-logic.ts`) shows connections, services, queues, databases, backups, regions — anything monitored — as rows: the name with its detail and the application's note; the state as a StatusBadge with the application's words and tone and an icon from its `kind` (`up` CircleCheck, `degraded` CircleAlert, `down` CircleX, `maintenance` Wrench, `unknown` CircleHelp; the application may give another icon) — never colour alone; the figures as label over value (`metrics`, the application's text); the last success ("Never" when null) and the last error with its time and message (`healthFacts`); and the application's actions (Retry, "Open log") as neutral secondary small buttons named with the thing ("Retry: SEF (e-invoicing)"), busy while a returned promise runs. It judges nothing: a figure never becomes a state, nothing is counted. Desktop: one card whose rows share one grid (CSS subgrid), so the columns line up across rows; an optional title row with `headerActions`. Phones: one card per thing (owner), the title above the cards (never cards in a card); figures and times as label / value rows, the error's message in full, the actions at the bottom. Loading: skeleton rows; nothing: the application's words (`emptyText`, default `messages['health.empty']`); a failed load: a danger Alert. Decided by the admin helper: the state's kind drives only the icon, the tone stays the application's (its status-to-tone map), as for every StatusBadge. The rule is D30 in AGENTS.md: anything monitored continuously is a HealthList row, and the list never turns a figure into a state.
- **2026-10-14 — The administration of a tenant (P5.29 a).** Built from the library only:
  - **Overview** is a DashboardPage: users, active sessions, failed sign-ins today, accounts without two-factor sign-in as StatCards; failed and blocked sign-ins of the last seven days as a stacked BarChart in the tones of the two states (warning, danger); the licences as a SectionCard with "24 of 30 seats used", a ProgressBar and a KeyValueList; the integrations with errors as a HealthList; the accounts without two-factor sign-in as a DataTable.
  - **Sign-in activity** is a ListPage: saved views (All, Failed and blocked, Today), a FilterBar (user, result, period — all inline), Export; a DataTable with when, user (name and e-mail), result (Success / Failed / Blocked in the application's words and tone), reason, device and browser, the approximate place, and the IP address as a MaskedValue: masked by default, shown after a reason from the application's list (or "Other"), the access logged; Hide.
  - **Audit log** is a ListPage: views (All, Access and settings, Documents and customers), FilterBar (changed by, record, period, search), Export; a DataTable of when, who, record (with its kind), field and the change — the old value struck through (`del`), an arrow (mirrored in right-to-left), the new value (`ins`, no underline), "From" / "to" for assistive technology, "empty" for nothing. **Never edited or deleted:** no selection, no row actions; a row opens the whole entry read only in an end Drawer (before, after, address, request id); the table's note says the log cannot be changed (`rowLimitMessage`).
  - **Security** is a page of SectionCards: two-factor sign-in per user (a DataTable; "Reset two-factor sign-in" confirmed, "Send a reminder"); signed-in devices of the user chosen in a SelectField with SessionList's Sign out and "Sign out everywhere" (confirmed; SessionList's own "Sign out all other devices" is for the person's own account, so it is not used for another user); API keys and tokens (name with the key's visible start, access, created by, last used, expires, state; Revoke from the row's menu with a destructive ConfirmDialog titled by the action with the key as its subject, D22; a revoked key stays listed as Revoked); the password and session policy as a KeyValueList from the Core's data with "Change policy".
  - **Integrations** is a HealthList of every connection (SEF, two banks, e-mail, Liro Bridge, the tax administration, the exchange rates) with Retry where the application offers it.
- **2026-10-14 — The platform's system status and network (P5.29 b, two views).** **System status** is a DashboardPage across every tenant: services up, 30-day uptime, response time (p95) and error rate as StatCards; response time (p95 and median) and the error rate for the last 24 hours as LineCharts; services, queues, databases and storage, and backups (the last good backup, the copy to the second region, the weekly restore test) as HealthLists; certificates (expiry and renewal) and scheduled maintenance as DataTables. **Network and infrastructure**: regions as a HealthList (latency, nodes, open alerts), the latency between regions as a LineChart, open alerts as a DataTable (Acknowledge in the row menu), nodes as a DataTable with a FilterBar (region, role, health; address, CPU, memory, latency, alerts).
- **2026-10-14 — Example data for administration (P5.29).** Invented throughout; IP addresses only from the documentation ranges (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24, 2001:db8::/32), e-mail addresses and host names at example.com, certificate issuers "Illustrative CA". Today 14.10.2026, now 09:40 (the screens' `Tenant today`), the same day and clock as the Superadmin's (`R_TODAY`, `R_NOW`, Belgrade) and the helpdesk's.
- **2026-10-14 — The administration's shell (P5.29 a).** `AdminShell` with `adminTabs()` in `screens-Q.tsx`: Overview, Users and roles (group C's `/settings/users`), Sign-in activity, Audit log, Security, Integrations — Milica Petrović's administration of Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o.

### The Superadmin (P5.29 b)

- **2026-10-14 — The Superadmin is built from the templates; nothing new was needed (P5.29 b).** Incidents: ListPage (views All / Open / Monitoring / Resolved, FilterBar with severity and service, DataTable) and an incident page on DocumentPage. Security events: WorklistPage. Tenants: ListPage with a row menu ("View as admin…", "Send an announcement…"). The tenant's view: AppShell's `impersonationBar` slot with ImpersonationBar over a read-only DetailPage. Announcements: ListPage and an editor on RecordFormPage. Every figure, state, duration, count and text is the application's (examples' `data-R.ts`); the screens filter, count and change it. The only library change is one optional prop (ImpersonationBar `note`, below).
- **2026-10-14 — An incident on DocumentPage (P5.29 b).** The h1 is the number and the title ("INC-2026-042 · SEF submissions delayed"); the lifecycle bar is the incident's stages (Detected, Investigating, Identified, Monitoring, Resolved); the key figures are severity, start, duration ("Going on for" while open, "Lasted" after) and the tenants affected. No lines (`lines={null}`): the sections in order are the status-page message (an Alert in the tone tenants see, with who posted it and when), the timeline (StatusTimeline: every update a step with its text and author, "· on the status page" when public; an incident not yet acknowledged shows "Not acknowledged — Paged … at 08:52 and again at 09:07" as the warning next step), the affected tenants (a KeyValueList, tenant → the application's impact) and the postmortem (RichText; before resolution "Written after the incident is resolved.", after it "Due by …" until written). Side panels: People (assignee, incident commander, on call, second on call), Affected services, Related incidents. Actions, the main last: Resolve… (positive, secondary), Post update…, and Acknowledge (primary) while nobody has; once acknowledged, Post update… is the primary. Post update is a Dialog with the incident as `subject`: the stage (radios), the message, and "Also post it to the status page" as an explicit checkbox. Resolve is a ConfirmDialog with the subject and two `notify` choices (post "Resolved" to the status page, checked; e-mail the affected tenants' administrators, not checked) — "Resolve and notify" (D24). **Phones see and acknowledge:** no header actions on a phone; Acknowledge stands in the bottom bar while the incident is not acknowledged.
- **2026-10-14 — Security events are a WorklistPage (P5.29 b).** Each event is decided one at a time — start investigating, then close it with the action taken — with its facts beside the queue, Previous / Next and "3 of 7"; a ListPage would open each event on a page of its own and lose the queue. The queue opens on what is not closed (State: New, Investigating), the most severe first, then the newest (the application's order). The row: kind, tenant · time, severity as the figure, state as the status. The summary above: New, Investigating, "High, not closed" (danger) and Closed. The 380px list holds the FilterBar with every filter in its drawer (`inline={0}`), the chosen ones as pills. Closing asks the action taken from the Core's list (ReasonConfirmDialog, details optional) and records it in the event and its history; checked rows close together with the same question and the count.
- **2026-10-14 — "View as" a tenant: the reason first, then an audited, read-only bar (P5.29 b).** A tenant's row (click, Enter, or the row menu) asks why first (ReasonConfirmDialog: "Support ticket", "Incident", "The tenant's own request", with the ticket or incident number as details; its message says the view is read-only and recorded). The tenant's administration then opens in the tenant's own shell (its brand, its company) under ImpersonationBar: "Viewing as Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o. administrator · Read-only · Reason: … · Every page you open is recorded in the audit log", "Exit view" at the end (also in the user menu). The page itself is read-only values and tables, no actions. ImpersonationBar gained an optional `note` (the application's text after the reason) rather than a second bar or a longer `mode`: the mode stays one word ("Read-only"), and the audit fact reads as its own part of the strip.
- **2026-10-14 — Announcements: the editor shows the Banner as tenants will see it (P5.29 b).** RecordFormPage with four FormSections: Message (kind: "Banner in the application" or "Status-page message", tone, title, message), Preview (the Banner for a banner, the Alert for a status-page message, live as the user types; a sentence while both texts are empty), Audience (all tenants, or chosen tenants through a MultiSelectField, searchable by name with the tax number as the option's description), Schedule (start and end dates with DateField, times from a half-hour SelectField — 48 options, so searched by typing, D20; the library has no time field and needs none for this). The checks are the application's: a title for a draft; the message, at least one chosen tenant, a start, and an end after the start to schedule. Actions by state: a draft or a new one — Cancel, Save draft, Schedule (primary); scheduled — Cancel, Move to drafts, Save changes; live — Cancel, End now… (caution, a ConfirmDialog with the subject), Save changes; ended — read-only fields and "Duplicate as new". The list: views All / Draft / Scheduled / Live / Ended, Kind and Tone filters, a draft's dates "—", a live one without an end "When ended". A tenant's row menu "Send an announcement…" opens a new one with that tenant chosen.
- **2026-10-14 — The Superadmin's statuses in the examples' one tone map (P5.29 b).** Incidents: Open danger, Monitoring warning, Resolved success. Security events: New warning (waits on someone), Investigating info (on its way), Closed neutral. Severity: SEV-1 / High danger, SEV-2 / Medium warning, SEV-3 / Low neutral. Tenants' health: Healthy success, Degraded warning, Failing danger, Suspended danger (existing). Announcements: Scheduled neutral, Live success, Ended neutral, Draft neutral (existing). The superadmin helper had Scheduled info; the merge kept one key "Scheduled" for scheduled announcements and scheduled maintenance (the admin helper's), neutral. The admin helper's block in the same map: Success success, Blocked danger, Up success, Down danger, In maintenance neutral, No report neutral, Revoked neutral, Expires soon warning, Valid success, On success, Off warning, Waiting for setup warning, Critical danger, Warning warning.

### The helpdesk for agents (P5.30 a–c)

- **2026-10-14 — The helpdesk is built from the library (P5.30 a–c).** The agent's inbox is ListPage + FilterBar + DataTable (views My open, Unassigned, Overdue, All with counts; "Assign…" and "Change status…" on the BulkActionBar, each asking in one Dialog whose title is a question with the count, D22); the ticket page is DetailPage (one "Conversation" section: MessageList and ReplyComposer) with SidePanels in the 300px side column (Properties changed in place with SelectFields, Service level, Contact, Other tickets as RelatedDocuments, Activity as ActivityList); the dashboard is DashboardPage with six StatCards, two BarCharts, a LineChart, a DonutChart and the overdue tickets in a card. Phones: the conversation full width, the panels in an end Drawer opened by "Details" (with the ticket as `subject`), the composer under the conversation. Three new pieces only, each generic: SlaTimer, ReplyComposer and the `internal` message.
- **2026-10-14 — SlaTimer: a deadline in words against the application's `now` (P5.30 a).** A due instant, the application's `now` (never the device's clock, as the NowMarker, D25), optional `paused`, `completedAt` and `warnWithin`: "Due in 2 h 15 min" (text.secondary, a clock), the same in the warning tone within `warnWithin` minutes, "Overdue by 40 min" in the danger tone with an alert icon and medium weight, "Paused" (a pause icon), "Met" (success) or "Missed by 25 min" (danger). The words always carry the state, never the colour alone. Minutes are whole: the time left is rounded up (30 seconds is "1 min"), the time late rounded down (right at the deadline: "Overdue"); under an hour "40 min", under a day "2 h 15 min", from a day "1 d 3 h" (minutes left out). `label` names the deadline before its words (two in a table cell); `showDue` writes the due instant under them. The arithmetic is pure and tested (`sla-logic.ts`: `slaReading`, `durationParts`, `slaUrgency` for the application's "most urgent first" order). It does not tick: the application passes a new `now`.
- **2026-10-14 — Internal notes in a conversation (P5.30 b).** `ThreadMessage.internal` / `MessageBubble internal`: the message stays on its author's side, on a new Bubble surface `note` — surface.sunken with a **dashed border.strong** line — and starts with a visible "Internal" mark (a lock and the word, `messages['message.internal']`), read first by assistive technology. A note differs from a reply by its line and its word, never by colour; no warning tone (a note is not a problem).
- **2026-10-14 — ReplyComposer (P5.30 b), in `@veljaos/ui/rich-text`.** RichTextField with two modes (`modes`, default reply and note; two pressed buttons in a group "Message type", the neutral selection; one mode shows no switch); the note's text box on surface.sunken with "Only your team sees internal notes." beside the switch; "@" mentions only in the note mode (a reply leaves the team). Tools under the text: the paperclip (`onAttach`, `accept`; dropping files on the composer is the shortcut; the files are the application's, shown in `attachments` — an AttachmentList), `onInsertLink` (the application opens its own search, e.g. a knowledge base in LookupDialog, and resolves `{ text, href }`; inserted at the caret, http(s) and mailto only), saved replies (`savedReplies`, grouped, searched by typing from 11 as SelectField, D20; inserted at the caret — a one-paragraph reply joins the line). Send (the primary family, light weight) or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter; a promise keeps the text with "Sending…" and empties it when it resolves. Labels from messages or `replyLabel` / `noteLabel` / `noteHint` / `insertLinkLabel`. No helpdesk word in the component.
- **2026-10-14 — RichTextField can be reached from outside (P5.30 b).** `ref` gives a handle: `insert(content)` at the caret where it was before a menu or dialog took the focus (a document, nodes or text; `insertable` decides), `focus()` and `clear()`. `surface` 'sunken' draws the text box on surface.sunken.
- **2026-10-14 — A list worked from the keyboard (P5.30 a).** DataTable's pressable rows (and phone cards) move the focus with ArrowDown / ArrowUp, Home and End (`rowFocusTarget`, pure and tested; `focusNeighbourRow` in data-table-card.tsx), besides Tab; Space presses and Enter opens as before. Every list with `onRowClick` gains it.

### The customer portal and the knowledge base (P5.30 d, e)

- **2026-10-14 — Six help-centre building blocks, generic (P5.30 d, e).** The library had no rating scale, no "Was this helpful?", no proposals while typing, no contents for one long page, no search result list outside the legal search and no category cards outside the Launchpad. Each is generic (no "ticket", "article" or "support" inside; every word is the application's or a provider message), in `packages/ui/src/components/`, with its logic in `help-logic.ts` (unit-tested), stories under "Components/Help/…" (default, every state, long text, phone, Arabic, Japanese, an interaction) and its exports in one block of `index.ts`.
- **2026-10-14 — SatisfactionRating (P5.30 d).** One question on a scale after work was done for the user. The scale is a radio group named by the question (Field `group`): Tab enters it, the arrows (following the page's direction) move and choose. Each step is a tile with the radio, the value (h3 size, semibold, tabular, digits through `format.number`) and the step's words (xs text.secondary): a step is never told by a colour or a face alone, and no step is an emoji. The whole tile is the label, at least 44px high; the chosen tile is the neutral selection (surface.selected, border.selected), only the radio's dot is blue (D17). Desktop: the steps in equal columns; phones: one row per step. An optional comment (TextAreaField "Comment (optional)"), Send (primary filled: the rating is the main action where it is shown). Send without a step says "Choose one of the answers." under the question instead of sending. `onSubmit` may return a promise ("Sending…" beside Send while it runs); `error` is the application's danger Alert above Send. Sent: a polite status with a success CircleCheck, the thanks and "Your answer: 4, Satisfied" with the comment. Controlled (`value`, `commentValue`, `submitted`) or not. Disabled with a visible reason.
- **2026-10-14 — HelpfulFeedback (P5.30 e).** "Was this helpful?" as a named group of two toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`), "Yes" with ThumbsUp and "No" with ThumbsDown — words beside the icons; the pressed one is the neutral selection, and the answer can be changed. Then a polite thanks. After No with `askWhy`: "What was missing?" and a neutral Send (`onComment`, a promise waits). `counts` is the application's sentence ("41 of 46 readers found this helpful").
- **2026-10-14 — LinkSuggestions (P5.30 d).** Pages the application proposes while the user writes (articles while a customer writes a ticket). The application searches (after a pause, 300ms as ComboboxField) and gives them; the box shows them and never takes the focus, opens anything or blocks the form. A raised box with a border (not a toned background: a hint, not a warning), the application's title with a Lightbulb, each suggestion a link with an optional context line and a summary (two lines; the whole summary is the link's description). While searching, the old suggestions stay with "Looking for suggestions…". Without suggestions nothing is drawn but a hidden polite status, so "3 suggestions" / "No suggestions" is announced as they change. `onOpen` reports a press (an application may keep the draft or open a drawer).
- **2026-10-14 — PageContents and RichText `headingIds` (P5.30 e).** "On this page" for one long reading page: the headings as links (subsections indented), the current one neutral (text.primary medium, a border.selected start line, `aria-current="location"`; never blue: it is a place, not an action), following the scroll (`currentEntry`: the last heading above the line under `--liro-shell-top`). A press scrolls (smoothly unless reduced motion), focuses the heading and keeps it current until the scroll ends — the SectionBar's behaviour. Desktop: a list for the side column (`sticky` under the shell); phones: a disclosure, closed unless `defaultOpen`. `RichText` gained `headingIds="<prefix>"`: every top-level h2 and h3 gets a stable id from its words (`richTextHeadings(value, prefix)` in the rich-text subpath lists the same ids, `headingSlug` keeps letters and digits of any script), `tabIndex={-1}` and a scroll margin of `--liro-shell-top` + 16px (WCAG 2.4.11). Which one: SectionBar for a detail page's sections, LegalContents for a legal act, TreeView for a structure to browse.
- **2026-10-14 — SearchResultList (P5.30 e).** What a search across texts found, as a list (a snippet needs the width). LegalSearchPage's snippet idea fits and is reused: the parts are the same shape (`HighlightPart` = `LegalSnippetPart`), so `snippetFromRanges` makes them; each match is a `<mark>` in semibold text.primary on the warning background, in the title and the snippet; the link's name is the whole title. Over the list a polite count ("3 results") or the application's sentence; while searching again a spinner and "Updating…", the old results kept; skeletons at first; EmptyState's no-results or the application's `empty`; ErrorState with "Try again". LegalSearchPage keeps its own row (gazette, status, article link); the two could share `HighlightedText` later.
- **2026-10-14 — CategoryGrid (P5.30 e).** The categories of a collection as cards, the Launchpad's card look without its keys (1–9 are window-wide shortcuts, wrong on a help page) and editing: icon square (blue on hover), the count at the end in the application's words, the title and a description (three lines). The link is named by the title and described by the count and the description. Columns of at least 15rem as many as fit; one on phones.
- **2026-10-14 — The customer portal and the knowledge base (P5.30 d, e; examples T).** Built from PortalShell, PageHeader, SectionCard, RadioGroupField, TextField, TextAreaField, FileDropzone, AttachmentList, DataTable (cards on phones), KeyValueList, MessageThread, RichText and the six blocks above. Ticket statuses in words and tone, each with a hint for the customer: Open (info, "With Liro support"), Replied (warning, "Waiting for your answer"), Paused (neutral), Resolved (success, "Solved: rate the help you got"), Closed (neutral). A resolved ticket shows "Rate the help you got" above the conversation; a reply opens it again; a closed ticket's reply field is disabled with its reason. The new ticket's articles stand beside the form on a desktop (18rem column); on phones the kind is a SelectField and the articles stand right under the subject, in the first screen (lower down, the sticky bottom bar covered part of a link and axe's target-size check failed); the draft is kept when the customer opens a proposed article and comes back. The agents' knowledge base is the same pages inside AppShell (Nikola Ilić, "Helpdesk › Knowledge base"), with each article's author, how helpful readers found it and "Copy link". The portal never receives the agents' internal notes: the dataset has none for it.

### Integration (2026-10-14)

- **2026-10-14 — One Superadmin shell (P5.29, the lead).** Groups Q (System status, Network) and R (incidents, security events, tenants, announcements) share `SuperadminShell` (`screens-R.tsx`) with six module tabs: System status, Incidents, Security events, Network, Tenants, Announcements. Q's `PlatformShell` is a thin wrapper around it. The routes are under `/superadmin/…` (Q's `R_PATHS` match R's `R_ROUTES`), and the operator is Vuk Stojanović.
- **2026-10-14 — One helpdesk shell (P5.30, the lead).** The agents' screens (group S) are under `/helpdesk/…`. The customer portal (group T) stays under `/support/…`; the two had collided on `/support/tickets`. The agents' knowledge base (`/helpdesk/kb`) is the "Knowledge base" tab of `SupportShell` (Tickets, Overview, Knowledge base), which group T's agent pages use too.
- **2026-10-14 — Ticket tones depend on who looks (P5.30, the lead).** The status-to-tone map is the application's data (D1), and "needs your attention" is warning:
  - the agent's map (`TICKET_TONES` in `data-S.ts`): Open warning (waits on the team), Replied info (on its way to the customer);
  - the customer's map (`TICKET_TONES` in `data-T.ts`): Replied warning (an answer waits on them), Open info (with Liro support).
  - Both maps: Paused neutral, Resolved success, Closed neutral. Neither map is in example-shell's one `TONES`: there "Open" is an incident's (danger), so each side keeps its own.
- **2026-10-14 — Ticket 4821's first response is due 09:10 and is overdue at 09:40 (P5.30, the lead).** The brief had 10:30, which is 50 minutes after "now" (09:40), so the agent helper's inbox and ticket page showed "Due in 50 min"; the lead corrected the data (`data-S.ts`) so the example shows an overdue ticket. Five other tickets are overdue too (4818, 4815, 4812, 4809, 4808) and fill the Overdue view.
- **2026-10-14 — `numericFormat` follows the provider's time zone when made without one (P5.29, the lead).** Found by the agent helper: inside the examples' `Tenant` provider, `format.dateTime` showed 06:30 for 08:30+02:00 (in the pinned Chromium, whose container runs in UTC), because `numericFormat('sr-Latn-RS')` built its own `dateTime` / `time` in the device's zone and replaced the provider's. `createFormat` now rebuilds a numericFormat's `dateTime` and `time` for the provider's `timeZone` when numericFormat was given none (a WeakMap marks numericFormat results). Tested in `format.test.ts`. Every example time is now shown in Belgrade time, as the data says.
- **2026-10-14 — Ticket numbers are written without "#" in data (P5.29, P5.30, the lead).** `liro/no-raw-colors` reads "#4821" as a four-digit hex colour (`#RGBA`), so the examples store numbers without the sign and write them through a helper (`ticketRef` in `data-T.ts`) or a template literal; example text says "Support ticket 4821". The rule stays strict (D6): no exception for "#" followed by digits.
- **2026-10-14 — Radix radios in play functions (P5.30, the lead).** Radix chooses a radio on focus but moves focus in a timeout after the keydown, so a play's `userEvent.keyboard('{ArrowDown}')` releases the key before that and nothing is chosen. A play holds the key (`{ArrowDown>}`), waits until the radio is checked, then releases it (`{/ArrowDown}`). This holds for any later keyboard play on a RadioGroup.
- **2026-10-14 — Sticky first-column cells on a layer of their own (`STICKY_START`, the class of P5.28's sticky header).** StatutoryFormPage "Narrow, scrolls sideways" gave two pictures in dark mode, one run in two: its first column (number and label, `sticky start-0` in a region that scrolls sideways) was antialiased one way or the other as Chromium gave the sticky cells a layer or not, as P5.28 found for header cells. `STICKY_START` (`sticky start-0 will-change-transform`, sticky-head.ts) now draws the statutory grid's first column and corner; 8 runs in a row gave one picture. The other grids' sticky first columns (DataTable in a card, AttendanceGrid, ShiftPlanner, ResourceSchedule, RoomRack, EditableGrid) have not flipped in thousands of runs; they move to `STICKY_START` with the next full picture run (P5.31), so their pictures change once.

## Workflows of the accounting product (P5.31–P5.43)

### Document inbox and recognition (P5.31)

- **2026-10-14 — PageViewer, not DocumentFrame, beside recognised fields (P5.31).** A recognised value must show where it was read: a region on the page, given by the application in the page's own units. DocumentFrame shows a viewer that runs on another origin in a sandbox; the host can neither see its drawing nor mark on it, and pointing at a region would need a version 2 of the frame protocol and every viewer to implement it. The recognition service already has the pages as images (it read them), so the library draws them itself: **PageViewer** (`page-viewer.tsx`, logic in `page-viewer-logic.ts`, tested) shows a document's pages as the application's images — a scan, a photo, a rendered PDF page — one at a time, with DocumentFrame's toolbar (previous / next page, "Page 1 of 2", zoom 50–300% in DocumentFrame's steps; 100% fits the width, more scrolls both ways) and one region highlighted (`regions`, `highlight`). The page is paper: light in both themes (`data-liro-theme="light"`, as PrintPage) and never mirrored in right-to-left (`dir="ltr"`, as FloorPlan's canvas); regions stand where they were measured, from the page's top-left corner, as percentages of the page (`regionBox`). A new highlight turns to its page (reported with `onPageChange`) and is scrolled into view; the first one is not scrolled to, so a picture never moves. "Highlighted: Total, page 1 of 2" is announced politely. States: loading (a page-shaped skeleton), `error` with "Try again", and `unavailable` — the application's own words and actions in place of the pages (a PDF locked with a password). DocumentFrame stays the viewer for a document the application shows from another origin (a signing service's preview).
- **2026-10-14 — The highlight is a marker pen (P5.31).** The region is status.warning.bg multiplied over the page (`mix-blend-multiply`: the printed text stays readable through it, as the search's matches on warning.bg) inside a 2px status.warning.fg frame, its name on a raised tag above it (below it in the page's top tenth, `labelSide`). Not warning.solid: the solid is allowed only where `tone-usage.test.ts` lists it, and the paper is light in both themes anyway. Not blue (D17): a highlight is not a selection or an action.
- **2026-10-14 — RecognizedField: the application's confidence, never the library's verdict (P5.31).** It wraps any field of the library; `children(describedBy)` renders the field with the note's id, so the confidence is read with the field. Under the field one xs line: "Confidence: 98%" in the application's words (`confidence` is a string: "98%", "from SEF", "not on the document"); a reading the application calls uncertain (`low`) has a TriangleAlert and "Low confidence" (or the application's `lowLabel`, "Not found on the page") in status.warning.fg, weight 500 — never colour alone. The component never turns a figure into "low" (the D30 rule for HealthList). Once the user changes the value, "Changed by you" with a Pencil replaces it. "Show where it was read" (`onShowSource`) is a link-styled button (text.link, ScanSearch, 24px high); while its region is shown (`sourceShown`) it is pressed (`aria-pressed`) with the neutral selection. ChangeableValue stays for a value the system filled in from its own records.
- **2026-10-14 — The document inbox is built from the library (P5.31).** The inbox is ListPage + FilterBar + DataTable: type, sender, received, source, amount and the state in words and tone (New, Recognised, Needs review, Posted, Rejected, Duplicate — the six of the plan; the application's map `DOC_TONES`); a new document's condition stands in words under its state (Recognising…, Not recognised: enter by hand, Locked with a password, Scan cannot be read), so the six states stay six. Views To review, Posted, Rejected and duplicates, All. "Add documents" is a FileDropzone above the card ("Choose files" is the way, dropping the shortcut; "Take a photo" on phones, `camera`), its description names the inbox's e-mail address; the main action "Review 11 documents" beside it. Checked rows: "Review" and "Reject…" (ReasonConfirmDialog, the count in the question). A done document opens in a QuickPreview with its page.
- **2026-10-14 — The review is decided document by document (P5.31).** WorklistPage, as the bank statement's lines (P5.23): the documents to review at the side (the queue is fixed when the review opens; a decided document stays in it with its new state), one in focus: its page (PageViewer) beside the recognised values (a container query: side by side from 48rem of the detail's width, the page first below it), then the lines (EditableGrid: description, unit, quantity, price, amount, account; the suggested account's reason as a line detail, an uncertain reading as a warning message under its row). The supplier is a LookupField: matched in the catalog by the tax number read ("Matched in your suppliers by tax number 106543218."), or "Not in your suppliers: tax number 109876543 was read" with "+ Create supplier". VAT by rate and the total as MoneyFields, a rate the document does not have empty ("not on the document"). Decisions in the detail's bar, the main one last: Save for later, Mark as duplicate… (CandidateList of the application's candidates for the original, one choice), Reject… (the application's reasons), Confirm and post ("Confirm and import" for a bank statement, "Confirm and file" for a contract or other); a toast with Undo, and the next document still to review opens. **Keyboard first:** Tab goes through the fields; Enter in a field confirms once the field has read its text (the decision waits one task), never inside an open list or the lines grid. A photo of a document already in the inbox shows DuplicateWarning with the original's link.
- **2026-10-14 — A document that cannot be read yet (P5.31).** Recognising: the page and skeleton fields with "Recognising the document…"; Confirm is unavailable with "Recognition is still running.". Recognition failed: a warning Alert and plain fields to enter by hand (no confidence — nothing was read). A PDF locked with a password: PageViewer's `unavailable` with "Enter the password…" (a Dialog with PasswordField; the password is used once and not kept), Confirm unavailable with "The file is locked with a password.". An unreadable scan: the blurred page, a warning Alert with "Upload a better copy" and "Enter by hand" (neutral secondary, D23).
- **2026-10-14 — Every sticky first column on a layer of its own (P5.31).** DataTable (in a card, with or without the selection column), AttendanceGrid, ShiftPlanner, ResourceSchedule and EditableGrid now use `STICKY_START` (and `STICKY_START_AFTER_SELECT` after DataTable's 48px selection column), as StatutoryFormPage has since P5.29. One compositing layer, one antialiasing: the same story gives one picture. Announced in P5.29's report; done here because every picture is made again anyway.
- **2026-10-14 — Merge values: saved replies and previews filled in (the owner's request, P5.31).** A merge field takes the application's value: plain text, or a typed value (date, instant, time, number, amount as decimal strings) written through the provider's `format` — never rounded (D4). A field may be **computed**: `computed: 'today'` is the provider's `today` (moved by whole days with `offsetDays`), `computed: 'now'` the application's `now` (never the device's clock, D25); the key is the application's ("date_now"). A field without a value stays a pill marked "No value" (dashed, warning tone, its name read) and a line under the text names it; nothing is replaced by an empty string or a guess. RichText (`mergeValues`) previews a template with sample values; RichTextField and ReplyComposer (`mergeValues`, `now`) write the values in for the first text and for everything inserted (a saved reply, a field chosen from "{{"); a template editor passes no values and keeps pills. `resolveMergeText` fills a plain-text template (a subject, an SMS). The library writes values; it never computes business values.

### The accountant's workspace (P5.32)

- **2026-10-14 — The accountant's workspace is built from the library; nothing new was needed (P5.32).** The clients overview is ListPage + FilterBar + DataTable (views My clients / Needs attention / All clients with counts; filters Accountant, Deadline — Overdue, Due today or tomorrow, Due within 7 days, Due this month — and Problem, all inline; search by name or tax number). Each row: the client with "PIB …" under it, the accountant, the next open deadline (its kind, DueDate, "Prepared" when it is, "N more open"), missing documents (the count in words and what they are), open tasks, last activity (time and what happened) and health (StatusBadge in the firm's words and tone — On track success, Needs attention warning, At risk danger, New client neutral — with the reason under it). The order is the application's order of urgency (at risk first, then the nearest open deadline, then the most missing documents); the list never sorts it and never turns a figure into a state (D30). 25 clients a page through DataTable's cursor paging: with 107 to 214 two-line rows the page is long and the story, accessibility and phone checks become slow; a virtualised DataTable needs `maxHeight` and draws one-line 44px rows, which would cut the deadline, missing-document and health lines. The row menu offers "Ask the client…" and "Month-end checklist"; a row opens the checklist.
- **2026-10-14 — A deadlines calendar across clients is CalendarView (P5.32).** Month on a desktop, agenda on a phone (CalendarView's own default), every client's deadline an all-day event "VAT return · Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o." with "VAT return, September 2026 · Prepared" as its description and the state's tone (Submitted success, Prepared info, Not started warning, Overdue danger: never the tone alone, the words are in the description and the day list). Above it Accountant (Everyone / Snežana / Marko), Kind and "Show submitted" (off: what is submitted is no longer a deadline); the 15th's dozens of VAT returns are CalendarView's "+N more" day list. A press opens the client's month-end checklist.
- **2026-10-14 — The month-end checklist is SetupChecklist (P5.32).** A client's month close ("Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o.: September 2026") is the same shape as a first-run setup: steps done (who and when), the one to do now highlighted with its action, steps blocked with the reason in words ("Waits for the purchase invoices (step 3)"), progress "3 of 7 done". No sibling component was needed. Beside it (300px side column, under it on phones) the client's deadlines, the requests sent to it and its facts. The step's action names what it asks ("Ask for the missing documents…"); the header keeps the general "Ask the client…".
- **2026-10-14 — Fast client switching at 214 clients is AppShell's company switcher, unchanged (P5.32).** The 214 clients (name, "PIB …" as the description, the account's status — Rakić Pekara SZR "Suspended" —, the application's note "3 missing" / "2 tasks") with pinned and recent clients; the list opens on the current company (the firm's own books on the overview), is virtualised (aria-setsize 214) and searched locally by name or tax number, without accents and in any word order ("mlin vojvo" finds Vojvođanka Mlin a.d.); Enter or a press opens that client's checklist. On phones the full-screen sheet with the search field at the top. Checked by two interaction stories (desktop by tax number, phone by name).
- **2026-10-14 — "Ask the client" is a Drawer for the accountant and a request page in the client's portal (P5.32).** The accountant's side (D14: a short edit with the list still in view, an end Drawer titled "Ask the client" with the client as `subject`, D22): What do you need (Documents / Answers, RadioGroupField), the items (one TextField per document or TextAreaField per question, "Add a document", remove with a CompactIconButton), Due (DateField, required, not in the past), Message, and the e-mail to the client's contact as an explicit checkbox (D24); Cancel / Send request. The application's checks show under the fields after Send. The client's side is PortalShell ("Client portal", Milica Petrović of Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o.; sections Requests with "2 open" and Documents): the open and earlier requests as DataTables (cards on phones; "1 of 3 given"), and one request on its own page — the accountant's message, then per document a FileDropzone named by the document ("Take a photo" on phones) that becomes an AttachmentList row once uploaded (removable until sent), per question a TextAreaField; one primary "Send to Snežana Jelić" (D13; what is left out stays on the request; nothing given says so in a danger Alert). Request states in both sides' words: Open warning (waits on the client), Answered info, Done success. Both sides read the same requests (kept above the screens), so a request sent from the Drawer is listed on the client's checklist.
- **2026-10-14 — Example data (P5.32, P5.36).** Knjigovodstvo Jelić: 214 clients — fourteen written out (Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o., Rakić Pekara SZR with an overdue payroll tax return and a suspended account, Medic Lab Niš d.o.o. without bank statements, Medija Print d.o.o. with an August VAT return overdue, …; the companies of `example-shell`'s switcher keep their tax numbers) and 200 made deterministically from name parts; VAT returns for September due 15.10.2026, payroll tax returns on 15, 20 or 30 October, a few annual accounts on 31 October (fictitious dates). Liro's plans: Start 3.900,00, Business 14.900,00, Pro 29.900,00 RSD a month without VAT; the seller "Liro Software d.o.o." with illustrative numbers; Kvadrat Gradnja on Business with Projects (2.400,00 RSD), 24 of 30 users as the administration's overview says, renewing 01.01.2027.

### Statements of open items, IOS (P5.33)

- **2026-10-14 — ValueComparison (P5.33).** The same things as two sources record them, side by side — our open items beside a partner's statement, a payment as each side booked it. A table: the row's name, the two sources' values (figures tabular at the end), the result in words — "Same" with a Check (text.secondary), or "Differs" or the application's `note` ("Only in their statement", "Dates differ") with a TriangleAlert in status.warning.fg on a status.warning.bg row; "2 of 4 differ" above it, announced politely. Phones: one card per row, each value labelled with its source. It compares nothing: which rows differ, and why, is the application's (`differs`, `note`). Loading: skeleton rows; no rows: `empty` ("Nothing to compare"). Helper `valueComparisonCounts` (the name `comparisonCounts` is LegalCompare's).
- **2026-10-14 — IOS: the statements of open items are built from the library (P5.33).** The partners are ListPage + FilterBar + DataTable: balance at the cut-off (the sum of the open items, whole paras), the statement's number, date, way and opening, the state (Not sent, Sent, Opened, Confirmed, Disputed, No answer; the application's map: on its way blue, confirmed green, disputed warning — it waits on us —, no answer after the deadline danger, not sent neutral) with the answer date, the reminder or their balance under it. ### The Liro Assistant (P5.34)

- **2026-10-14 — The assistant is data, never a model (P5.34).** Nothing in the library or the examples calls a model. An answer is the application's data: a list of blocks (`AnswerBlock`: `heading`, `text`, `list`, `table`, `chart`, `sources`) and a state (`AnswerState`: thinking, streaming, done, stopped, error, noAccess). "Streaming" is a state the application renders — the text it has so far, "Writing…" and Stop; nothing in the library runs a timer. The examples choose a fixed answer object by its question (`data-X.ts`, `answerKeyOf`).
- **2026-10-14 — Four generic pieces and a page (P5.34).** `AssistantAnswer` (one answer), `ProposedAction` (an action the assistant proposes), `AssistantComposer` (the question box), `AssistantPanel` (the side panel) and the template `AskPage`. No domain word inside: "invoice", "post", "salaries" are the application's words. Logic in `assistant-logic.ts` (unit-tested: `answerBusy`, `shownBlocks`, `followUpsShown`, `canReport`, `questionReady`, `questionKey`, `actionOffers`, `actionSettled`, `answerSources`).
- **2026-10-14 — Labelled AI-generated; a wrong answer is reported (P5.34).** Over every answer the assistant's name and AgentMark with the words "AI-generated" (`messages['assistant.generated']`; AgentMark gained an optional `label`, default still "Agent"). Neutral, never blue (D17). Under a complete or stopped answer "Report a wrong answer" (a small neutral text button with a flag) opens ReasonConfirmDialog — titled by the action, the question as its subject (D22), the application's reasons or a required text; `onReport` receives the answer; then "Thank you. Your report was sent." (`reported` controls it).
- **2026-10-14 — An answer's blocks (P5.34).** Paragraphs and headings take their direction from their content (D15). A **table** is a real table (caption, column headers, numbers at the end in tabular digits, a total row the application computed) on the "Ask" page; in the side panel (`size="panel"`) and on phones each row is a small card — the first cell as its title, the others as label / value lines — so nothing scrolls sideways (D19). A row's `href` links its first cell to the record it came from. A **chart** is a slot (`kind: 'chart'`, a ReactNode): the application passes one from `@veljaos/ui/charts`, so the main entry never loads Recharts. **Sources** are a numbered list of links with a detail line, under "Sources".
- **2026-10-14 — The answer's states (P5.34).** Thinking: a spinner and "Thinking…" (polite status), no blocks. Streaming: the blocks so far, "Writing…" and Stop (neutral). Stopped: the blocks written, "Stopped. The answer may be incomplete." and Try again. Error: the application's words in a danger Alert with Try again as a neutral secondary button (D23). No access: the application's words ("You do not have permission to see salaries.") in a **neutral** Alert with a lock — a permission is not a failure. While thinking or streaming the answer is `aria-busy`, so assistive technology reads it once it is written. Follow-ups (the application's questions as buttons) only under a complete answer.
- **2026-10-14 — A proposed action always waits (P5.34).** `ProposedAction` is a raised card with a border (never a tone: a proposal is not a status): "Proposed action" (Sparkles, xs text.secondary), the title, a line, the facts (KeyValueList), "Nothing is done until you confirm.", then Dismiss and Confirm (the main action last, D13). Only Confirm runs it, through the application's `onConfirm`; a promise shows "Working…" with both buttons waiting; then a polite status with the application's outcome ("Posted on 14.10.2026. as entry 2026-0884." with a link), or "Dismissed. Nothing was done."; `failed` shows the application's words in a danger Alert and Confirm can be pressed again. `unavailableReason` disables Confirm and says why in words.

### The project timeline (P5.37)

- **2026-10-14 — Gantt on SVAR React Gantt 2.7.3, MIT edition, `@veljaos/ui/gantt` (P5.37, owner: "an MIT library: evaluate SVAR React Gantt (MIT edition, never PRO) and Frappe Gantt …; pick one, pin it, add its notice, record why").** SVAR was chosen over Frappe Gantt (evaluation of 2026-10-14): React-native and typed, milestones, a hierarchy (summary rows with `parent`), all four dependency types, progress, an action bus to stop and report edits (`api.intercept`), React templates for bars (`taskTemplate`), scale labels as functions (`format`), `readonly`, and colours behind CSS variables. Frappe has no keyboard, no ARIA, no milestones or hierarchy, no React integration, takes "today" from the device's clock (D25) and writes task names with `innerHTML`. **Pinned at 2.7.3** (published 2026-09-09, more than two weeks old); 2.8.x was too new. Checked in 2.7.3's code before pinning: `type: 'milestone'`, `type: 'summary'` with `parent` and `open`, links `e2s` / `s2s` / `e2e` / `s2e`, `progress` with its drag marker, `api.intercept`, `taskTemplate`, `scales[].format` as a function, `readonly`, `start` / `end` with `autoScale={false}`. The MIT store switches the PRO features off at runtime (`markers`, baselines, critical path, undo, auto-scheduling, calendars, resources); none is used.
  1. **A subpath of its own** (tsup entry `gantt`, `exports["./gantt"]`), as `@veljaos/ui/diagram`: only `dist/gantt.js` imports `@svar-ui/react-gantt`; the root `@veljaos/ui` exports nothing of it. `packages/ui/src/gantt/`: `gantt.tsx` (the component, the table, the chart wrapper), `gantt-parts.tsx` (the row words, the list by phase, the four dialogs), `gantt-logic.ts` (pure, tested: `ganttRows`, `phaseGroups`, `chartDate`/`chartEnd`/`dayOfChartDate`, `durationDays`, `movedDates`, `draggedDates`, `dragChange`, `chartRange`, `nowPosition`, `isProgress`, `progressWidth`, `linkType`/`dependencyType`, `predecessors`, `dependsOn`, `dependencyCandidates`, `applyGanttChange`, `nextDependencyId`, `forbiddenGanttPackages`), `gantt.css`. The consumer-check app renders an editing Gantt from the packed subpath (`apps/consumer-check/src/GanttExample.tsx`).
  2. **Never the trial, PRO or GPL builds.** `@svar-ui/trial-*` (a paid licence) and `wx-react-gantt` (GPLv3, SVAR's old name) must never enter the lockfile: `gantt-logic.test.ts` reads `pnpm-lock.yaml` and fails if `forbiddenGanttPackages` finds either.
  3. **SVAR's style sheets, themes and icon font are not shipped.** SVAR's `style.css` / `all.css` hold raw colours in their theme blocks; the theme components (`Willow`, `WillowDark`, `Material`) load `https://cdn.svar.dev/fonts/wxi/wx-icons.css` when rendered. Gantt renders none of them. `gantt/gantt.css` sets the `--wx-*` variables SVAR's components read to Liro tokens in the `.liro-gantt` scope only and keeps the structural rules of `@svar-ui/react-gantt`'s `dist/index.css` (MIT, noted in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) that position and layer the chart's parts, selected by SVAR's stable class names (`wx-bar`, `wx-scale`…), never its hashed ones; imported into the base layer of `styles.css` (no hex, rgb or hsl). SVAR's CellGrid paints the grid into a canvas image from a colour it reads once; the image is hidden and the grid is two CSS gradients in `border.subtle`, so it follows the theme. SVAR's one icon on the chart (the X that removes a chosen dependency, `wxi-close`) is lucide's `x` as a CSS mask in the button's colour. SVAR measures and positions in physical pixels (`left`, `dir="ltr"` on the chart), so `left`/`right` in `gantt.css` are the time axis, not page layout.
  4. **Controlled; every edit reported, nothing saved.** Gantt passes its rows to SVAR and intercepts what would change them: a drag (`update-task` with a whole number of days; `drag-task` is allowed while it moves, blocked on a phase), a progress drag, a dependency drawn between two bars' end dots (`add-link`), a chosen dependency removed (`delete-link`). Each becomes one `GanttChange` through `onChange` — `{ type: 'dates', id, start, end }`, `{ type: 'progress', id, progress }`, `{ type: 'add-dependency', from, to, dependencyType }`, `{ type: 'remove-dependency', id }` — and SVAR is rebuilt from the application's rows, so a drag the application has not accepted goes back. A double click opens Change dates…. SVAR's own keys (Backspace deletes, Ctrl+C/X/V/D) and its add / delete / copy / move / indent / split actions are blocked. `applyGanttChange` is what an application may do (phases are not recomputed, dependants not moved: scheduling is the application's; example AA lets each phase span its tasks). A phase's dates are the application's: it has no Change menu and its bar does not drag.
  5. **Every drag has another way (WCAG 2.5.7):** each task and milestone row has a Change menu (`Change Floors 3–4`, a 28px button) — Move… (a new start; the length stays, "Ends on …"), Change dates… (a range; a milestone's one date), Set progress… (0–100, a decimal string), Dependencies… (what it comes after, each with Remove; a task to add, chosen from the ones that make no loop (`dependencyCandidates`), and how, in words: "Starts when it finishes", "Starts when it starts", "Finishes when it finishes", "Finishes when it starts"). Each dialog is titled by its action with the row bold under it (D22). Every reported change is announced politely. Moving a bar with Enter and the arrow keys (as Diagram) is not built: the dialogs are the keyboard way.
  6. **The table is the accessible plan.** At the start of the timeline, a table (`role="table"`, named by `label`) with one row per bar at the same 44px: the row header names the row in full ("Task: Floors 3–4, in Structure, 05.10.2026. – 30.10.2026., 40% done, Crew Ilić, At risk, After: Floors 1–2"); visibly the name (cut with "…" when long, the full name in `title`), its dates and who does it, its state, its progress and, when the application gives them, a phase's budget and what was spent with the application's verdict ("Over budget", warning). Every bar carries the same name for assistive technology (visually hidden, through `taskTemplate`). The chart is one scrolling region ("Timeline: Residential building Liman 4", Tab stop, arrows scroll it, described by how to use it); SVAR's own focusable layout box is taken out of the Tab order. The header rows of the table and the time scale stay below the shell while the page scrolls (D21, `useStickyHead`'s `--liro-head-shift` on both).
  7. **The one "now" marker is ours (D25).** SVAR's markers are a PRO feature (the MIT store empties them). Gantt draws NowMarker into SVAR's chart area from the application's `now` ("HH:mm" of the provider's `today`, a local date-time or an instant shown in the provider's `timeZone`), at the x SVAR gives a date (its own scale's `diff`, times the column width it settled on — SVAR widens the columns of a short plan to fill the chart), plus the part of the day passed (`nowPosition`). Named "Now, 14.10.2026. 09:40". The chart opens scrolled so that now is in view.
  8. **Look (D17, tokens only):** a task is a bar in its tone (neutral unless the application gives a state: "At risk" warning), its progress a 4px line along its bottom in the text colour (never a fill under the text, so the text keeps its contrast); a phase a slim `surface.inverse` bar with its progress in `surface.raised`; a milestone a `text.primary` diamond with its name after it; dependencies `border.control` lines (3:1), strong on hover; the chosen row `surface.selected` with the 3px `border.selected` bar, never blue.
  9. **Scales: months (default) and days.** Labels from the provider (D11): "Oct", "October 2026" through `format.monthName`, years and day numbers as digits. **No weeks scale:** SVAR places weeks by its own locale's first day, not the provider's (D11); days and months need none.
  10. **Right to left: the timeline is mirrored** (SVAR has no right-to-left). The chart is drawn with `transform: scaleX(-1)` so time runs from the leading edge beside the table (which stands at the start), and every text in it is turned back (`data-gantt-text`, the scale's labels). **Dragging is off in right-to-left**: SVAR measures the pointer in physical pixels, so a mirrored drag would move the bar the wrong way; the rows' dialogs edit instead. The table, the list and the dialogs follow the page's direction.
  11. **Phones** (below 48em, or `screen="phone"`): the plan opens as the list by phase (each phase a card: name, dates, progress, budget and spent, state; its tasks and milestones with dates, progress, who and "After: …"); "Timeline" shows the chart alone, read-only, scrolling sideways inside its card (D19). Editing says "Open this plan on a larger screen to change it." The list is the plan as text on every width ("List").
  12. **States:** `loading` (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`), no rows ("No tasks yet"), `error` (the message and Try again).
  - Messages (new, at the end of `messages.ts` under "P5.37 gantt"): `gantt.kindPhase`, `kindTask`, `kindMilestone`, `rowName`, `inPhase`, `done`, `after`, the column headers (`task`, `progress`, `planned`, `actual`), `actions`, the menu entries (`move`, `changeDates`, `setProgress`, `dependencies`), the dialogs' titles, fields, checks and buttons, the four dependency kinds, the announcements, the views and scales, `monthYear`, `timeline`, `timelineHint`, `dragHint`, `now`, `empty`, `loading`, `error`, `retry`, `editOnLargerScreen`.
- **2026-10-14 — Pictures of a Gantt (P5.37).** The stories wait for `data-ready` (`ganttReady` in `gantt-story-data.ts`, inside `waitFor`), set once SVAR has measured its chart (`resize-chart`), the now marker is placed and the chart scrolled to it. SVAR measures with ResizeObservers, as React Flow does; nothing depends on the device's clock (the chart's range comes from the rows and the provider's `today`, never `new Date()`).
- **2026-10-14 — Example screens of P5.37 (group AA).** `apps/storybook/src/examples/screens-AA.tsx` + `data-AA.ts`: Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o.'s **"Residential building Liman 4"** (`/projects/liman-4/timeline`) on 14.10.2026 at 09:40 — Design, Permits, Excavation, Foundations, Structure, Roof, Installations, Finishes, Handover, with their tasks (Studio Linija d.o.o., Crew Petrović, Crew Ilić, Crew Jovanović, Crew Lazić, Elektro Sistem d.o.o., the City of Novi Sad), milestones (Design approved, Building permit issued, Structure complete, Handover to buyers) and 23 dependencies; each phase's budget against what was spent (249.000.000,00 and 112.295.000,00 RSD in all; Permits over budget); Floors 3–4 at risk (the fourth floor's slab is poured at night on 15.10. — Nikola Marković's changed shift in group Y). The screen plays the application: it applies each change and lets each phase span its tasks again (`applyPlanChange`). Desktop and phone; also by days and with Move… open (`'!dev'`).

### E-mail and notification templates (P5.38)

- **2026-10-14 — EmailPreview: a message as its reader sees it (P5.38).** New `EmailPreview`: From, To and Subject over a thin rule, the sender's logo at the start, the body, the footer in small grey text under a thin rule — as simple as the printouts (D27): black and grey, no boxes, frames or shaded bands, the brand colour only in links. Two segmented switches over it: Width (Desktop 600px / Phone 360px, never wider than the room) and Mail client (Light / Dark); the message resolves its tokens in the chosen scheme (`data-liro-theme`), as a dark mail client inverts a message whatever the page's theme. Controlled or not; `controls={false}` hides the switches; `lang` marks a variant in another language (D15).
- **2026-10-14 — The preview's sample data uses the shared merge values (P5.38).** No substitution of our own: the preview is `RichText` with `mergeValues` and the subject `resolveMergeText` (the lead's `@veljaos/ui/rich-text`, P5.31), written through the provider's `format`. The fields are typed (dates, amounts in RSD, a number) and one is computed from the provider's today (`date_now`, "Today", in the payment reminder: "On {{date_now}} invoice … is still open."). The samples are plain records in `data-AB.ts` (`SAMPLE_VALUES`): Gradska toplana Novi Sad (every field filled) and Stanogradnja Plus d.o.o. (no contact person, no payment reference yet — those stay pills marked "No value"); one sample choice above the preview serves the preview and "Send test". The editor's RichTextField keeps the fields as pills (no `mergeValues` there: the template is edited, not a message).

### IPS NBS QR and payment orders (P5.40)

- **2026-10-14 — QR codes are real (P5.40).** QrCode encodes any text in the browser (`qr` 0.7.2, MIT OR Apache-2.0, used under MIT, no dependencies; published 2026-09-28) and draws one SVG path, dark on the light surface in both themes (`data-liro-theme="light"`, as paper), with a 4-module quiet zone, medium error correction, named by `label`; `size` in px or `fill` (a printout's slot). A text too long for any code shows the provider's message, never a broken code. **Fixed as a class:** every illustrative, unreadable code in stories and examples (StoryCode, `illustrativeCode`, a lucide icon standing in for a fiscal code) is now a real QrCode; `story-code.tsx` and `illustrativeCode` are removed.
- **2026-10-14 — IPS NBS QR text (P5.40).** `ipsQrText(payment)` writes the IPS QR text of the National Bank of Serbia from the application's payment and names every problem by field (`IpsProblem`, words from `messages['ips.problem']`): tags K|V|C|R|N|I|P|SF|S|M|JS|RO|RL|RP in that order; K PR (a bill), PT (shown by the merchant), PK (shown by the buyer), EK; the payee's account normalised to 18 digits and its MOD 97 control number checked; the amount "RSD294000,50" from the decimal string (decimal comma, no separators, 0,01 to 14 whole digits; more than two decimals is a problem, never rounded, D4); SF required on a bill (3 digits, first 1 or 2); M required at a point of sale; RO the model and number (model 97's control number checked, written without dashes; no model is "00"); lengths 70 / 35 / 140; Latin letters (Serbian ones too), digits and common punctuation, never "|". A national payment standard is a format, like a locale's digits; what is paid is the application's. **Source:** ips.nbs.rs was blocked by the environment's network policy, so the guidelines PDF was not read; the rules come from two public MIT implementations (`ips-qr-code`, `nbs-ips-qr`, read only, not installed) and are checked against a known valid code. To confirm with the NBS validator when the site is reachable.
- **2026-10-14 — Payment orders as their real forms (P5.40).** PaymentOrderForm draws a bank's paper payment order — in Serbia forms 1 (nalog za uplatu), 2 (nalog za isplatu) and 3 (nalog za prenos) — with its boxes (an official form is its real grid, D28), black on white in both themes; every word is the application's (the official Serbian labels in the examples). The IPS QR code stands on forms 1 and 3; a withdrawal pays out cash and has none. The examples' screen (Banking → Payment orders) checks the order when the user prints or downloads, each problem under its field and the first focused.
- **2026-10-14 — The till's two instant payments (P5.40).** The till shows the merchant's IPS QR code (PT: the merchant category and the sale's 19-digit reference), or the cashier scans the buyer's code (PK) with ScanField; the bank's answer is the application's (`cardState`). PaymentDialog draws no frame for an empty code.
- **2026-10-14 — Valid control numbers in the examples (P5.40).** The examples' account numbers and model 97 references now carry valid control numbers (160-0000012345678-67, 160-0000000456789-28, "97 32-2026-0412", "97 14-2026-0418", "97 38-2026-0410"), so every IPS code scans as a bank would accept it.

### Maps (P5.41)

- **2026-10-14 — Maps on Leaflet 1.9.4, `@veljaos/ui/map` (P5.41, owner: "add maps … show lines around that municipality, or … geolocation confirmation; use open source systems").** Leaflet 1.9.4 (BSD-2-Clause, published 2023-05-18, no dependencies), pinned exactly, a runtime dependency of `@veljaos/ui` imported only by the new subpath (tsup entry `map`, `exports["./map"]`; only `dist/map.js` imports `leaflet`; consumer-check renders both components from the packed tarball, `apps/consumer-check/src/MapExample.tsx`). `@types/leaflet` 1.9.22 (MIT) is a development dependency. **Never react-leaflet** (Hippocratic License 2.1, not open source): `map/map-canvas.tsx` is our own thin wrapper on Leaflet's API. **Never MapLibre GL** here: WebGL pictures are not stable. Leaflet draws with **SVG** (`renderer: L.svg()`), with every animation off (zoom, fade, inertia), so a fitted view and its picture are the same every time.
  1. **Leaflet's style sheet, controls and images are not shipped.** `map/map.css` keeps the structural rules of `dist/leaflet.css` (panes, tiles, the SVG layer, touch actions; BSD-2-Clause, noticed) with tokens for every colour; imported into the base layer of `styles.css` (no hex, rgb or hsl). Shapes take their colours from CSS classes (CSS wins over the attributes Leaflet writes), so they follow the theme. Zoom in, zoom out and "Show all" are our IconButtons with lucide icons, at the page's end corner over the map. Leaflet's attribution control is off; the **tiles' attribution, from the application, is always written under the map** when tiles are given.
  2. **No backend (D1).** The base map is optional — `tiles?: { url, attribution, urlDark? }`, the application's (its own tile server, or OpenStreetMap's with its attribution); without tiles only the shapes are drawn on `surface.sunken`. Shapes are GeoJSON (`Polygon` / `MultiPolygon`, [longitude, latitude], holes after the outer ring). **The library never calls `navigator.geolocation`**: "Use my location" calls the application's `onLocate` (a returned promise shows "Finding your location…"), which asks the browser and passes back `{ lat, lng, accuracy, at }`. Stories and examples pass no tiles: no network in tests, stable pictures; the docs say a real application passes its tile source.
  3. **AreaMap** — areas (municipalities, a tax's zones, service areas) as lines and light fills in their tone: neutral or one of the five categorical chart colours (`--liro-chart-category1…5`, the validated palette); the chosen area neutral (D17: `border.selected` line, `surface.selected` fill; in the list the selected bar). Each area's name on the map where it fits: placed at its polygon's centroid, or — for a ring around a hole — at the point inside farthest from every line (`labelPoint`); measured and shown only when its box stands wholly inside its area, clear of holes and notches (`labelFits`), never cut; the list names every area. **The list beside the map is the keyboard's and the screen reader's way** (a single-choice listbox, arrows / Home / End move and choose, `areaListKeyTarget`; the choice is announced); a click on an area chooses too. An optional `point` (an address) with "Falls in: Zone II" (`areaAt` / `pointInArea`, built on FloorPlan's `pointInPolygon`); the legend in the application's words. Phones: the point and the list first, the map full width under them. States: loading, empty, error.
  4. **LocationCheck** — made for a phone first: the workplace (a circle of metres or a polygon, dashed in `text.secondary`, 3:1), the person's position (a dot) with its accuracy circle, and **the state in words and tone as the application decides it**: inside (success), outside (warning), unknown (neutral), denied (warning), with the application's detail; the facts in words (the allowed area, the application's distance, the accuracy through `format.number`, the time through `format.time`); "Use my location"; the check-in (or any action needing the place) unavailable with the application's reason (UnavailableAction). `distanceMeters` (haversine, IUGG mean radius) and `withinRadius` are helpers for applications; the verdict is never the component's.
  5. **Accessibility.** The map is one Tab stop, a region named "Map: …", described by its keys: the arrow keys pan and plus / minus zoom (Leaflet's keyboard handler); the buttons zoom and fit. Nothing needs dragging. Every shape is also in words (the list, the facts). Labels on the map are hidden from assistive technology (the list says them).
  6. **Right to left:** a map is **never mirrored** (`dir="ltr"` on it: east stays right; coordinates are never flipped); the list, the facts, the buttons and the legend follow the page.
  - Messages (new, at the end of `messages.ts` under "P5.41 map"): `map.keys`, `map.zoomIn`, `map.zoomOut`, `map.showAll`, `map.name`, `map.areas`, `map.legend`, `map.fallsIn`, `map.fallsInNone`, `map.chosen`, `map.empty`, `map.loading`, `map.error`, `map.retry`, `location.inside`, `location.outside`, `location.unknown`, `location.denied`, `location.locate`, `location.locating`, `location.accuracy`, `location.takenAt`, `location.allowed`, `location.position`.
- **2026-10-14 — Maps in charts: RegionChart (P5.41, owner: "maps in charts — for companies working in several countries, or that want to see their regions").** A choropleth with an optional point or bubble per place, exported from `@veljaos/ui/map` (`RegionChart`, `RegionChartArea`, `RegionChartPlace`), drawn on the same Leaflet SVG map without tiles, and built as a chart of `@veljaos/ui/charts`' kind:
  1. **The charts' frame, reused, without Recharts.** RegionChart stands in the charts' `ChartCard` (title and description, the application's `controls`, the 28px "Show as table" button, the legend above the plot — under it on phones —, the loading skeleton, the empty state `chart.noData` and the error with Retry; `defaultView`), and its tooltip is the charts' `ChartTooltipContent`. That body, the swatch and the legend moved unchanged from `primitives/chart.tsx` to a new `primitives/chart-parts.tsx` (re-exported by `chart.tsx`), so the map subpath imports them without Recharts; `ChartCard` gained a `block` skeleton (one block, for a map). `dist/map.js` imports Leaflet and no Recharts (checked).
  2. **Values are decimal strings (D4).** The step an area falls in is found by comparing its value with the application's `breaks` exactly, as strings (`regionStep`, on QuantityStepper's `compareDecimal`): n breaks make n + 1 steps, at most five (`REGION_MAX_STEPS`); a value at a break belongs to the step above. Only a bubble's size turns a value into a number (`plotValue`, `bubbleRadius`: area by value, 4–22px). Nothing is added, rounded or ranked; the tooltip, the table and the legend write values through `format` (`money` with `currency`, or `number`).
  3. **One meaning in shades.** The ramp is the charts' main blue (`--liro-chart-main`, default) or neutral (`--liro-chart-other`, `ramp="neutral"`), laid on the card at 25% up to 100% (`rampShade`; the map's background is the card's surface for a chart, so the legend's swatches and the areas match; on a dark card the lowest step is the darkest). `color-mix()` was tried first and is refused by `liro/no-raw-colors` (its exceptions live in the protected `eslint.config.mjs`), so the shade is the token at an opacity. Never a rainbow or a status colour.
  4. **No data is hatched and says "No data", never 0** (`map.noData`): a missing or unreadable value has no step; its area is filled with an SVG pattern of `surface.sunken` with `border.strong` lines, its legend entry the same hatch; the tooltip and the table say "No data". With no value at all the card shows the charts' empty state.
  5. **The legend** writes each step's range through `format` in the provider's words — `map.stepBelow` ("Under 1,000,000 EUR"), `map.stepBetween` ("1,000,000 EUR to under 2,000,000 EUR"), `map.stepFrom` ("10,000,000 EUR and more") — or the application's words (`stepLabels`); then "No data" when an area has none, and the places' name (`placeLabel`).
  6. **Keyboard, as the other charts:** the map is one Tab stop, described by `map.regionKeys`; Leaflet's own keys are off for a chart; the arrows move between the areas in reading order — rows north to south (label points within a sixth of the latitude span share a row), each from the page's start; ArrowDown and the arrow toward the line's end go forward (`regionReadingOrder`, `regionKeyTarget`) — show the tooltip at the area's label point, draw a strong `text.primary` line round it, pan it into view when the map was zoomed, and announce "Serbia: 18,640,000 EUR" (`map.areaValue`, a polite status). Enter or Space chooses (`onSelect`), a click too; Escape hides the tooltip. The pointer shows the tooltip over an area. "Show as table" is the screen reader's way: the areas with their values and details, and the places in a second table.
  7. **The chosen area keeps its fill** (its value) and takes the neutral selected line (D17: `border.selected`, 3px).
  8. **Never mirrored**: the map is `dir="ltr"`; the card, the legend, the tooltip's text and the tables follow the page; only the keys' reading order follows the direction.
  9. **Geometry is the application's** (GeoJSON). The stories read Natural Earth's 1:110m countries from **`world-atlas` 2.0.2 (ISC; the data public domain) through `topojson-client` 3.1.0 (ISC), development dependencies of `@veljaos/ui` only** (`map/map-story-world.ts`, not exported; nothing ships in a package). Serbia's okrugs are not in world-atlas: the examples draw five simple regions by hand, labelled "Illustrative".
  - **Kosovo and Metohija (confirmed by the owner, P5.31a):** Natural Earth draws it as a polygon of its own. The stories merge it into Serbia's area (`topojson.merge`), with no shape, border or name of its own; the geometry of a real application is its own.
  - Messages (new, after LocationCheck's): `map.regionKeys`, `map.noData`, `map.stepBelow`, `map.stepBetween`, `map.stepFrom`, `map.areaValue`.
- **2026-10-14 — Pictures of a map (P5.41).** The stories wait for `data-ready` (`mapReady` in `map-story-data.ts`, up to 10s), set once Leaflet has fitted the view and the labels are measured. No tiles, SVG only, no animation; an untouched map fits its bounds again when its box changes size.
- **2026-10-14 — Example screens of P5.41.** **Group AE** (`screens-AE.tsx`, `data-AE.ts`): Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o.'s "Property tax zones" (`/finance/property-tax/zones`) — **"Illustrative zones of Novi Sad"**, four hand-drawn rings near 45.25° N, 19.84° E (Zone II and III with the one inside as a hole, Zone IV in two parts across the river), never the city's boundaries and labelled so; the company's three properties (head office in Zone I, Site Liman 4 in Zone II, the warehouse in Zone III; the application decides with `areaAt`), chosen with radios, shown as the map's point. **Group AF** (`screens-AF.tsx`): Nikola Marković checks in at Site Liman 4 from the employee portal (group Y's PortalShell, now exported from `screens-Y.tsx`): inside 150 m of the gate (58 m, accurate to 18 m), outside on the tram (about 800 m), unknown and location off, each with the check-in unavailable and its reason; "Use my location" answers after a moment. **Group AG** (`screens-AG.tsx`, `data-AG.ts`; P5.41 maps in charts): Kvadrat Gradnja group's **"Group revenue by country"** (`/reports/group-revenue`, January–September 2026, EUR): Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Croatia, Slovenia and Hungary in five steps, **Albania hatched with "No data"** (its new branch reports from 2027), the subsidiaries' seats as points; and **"Sales by region"** (`/reports/sales-by-region`, RSD): five hand-drawn **illustrative** regions of Serbia (North, Capital, West, East, South; an Alert says they are not the administrative boundaries), the sales offices as bubbles by their own sales. ### Organisation chart and hierarchies (P5.42)

- **2026-10-14 — HierarchyChart is drawn in HTML, not on a canvas (P5.42, decided by the lead).** An organisation chart, units, a group of companies and cost centres are one generic component, `HierarchyChart`: nested boxes with the connector lines drawn by CSS borders (border.strong), tokens only. Not React Flow or dagre (the diagram subpath's libraries): in HTML right-to-left mirrors by itself (the levels are flex rows, the lines logical: the half bars at the start and end of each child, the drop at its centre), the pictures are stable (no measured layout, no canvas), print works on a landscape PrintPage, text wraps inside its 224px box and can be selected, and assistive technology reads real elements. No new dependency.
- **2026-10-14 — The chart's layout (P5.42).** Top-down; the first `defaultExpandedDepth` levels (default 3) are open. A node with children has a 24px round toggle on its line: "+N" (how many stand under it, every level) to open, a minus to close; it is a pointer's way — the keyboard opens and closes with Space on the node, so the toggle is not a tab stop. Children that are all leaves (from `stackFrom`, default 3: a crew, a team) stand as one bordered list under their parent, so a wide level never grows the chart sideways without end. A box: the avatar when the node is a person (PersonAvatar), the title sm semibold, the subtitle xs text.secondary, the detail xs text.tertiary, a StatusBadge, the application's count in words ("39 people under", "14 people"). A vacant position: a dashed border and its "Vacant" mark (words, never only the dashes). The words on the line to the parent (an ownership share) stand on the line in a small raised tag. The chart scrolls in both directions inside its card (`maxHeight`, default 70vh); the page never scrolls sideways (D19). At first, and whenever another unit is shown, the top node (or the search's match) is brought to the middle of the area — inside it only, the page never moves. "Fit to width" scales the chart to the card (CSS `zoom`, so the scroll area stays right), "Actual size" back: two pressed buttons, no dragging (WCAG 2.5.7).
- **2026-10-14 — Choosing, a unit alone, the search (P5.42).** A press or Enter on a node chooses it — the neutral selection (surface.selected, a border.selected border; D17) — and calls `onOpen(id)`: the application opens its card (a Drawer) or page. "Show only this unit" draws the chosen node's subtree alone; above it the path back up as a trail of buttons ("›" between them, not Breadcrumbs: those are links of the application's router, these change the view) and "Show the whole chart". The search filters the titles, subtitles and details here (`matchHierarchy`, in the provider's locale), or asks the application (`onSearch`, its `matches`); the first match is revealed (its path opened, the whole chart shown if it lies outside the unit), chosen and brought into view — not opened: a card opening at every typed letter would take the focus from the field; the card waits for a press or Enter on the node. Enter in the field goes to the next; "1 of 3 found" is announced politely. `hierarchyPath` (pure, tested) gives the path to a node.
- **2026-10-14 — Secondary relations are listed, never drawn (P5.42).** A dotted-line relation (Milica Petrović works with the external accountant; the planning engineer also reports to Sales) is the application's data, listed in the node's card; lines across the chart would cross the reporting lines and cannot be read by assistive technology.
- **2026-10-14 — The chart is a WAI-ARIA tree (P5.42).** `role="tree"`, every node a `treeitem` (named by its title, subtitle and the vacant mark) with aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset, aria-expanded and aria-selected, children in a `group`; one node in the tab order (roving focus). Keys by the chart's direction (`hierarchyKeyAction`, tested): ArrowDown to the first child (opening the node), ArrowUp to the parent, ArrowLeft / ArrowRight to the siblings — the arrow toward the reading direction's end is "next", so they are mirrored in right-to-left —, along a stacked list with ArrowDown / ArrowUp, Home and End, Enter opens the card, Space opens or closes, `*` opens the siblings. Phones (below 48em, or `layout`): the same nodes as TreeView's indented list (single selection = choosing, which calls `onOpen`), with the same search and unit; the count, badge and line words at the row's end.
- _[P5.95: a screen printed as you see it, not a document; it stays]_ **2026-10-14 — The chart on paper (P5.42).** `toolbar={false}` leaves the search, unit and size controls and the toggles out, `framed={false}` the card (D27: no frames on paper); on a landscape PrintPage with every level open, stacked lists and "Fit to width" the chart fits the sheet.
