### Files and folders (P5.43)

- **2026-10-14 — FileBrowser: a company's files and folders are one template (P5.43).** Design system only: folders, files, owners, sizes, permissions, storage, versions, sharing, signing and retention are the application's, through props; the browser shows them, takes the files the user chooses and reports every action. It never sorts, filters, searches or adds up sizes (D4): the entries arrive in the order to show. **Desktop:** the folder's path as Breadcrumbs (every folder has an address, B.8), the location's name as the page's h1 (PageHeader); a start column (256px, "Hide folders" / "Show folders") with the quick places (Recent, Favourites, Shared with me, Trash: the application's, the current one neutral with the selected bar, D17), the folder tree (TreeView, one choice) and the storage used against the quota (the application's UsageMeter); one card with FilterBar (search at the start, "Type" and the application's filters, at the end Hide folders, List / Grid, Details, the application's own, New folder, Upload — the main one last), while searching "Search in: <folder> / Everywhere" (pressed chips, neutral), the uploads (AttachmentList with P5.5's states and progress per file, "2 of 5 uploaded", Clear), and the content: the list (DataTable: name with its icon, marks — shared, favourite, the application's badges — location and upload state; owner; modified; size or a folder's items through `format`; linked to, as links; the application's columns after them; sorted by the headers) or the grid (FileGrid). The details column (320px, FileDetails) at the end while open. **States:** loading (skeleton rows or tiles), the application's error with Try again, an empty folder ("This folder is empty", Upload), nothing found ("No files match", "Search everywhere"), no access (Lock, "You do not have access to this folder" with the application's reason and way on), offline (a neutral Alert; Upload and New folder unavailable with "Not available while offline.").
- **2026-10-14 — Upload: FileDropzone in a dialog, the card as the drop shortcut (P5.43).** "Upload" opens a dialog titled by the action with the folder bold under it (D22): FileDropzone (the accepted types and the size limit shown before choosing; "Take a photo" on phones, `camera`) and, on desktops, "Choose a folder" (a whole folder; each file keeps its path, `UploadedFile`, `withPaths`). Files dropped from the computer anywhere on the card upload too — the card takes the neutral selection and says "Drop the files to upload them to <folder>"; dropped folders are read through (`webkitGetAsEntry`) with their paths. Every file is checked again (`checkFiles`, P5.5) and the rejected ones are named under the toolbar in an always-present `role="alert"`. Progress per file is AttachmentList's (it already showed it): no new upload list.
- **2026-10-14 — Moving by drag has the menu's way (P5.43, WCAG 2.5.7).** A row or a tile dragged onto a folder — a folder row, a folder tile, a folder in the tree — is reported with `onMove(ids, folderId)`: the dragged item, or the whole selection when it is in it. The dragging rule ("Launchpad dragging is live"): pointer events, never HTML5 drag and drop; a mouse after 4px, a touch after a 250ms press; a neutral chip "Moving 3 items" / "Move into Permits" follows the pointer (shadow lg, border.strong, positioned from the inline start), the folder under it takes surface.selected with a 2px border.selected inset frame and is announced politely; never a moved folder, a folder inside one, or the folder they are in (`canDropInto`, `folderPath`); Escape cancels ("Move cancelled."), the click after a drag opens nothing. The keyboard's and the menu's way is the application's "Move to…" in each item's menu and on the selection: **FolderPickerDialog** (the action as title, what is moved as subject, a TreeView with one choice; the moved folders and their folders cannot be chosen and say why, `blockedFolders`, `pickerTree`; "Destination: Company documents / Site documentation / Permits" or why the button cannot be used — nothing chosen, already there — through UnavailableAction's `reasonId`). Phones have no drag.
- **2026-10-14 — FileGrid: thumbnails, checked neutrally (P5.43).** Tiles (radius lg, 12px padding) with a 4:3 picture (the application's thumbnail, decorative, or the family's 40px icon on surface.sunken), the name in two lines, the marks, the facts. A checked tile is surface.selected with a border.selected border (D17); the checkbox in the top start corner is the pointer's way (blue only when checked). One tab stop: arrows by the measured columns (`launchpadArrowTarget`, mirrored in right-to-left), Home / End, Space checks, Shift+arrows extend from the last tile checked (`selectRange`), Ctrl/Cmd+A checks all, Enter opens; Tab reaches the focused tile's menu (28px, "Actions: <name>"); Ctrl/Cmd+click and Shift+click.

Keep both is chosen at first (nothing is lost). With more waiting: "Conflict 1 of 3" and "Apply to all 3 conflicts" (`resolveConflicts`: a conflict that cannot be replaced keeps its own question). Each Continue reports its answers and the next question starts fresh.

FilePreview: a full-screen sheet on every width — the name as title, the application's line, "3 of 12", Previous / Next file (and ArrowLeft / ArrowRight by the reading direction outside the viewer), Download, the application's actions; the viewer is the application's (DocumentFrame for PDFs and office files, PageViewer for photos and scans — the paper is light and never mirrored, which suits a photo too); `unavailable` says "This file cannot be previewed" with Download. - **2026-10-14 — The phone-overflow test and a button that closes its own dialog (P5.43).** `apps/storybook/tests/phone-overflow.spec.ts` opens every button inside a dialog whose name ends in "…" and reads the dialog again; a button that closes its dialog (it leaves the page) made the test wait until its timeout. FileBrowser's phone sheet is therefore a WAI-ARIA menu (`role="menuitem"` entries, also the right semantics), not buttons. The test is a protected file and is left for the owner to change.
- **2026-10-15 — An action row that folded unfolds again (P5.31, the lead).** The first full CI run pictured the e-mail template's, the IOS portal's and the document review's actions folded into "…" in some modes and runs and not in others (39 pictures, the other modes passing), with room to spare. Traced in the pinned image: a full-page screenshot narrows the page to 1px for a moment; ActionGroup's row (OverflowRow, also BulkActionBar's) folded then, and where its parent sizes it by its content (PageHeader's actions, WorklistPage's bar) the row is as wide as what it shows, so it never saw its room again — as a user's row would stay folded after the window or a panel widened. The row now decides with every action laid out, before paint: on mount, when the actions change (by content: the same actions in a new array would close an open "More" menu), when their widths change (a font arrives) and when the nearest box whose width does not follow its content changes width (`placeOf`); its own resizes still fold it at once. Its "More" button stays mounted while every action is laid out to measure (hidden then, `display: contents` otherwise), and the row does not re-check while that menu is open or the focus is in it: a remounted button lost a press on its way (the overflow story's click as the web font arrived), and an open menu that widened the page would have closed. It also adds unrounded used widths (`getComputedStyle`, not the bounding box, which a dialog's opening zoom scales), with half a pixel's tolerance (`FIT_TOLERANCE`, tested in `actions.test.tsx`): `offsetWidth`'s rounded sum could exceed a content-sized row by a pixel. 32 of 32 screenshot runs kept the row whole, against 2 of 24 folded before.
- **2026-10-15 — AssistantPanel keeps the last question at the top until the reader scrolls (P5.34).** It placed the question once, on opening; a web font arriving afterwards changed the height of the turn above, and the right-to-left picture of "Long text" showed the conversation at another place in two runs of three. The question now stays at the top through any resize of the conversation until the reader scrolls (wheel, touch, keys, a press); an answer growing below it still moves nothing.
- **2026-10-15 — Gantt's mirrored scale labels stand on whole pixels (P5.37).** In right to left each month label was turned back about its own middle, at a fractional place, inside the scale's own compositing layer (the sticky head's `will-change`); its text was drawn a pixel apart from run to run. A label now fills its cell and is centred in it, so the two turns land on whole pixels.
- **2026-10-15 — An interaction story ends where nothing more happens (P5.31).** The till's "instant payment, buyer's code" story stopped while the example's bank was still to answer (a timer of 1.2 s); on a busy CI machine the answer arrived while axe measured the dialog, and the contrast of a button was read halfway through its change. The story now waits for the approval, and every example interaction settles again after its checks (`deskPlay`, `phonePlay`), so the accessibility check measures a page at rest.

### The owner's decisions after P5.31–P5.43 (P5.31a, 2026-10-15)

- **2026-10-15 — Maps follow the law of the Republic of Serbia (P5.31a, the owner).** Kosovo and Metohija is part of the Republic of Serbia, and the design system's stories and examples follow Serbian law: every map draws it within Serbia's area, with no shape, border or name of its own (`map-story-world.ts` merges Natural Earth's separate polygon into Serbia). `map-story-world.test.ts` fails if a change draws it apart: Priština, Prizren, Peć, Kosovska Mitrovica and Gnjilane must lie within Serbia and within no other country, and no country key names it; checked against Serbia's polygon alone, which leaves Priština out. AGENTS.md rule D31.
- **2026-10-15 — IPS QR against the NBS validator (P5.31a, the owner).** The owner asked for every IPS code to be checked with the National Bank of Serbia's validator. `ips.nbs.rs` is refused by the environment's network policy (the proxy answers 403); the check runs once the owner allows the domain. Until then the rules remain those of P5.40 (two public implementations, checked against a known valid code). Done in P5.31b: every code accepted.
- **2026-10-15 — The phone test no longer waits on a trigger whose dialog closed (P5.31a, the owner).** `phone-overflow.spec.ts` lists a dialog's triggers, then opens them one by one; a trigger that closed its own dialog while another stayed open (one that cannot be dismissed while it works) left the rest of the list off the page, and reading the next one's name (`locator.evaluate`, no timeout) waited until the test's 120 seconds. Reproduced with a throwaway story (a dialog of "…" buttons, each closing it and opening a dialog that stays): the old test timed out in both directions, the new one passes in under 4 seconds. A trigger no longer on the page is now skipped at once (its name "(gone)", read with a 1-second limit), and a dialog's pass ends when that dialog has closed. Locally 365 phone tests passed with it (none failed) before one machine's 25-minute limit; CI runs all of them in its parts. FileBrowser's phone sheet stays a WAI-ARIA menu (P5.43): the right semantics either way.
- **2026-10-15 — Map labels are measured again when the fonts arrive (P5.31a).** CI pictured "Group revenue by country" with 425 pixels different in light, left to right and right to left, on a commit that does not change maps; locally the same pictures passed 12 times of 12. The map decides which names fit inside their areas by measuring each label once, when the labels are placed: a web font that arrived after that measurement changed every label's width, and the decision stayed the old one. The class is the one FloorPlan fixed in P5.28 ("labels measured and never cut"): MapCanvas, under AreaMap, LocationCheck and RegionChart, now measures again on `document.fonts.ready` and on every `loadingdone`, and reports itself ready (`data-ready`, which the stories wait for) only once the fonts are settled. Every map picture then passed three times of three in the pinned image, the failing two and Property tax zones five times of five.
- **2026-10-15 — IPS QR codes checked with the NBS validator (P5.31b, the owner).** With `ips.nbs.rs` allowed, every IPS text the stories and examples show went to the National Bank of Serbia's validation API (`https://nbs.rs/QRcode/api/qr/v1/validate`, the method of its "Smernice Generator / Validator"); its own example answered "OK." first. All eleven answered "OK.": the bills (PR) of QrCode, PrintDocument, the invoice printout (data-J) and payment orders forms 1 and 3, and the tills' instant payments (PT) of QrCode, PaymentDialog, the bakery's till and both cafés' tabs; so did the three codes of `ips-qr.test.ts`. Not checked there: the buyer's code (PK) the till scans, which the validator does not take ("Uneta identifikacija IPS QR kôda nije podržana."; the guide names PR, PT and EK) and which the buyer's bank writes, not the design system; and the UTF-8 sample of `qr-code.test.tsx`, which tests the QR encoder with a dash outside the IPS characters on purpose. `ips-qr.test.ts` now holds three accepted texts exactly (a bill with a payer and model 97, form 1 with names on two lines, a till's PT), so a change to `ipsQrText` that writes them differently fails until it is checked there again. A scan with a banking application stays a good last check.

  (comparison, grey) against actual (main). TreeTable has no "open a row" event: the drill-down
  is its single selection (neutral) and "Show entries of <code>" in the card's header — an
  UnavailableAction "Choose a line first." while none is chosen. The entries page shows the line's
  figures and its latest entries from the books (a document links to its page where the examples
  have one — a depreciation to the asset card, group AP), the totals row the line's actual with
  the application's count ("Actual, 236 entries") and `rowLimitMessage` "The latest 3 of 236
  entries."
- **2026-10-15 — Loans and leases: a list and a record with its schedule (P5.60).** ListPage
  (lender, kind, principal, rate, term, outstanding, the next instalment with its date, the state
  in words: Active, Overdue, Repaid; views Active / Repaid / All) and DetailPage with KeyFigures
  (principal, rate, term, outstanding — danger when overdue), the contract (what it financed links
  to the asset card), an AreaChart of the outstanding principal after each instalment, and the
  repayment schedule as a DataTable (no., due date, instalment, principal, interest, balance
  after, Paid / Due / Overdue / Upcoming in words) with the totals from data. An overdue lease says
  so in a danger Alert above its contract.
- **2026-10-15 — Service and author contracts: the calculation is the application's answer
  (P5.61).** The new contract is a RecordFormPage (person, kind as radios with what each is for,
  work, period, project; the amount agreed as gross or net, the amount, the normed costs' share
  the application offers for the kind — read-only when there is one); the Calculation section is
  DocumentTotals (gross, normed costs, tax base, tax, pension and disability insurance, health
  insurance; the final row "Net to <person>"), every figure from the application for the inputs
  given. For an amount the application has not calculated the figures read "—" with a neutral
  Alert "Calculated when the draft is saved" — the screen never computes a tax. The monthly run
  of such contracts is PeriodicRunPage (checks in words — a payment held for a missing bank
  account —, KeyFigures and every contract's calculation with totals, Post and pay).

### Purchasing and sales chains, price lists, offsets (P5.49, P5.50, P5.54, P5.55)

- **2026-10-15 — The purchasing chain is three pages and one match (P5.49).** Purchase order
  NB-2026-0087 and goods receipt PRI-2026-0213 are DocumentPages; the receipt is "Based on" the
  order (DocumentReferences) and shows each line received against ordered in the Original /
  Change / New pattern — `correctionColumns` with the headers Ordered / Difference / Received —
  with the receiver's reason in its own column; the received value and the difference against
  the order are the application's figures (key figures and totals). The three-way match is a
  DetailPage of the supplier invoice ("Match 2026-1187") built on ValueComparison with three
  sources (order, receipt, invoice): one row per quantity, price and total, the application's
  verdict in words ("Invoiced as received", "More than ordered: needs approval"), "1 of 8
  differ". The invoice itself is still reviewed and posted in the document inbox (P5.31): the
  match and the inbox link to each other through the chain (RelatedDocuments on every page). The
  match's actions: Open in the document inbox, Ask for a credit note (neutral), Accept the
  difference (the main one, last); once accepted, "Post in the document inbox".
- **2026-10-15 — The next document of a sales chain is the page's main action, in one click
  (P5.50).** Quote → order → delivery note → invoice, each a DocumentPage "Based on" the one
  before it. The next document is a SplitAction (`intent="create"`: "Create order", "Create
  delivery note", "Create invoice"), its menu the other documents the application can make from
  this one (a proforma, an advance invoice, one invoice for several delivery notes); one click
  and the application creates it — its page opens. On a phone the SplitAction is in the bottom
  bar. The chain so far is the Related documents panel of every page, in the chain's order; a
  document with nothing after or before it yet (a new quote) has no panel. Once the next
  document exists the create action is gone (the document is in the panel instead).
- **2026-10-15 — Price lists, promotions and discount rules are lists of data (P5.54).** Price
  lists on ListPage (who each applies to — a customer group or the own shop —, with or without
  VAT, valid from / until, items, state); one price list on DetailPage with three flush tables:
  its prices (with the previous price where it changed), the customers' own prices on it, and
  the group's customers. Promotions on ListPage with views Active / Scheduled / Ended / All: the
  rule is the application's sentence ("Buy 2, get 1 free"), never composed by the library. The
  discount rules in the application's order, On / Off from their row menu, how they combine as
  the application's sentence under the table (`rowLimitMessage`). The states (Active, Scheduled,
  Ended) are the application's words: no date is compared on the screen.
- **2026-10-15 — Compensation, cession and assignment are one document pattern (P5.55).** One
  DocumentPage for all three kinds: the other parties with their roles at the counterparty's
  level ("Partner"; "Assignee" and "Debtor"; "Paying party" and "Receiving party" — the new
  `counterparties` prop), what the document does in one sentence (`details`), "Based on" the
  confirmed statement of open items for a compensation; the items of both sides in ONE table — a
  heading row per side ("Beton Mix d.o.o. owes Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o."), each item with Open /
  the settled column (Offset, Assigned, Paid on instruction) / Remains, a subtotal row per side
  (DataTable line types) —, the amount settled in the totals; "What remains" as the
  application's sentences; "Signatures": SignerList with `sequential={false}` (each party signs
  in any order; a cession's debtor acknowledges). Send reminder while signatures are missing,
  Post once all have signed.

### Stock and production (P5.51–P5.53, P5.57)

- **2026-10-15 — The item card and transfers are assembled, not new (P5.51).** The item card is a
  DetailPage: four key figures (on hand, available, stock value, average cost), "Balance by
  warehouse" (DataTable: on hand, reserved, available, average cost, value, and the application's
  totals of both warehouses; pressing a warehouse shows its movements), "Movements" (DataTable:
  date, the document as a link, the partner or purpose, in, out, the running balance, the signed
  value and the running value; the opening balance as the first row; the period's totals in the
  totals row; a SelectField with a hidden label chooses the warehouse) and "Details". Every
  balance, value and average is the application's; nothing is added on the screen. Every
  movement's document opens (drill-down): the transfers their own page, a goods receipt, a
  delivery note and an issue a small read-only stock document (DocumentPage). A transfer is a
  DocumentPage with Draft → In transit → Received in the application's words; while it is a draft,
  its lines are an EditableGrid whose "Available" column is what the source warehouse can give,
  from the application, and the application's check says under a line when it asks for more
  ("Only 3 roll available in Central warehouse.") — Send is an UnavailableAction with the reason
  until every line passes. Received transfers show Sent and Received.
- **2026-10-15 — Production on TreeTable, the correction columns and Gantt (P5.52).** A bill of
  materials is TreeTable inside a DetailPage: the components with their quantity and unit (one
  cell, the phone's main figure), kind and cost for a batch; a semi-finished good (the rye
  sourdough starter) is a branch whose children are its own bill, open at first, and its bill is a
  page of its own linked from the section's description. The work order's material is the
  Original / Change / New pattern with the headers Planned / Difference / Used and each
  difference's value; its output (good, scrap with the reasons) a second table, so the lines'
  card carries a title ("Material"). The production plan is Gantt: each production line or oven a
  phase, each work order a task with its shift as "who", a delivery a milestone, the starter before
  the bread a dependency, "now" from the application. Moving an order is reported and applied by
  the example as group AA does (`applyPlanChange`).
- **2026-10-15 — The retail price calculation: one editable column (P5.53).** The kalkulacija's
  lines are an EditableGrid whose only editable cell is the retail price (with VAT), the shop's
  choice; purchase price, dependent costs, cost price, margin % and amount, price without VAT,
  VAT rate and amount and the line's retail value are `display` columns — the application's
  answer. Prices per piece are written with two decimals and the currency named once in the
  header ("Currency: RSD"), so thirteen columns fit; values are in DocumentTotals (purchase value,
  dependent costs, cost value, margin, value without VAT, VAT, retail value) with the VAT by rate
  as its `recap`. A margin below cost is the application's warning under the line. The price
  change it causes on the shelf is the Original / Change / New pattern (Old price / Change / New
  price) with the value of each change, on the calculation and as its own document
  (NIV-2026-0012). In the example the application's calculation is played in whole paras in
  `data-BA.ts` (VAT out of the retail price, half up to the para; margin % of the cost price,
  half up to two decimals), as data-I plays the till; the stated figures are checked in
  `dataset-checks.ts`.
- **2026-10-15 — Stocktaking lists (P5.57).** The list is a DocumentPage: per line the location,
  the item with the commission's note, Book / Difference / Counted (`correctionColumns`), the
  average cost and the difference's value; key figures and DocumentTotals (book value, counted
  value, surplus, shortage, net difference) from the application; the commission's signatures
  as SignerList (in order; the current member's Sign); "Post differences" an UnavailableAction
  with "2 of 3 signed" until all have signed, then a ConfirmDialog titled by the action with the
  list as its subject and what will be posted as its preview. Posting is the application's (it
  writes the surplus and shortage documents). The count itself is group I's handheld (StockCount
  in `Handheld`), counting **blind**: the books' quantities and differences are not passed
  while the commission counts.
- **2026-10-15 — Example screens of P5.51, P5.52, P5.53, P5.57 (groups AY, AZ, BA, BB).**

## Users, HR, documents and governance (P5.62–P5.71)

### My profile and the sign-in flows (P5.62, P5.63)

- **2026-10-16 — My profile is a SettingsPage with three tabs (P5.62).** Preferences (name and
  e-mail read-only — the administrator changes them —, the interface language and the theme: the
  provider's choices as the Core offers them, saved at once with "Saved"), Sign-in and security
  (password, two-factor sign-in, passkeys) and Devices (an e-mail about a new device as a row,
  SessionList as the section's block). Each tab has its own address (`/profile`,
  `/profile/security`, `/profile/devices`); the user menu's "Profile" opens it. Dialogs stand at
  page level, outside the tabs (D16).
- **2026-10-16 — Turning on two-factor sign-in is one Dialog in two steps (P5.62).** "1. Add Liro
  to your authenticator app": QrCode of the Core's `otpauth://` text (176px, dark on light in both
  themes), "Cannot scan it? Type this key in the app:" and the same secret as text (monospace, left
  to right, grouped by four, selectable); on a phone also "Open in the authenticator app on this
  phone" (the otpauth link), since a phone cannot scan its own screen. "2. Enter the code the app
  shows": CodeInput; a wrong code is the Core's sentence under the boxes. Then "Save your
  recovery codes": RecoveryCodes in the same dialog, not dismissible until "I have saved these
  codes" and Continue. While on, the row reads "On since … · 8 of 10 recovery codes left" (the
  Core counts) with a success "On" badge, "New recovery codes" (the same RecoveryCodes) and "Turn
  off" (ConfirmDialog, destructive: "Your recovery codes stop working.").
- **2026-10-16 — Passkeys are rows; adding is the Core's browser step (P5.62).** Each passkey is a
  setting row (its name; "Added … · Last used …" or "Not used yet"; Remove → DeleteConfirmDialog
  titled "Remove passkey" with the passkey as `subject`, D22). The last row is "Add a passkey":
  the Core runs the browser's WebAuthn step; a failure is the row's error in the Core's words
  (`state: 'error'`, announced); a success opens "Passkey added" to name it (the Core's suggestion
  from the device filled in).
- **2026-10-16 — The sign-in flows continue the sign-in screen (P5.63).** The e-mail screen of P4.8
  (`SignIn`) now goes on to the password step (who is signing in, with Change; the password;
  "Forgot your password?"), then the two-factor code (CodeInput, "Do not ask for a code on this
  device for 30 days", "Use a recovery code" → a TextField left to right), then the home page.
  The Walk-through types the password and a code. The main button of each card is full width as
  EmailFirstForm's Continue (the form column stretches it); secondary ways are a centred line of
  links under the form.
- **2026-10-16 — Forgot password says the same for every address (P5.63).** EmailFirstForm with
  "Send the link", then "Check your e-mail": "If an account uses …, a link … is on its way" and
  the link's validity in the Core's words — the page never tells whether an account exists.
  "Choose a new password": two PasswordFields (`new-password`), the company's rules as the first
  field's description, a broken rule as the Core's sentence on the first field, a mismatch on the
  second; an expired link is a warning Alert with "Send a new link" (neutral, D23).
- **2026-10-16 — Invitation, locked account, expired session (P5.63).** The invitation names the
  company (with PIB and city), who invited (with their position) and the role with what it
  allows, the e-mail fixed (read-only), the name, a password twice — or Microsoft / Google with
  the same address (ProviderSignInButtons, "or" above); an expired invitation says who can send a
  new one. A locked account is a warning Alert with until when (the Core's instant through
  `format.time`) and the way in that does not wait: "Choose a new password" (primary). An expired
  session knows the account: the account line with "Not you?", only the password, "Sign in and
  return" back to the page (F-2026-0412); the device is trusted for the code. StatusPage's 401
  stays for a page opened with no session to resume.

### Recruitment, onboarding and CRM (P5.64, P5.65, P5.67)

- **2026-10-16 — Recruitment is assembled from the library (P5.64).** The openings are a ListPage
  (views Open / Filled / All); a job posting is a DetailPage read and edited as a whole (P4.9:
  Edit turns the same sections into fields, Cancel / Save in the bottom bar); the candidates are a
  KanbanBoard with the stages Applied → Interview → Offer → Hired / Rejected. A move is only
  reported and the application decides (D24's spirit for people's applications): Rejected asks
  why first (ReasonConfirmDialog with the company's reasons), Hired is refused until an offer is
  accepted and a toast says why, every other move is applied. A candidate is a DetailPage — the
  application, the CV and documents (AttachmentList), the interviews (DataTable), the scorecards
  side by side (a DataTable of criteria × interviewers, "—" for a scorecard not submitted) and the
  history (HistoryList) as sections, no side column (P4.9). **Scorecards are RadioGroupFields**
  on the posting's criteria and the company's scale (both data) inside a RecordFormPage, with the
  recommendation and notes; sending checks every criterion and says so under the group. Not
  SatisfactionRating: it is one question with its own Send and thanks, and a scorecard is four or
  more questions sent once. Not Questionnaire: it walks one question at a time with branching,
  and an interviewer reads and changes the whole card at once. **Interview scheduling is a Dialog
  with SlotPicker** — the candidate as its subject (D22), the format, the slots when every
  interviewer is free (the application computes the overlap), the invitation an explicit
  checkbox. CalendarView was not needed: showing everyone's week would leave the user to find the
  overlap the application already knows.
- **2026-10-16 — Onboarding: a DataTable for HR, SetupChecklist for the new employee (P5.65).**
  HR's checklist is a DetailPage with one flush section per kind of task (equipment, accounts,
  training, documents to sign), each a DataTable: the task (a done task's note, a blocked task's
  reason), its owner (PersonName), its due date (DueDate: overdue in words; a done task its
  plain date) and its state (StatusBadge), a row menu to mark it done or remind its owner; key
  figures count done, overdue and waiting. **SetupChecklist was not given owner and due-date
  props:** onboarding tasks run side by side, each owned by someone else, and HR scans them by
  owner, date and state — a table's job — while SetupChecklist is one person's steps in order
  with one step to do now and a single progress. It is exactly that on the new employee's side
  (PortalShell, phone first): "Before you start" with her own steps, the next highlighted, the
  date in the step's description, the training blocked until her first day with the reason. Her
  documents are signed on SigningPage with SignerList (the director signed first); her salary
  account is a Dialog checked as the application checks it (MOD 97, `ipsAccountValid`). What she
  does reaches HR's checklist (the examples keep the tasks above the screens).
- **2026-10-16 — CRM: the pipeline on KanbanBoard, the contact's timeline on HistoryList (P5.67).**
  Leads → opportunities → quotes → won / lost, each card a deal: the customer, the owner
  (assignee), the next activity (DueDate), the value in the card's `meta` ("Value 549.120,00 RSD",
  the application's figure through `format.money`) and its quote as the card's `record` link into
  the sales chain (group AV, `/sales/quotes/…`). Column counts are counts of deals only: a column
  sum is a computed figure, the application's, and KanbanColumn's `count` already carries it
  ("3 deals · 1.579.920,00 RSD") when the application sends it — the examples do not add amounts.
  The application's rules: Lost asks why (ReasonConfirmDialog), Won asks first (ConfirmDialog) and
  only for a deal whose quote is accepted or ordered, Quotes only for a deal with a quote; a
  refused move says why in a toast. A deal and a contact are DetailPages; the deal's quote is a
  RelatedDocuments link to PON-2026-0031, its history a HistoryList of stage and value changes;
  the contact's timeline is a HistoryList of calls, meetings, e-mails and documents, and "Log
  activity" is an end Drawer (D14: a short edit with the page in view). Activities are a ListPage
  (My planned / Overdue / Done / All) and the same activities on CalendarView (week; agenda on
  phones; the application's `now`), switched by a "Show as calendar" / "Show as list" button.

### Documents from definitions, the registry, the archive, meetings and contracts (P5.66, P5.68–P5.71)

- **2026-10-16 — DefinedForm: a form drawn from the application's field definitions (P5.66).**
  The documents of P5.66 (and the report to an authority of P5.87) are made from templates whose
  fields the application keeps as JSON. `DefinedForm` draws such definitions with the library's
  own parts, so a generated form looks and works as a hand-written one: `sections` of `fields`,
  each section a FormSection card (title, description, 1–3 columns by its own width, one on
  phones, `collapsible`); each field one of the library's fields by its `type` — text, textarea,
  email, number, money, date, select, multiselect, radio, checkbox, switch — or `custom`, drawn by
  the application (`renderCustom`: a document's lines, a lookup). **Conditions are data:**
  `visibleWhen` (fields and sections) and `requiredWhen` (fields) with `equals`, `notEquals`,
  `oneOf`, `filled`, combined by `all`, `any`, `not`; a multiple choice equals a value when that
  value is chosen; numbers, amounts and dates compare as the strings they are, never as numbers
  (D4). Conditions are read in the definitions' order and **a hidden field counts as empty** (an
  old value of a hidden field never shows anything); a value that is no field (the document's
  kind, the body of a meeting) is a context value the application adds, read as given — one
  commercial definition serves the proforma, the invoice and the advance invoice abroad. **Hidden
  values are kept but not submitted**, as in Questionnaire. **Required** fields carry the mark;
  what is missing is said in words under the field — "Fill in this field.", "Choose an option.",
  "Tick this to go on." — once `showMissing` is set or after the handle's `check()`, which also
  focuses the first problem (opening a folded section) and returns `{ valid, missing,
unreadable, values }` (the values to submit; an unreadable number or date blocks it too). A
  read-only or disabled field is never missing. The application's own checks come back as
  `errors` by field id, before the missing words. `readOnly` shows a numbered or sent document's
  data as text; `lang` marks definitions written in another language (labels, hints, section
  titles and radio options carry it; select options are plain strings). The pure rules are
  exported (`definedFormState`, `definedConditionHolds`, `definedFieldRequired`,
  `definedValueFilled`, …) and `definedFormProblems` lets the application test its definitions
  (an id used twice, a choice without options, a condition on a later or unknown field). Not for
  a form designed once for one screen (FormSection and the fields) nor for questions asked one at
  a time (Questionnaire).
- **2026-10-16 — A document from a JSON definition: the form is ours, the document is the
  application's (P5.66).** "New document" lists the application's types by group (CategoryGrid in
  section cards: decisions and conclusions, letters, commercial documents outside SEF, internal
  acts and records, company bodies). A draft is a RecordFormPage: DefinedForm on the start side,
  the preview on the end side from 80em (under the form on phones) — DocumentFrame showing what
  the application's renderer returns: loading (the page skeleton), ready, failed (the renderer's
  words and "Try again"). The preview is not redrawn on every keystroke: after a change a
  neutral Alert says "The preview shows the values before your last change." and "Update
  preview" checks the form first (the missing values said, the focus on the first). "Assign
  number" checks, asks (ConfirmDialog with the document as `subject`: "entered in the registry
  book as outgoing act 01-412/2026 … can no longer be changed"), then the document is
  **Numbered**: the form read-only, an info Alert that a change is a new document, "Send for
  signature" the main action. Signing is SigningPage (the preview first, SignerList in order:
  the director, then the employee confirming receipt; the registry entry as a section).
- **2026-10-16 — The registry book is RegisterPage (P5.68).** One entry per act: the number from
  the book, the date entered, the kind in words with an arrow (Incoming, Outgoing, Internal; the
  arrow mirrors in right to left), the sender or recipient, the subject with the act's own number
  and date, the assignee, the due date as DueDate ("2 days overdue" in words; settled when done),
  the state in the application's words, and the linked document (a draft reply, the numbered
  decision of P5.66) with the count of files. A wrong entry is corrected by a new one that refers
  to it ("Corrects no. 409" / "Corrected by no. 411"), never deleted. The year is the first row's
  select (2025 lives in the archive); "Show" filters by kind or "Not done". An entry is a
  DetailPage: the act, the linked documents (RelatedDocuments), the files (AttachmentList) and the
  history (ActivityList); Reassign, Reply (a letter of P5.66), "Mark as done" last. A new entry is
  a RecordFormPage: Incoming / Outgoing / Internal (an outgoing document numbered in Documents is
  entered by itself), the party, their or our number, the subject (required, said in words), the
  classification of the archive's plan, the assignee and the due date, the scanned act with
  FileDropzone (`camera` on phones); the number is the book's, given on saving.

## Analytics and automation (P5.77–P5.81)

- **2026-10-16 — The pivot library: evaluated, built on TanStack Table (P5.77, owner: "an MIT library if a maintained, accessible, themeable one exists, otherwise built on TanStack Table; the evaluation recorded").** Checked in the npm registry on 2026-10-16 (`npm view <pkg> version and theming are judged from each package's documentation, its dependencies and its known architecture; none was installed.
- **2026-10-16 — `@veljaos/ui/pivot`, a subpath of its own (P5.77).** As `charts`, `gantt` and `map`: a tsup entry `pivot`, `exports["./pivot"]` in `packages/ui/package.json`, a consumer-check example (`apps/consumer-check/src/PivotExample.tsx`) rendered from the packed tarball. TanStack Table is also used by the main entry (DataTable), so the subpath keeps only the pivot's own code (grid, chooser, logic) out of `dist/index.js`.
- **2026-10-16 — Pivot: the application computes, the library lays out (P5.77).** `Pivot` takes `fields` (dimensions and measures with the application's aggregations, a dimension's values for filtering), `value` (the layout: rows, columns, values with their aggregation, filters with their kept values) and `onChange`, and `result` (the application's column tree, row tree and grand total; every cell a decimal string by leaf column key, null "—"). It never adds, averages or counts. **Subtotals are the group's own row** (compact form: a group row carries its figures, semibold, and its members under it), so no separate subtotal rows; total columns (`total`) and the grand total row are semibold on `surface.sunken`, the grand total under a 1px `border.strong` line in a `tfoot`, as DataTable's totals. A column (or a group above it) sets how its figures are written (`kind` 'number' | 'money' | 'percent', `currency`, `decimals`) through the provider's `format`; tabular, end-aligned. `loading`: skeleton rows the first time, then "Updating…" at the toolbar's end with the old figures kept (`aria-busy`), never a translucent overlay. States: no value chosen ("Choose a value", with "Choose fields"), `error` with Try again (`onRetry`), no figures for the layout. A filter with no value chosen keeps every value; a measure stands in Values once (its aggregation changes in place).
- **2026-10-16 — The field chooser: buttons and menus, no dragging (P5.77, WCAG 2.5.7).** Filters, Columns, Rows and Values (a spreadsheet field list's order), each an h3 and a list, then "Available fields". A used field has a 28px "Options: <field>" menu: Move up, Move down, Move to <each other area it may stand in>, Remove; a value has its aggregation as a SelectField (one aggregation is plain text), a filter its kept values as a MultiSelectField in summary mode ("All values" while none is chosen). An unused field is added by "Add <field> to <area>" when it fits one area, else by an "Add <field>" menu of the areas. **No dragging at all**: the owner made dragging optional; every change takes one or two presses, and a drag would only duplicate the menus. Every change is reported at once (`onChange`); there is no "Apply" — the application shows `loading` while it computes. On wider screens the chooser is a 288px start column beside the grid, shown and hidden by "Fields" (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`; open by default); on phones it is a full-screen sheet (the Drawer at the phone's width) with "Done", closed by default. Without `onChange` the layout is fixed and there is no chooser.
- **2026-10-16 — The pivot grid: a treegrid around a layout table (P5.77).** A WAI-ARIA treegrid, one cell in the tab order: arrows cell by cell (ArrowRight towards the end, so mirrored in right to left), Home / End (with Ctrl or Cmd the grid's first / last cell), Page Up / Down by ten rows (`pivotKeyTarget`, tested); Enter or Space on a group's row header opens or closes it (the row carries `aria-level` and `aria-expanded`), on a figure reports it (`onDrillDown` with the row and column keys and their labels from the top, `PivotCellRef`); a press does the same. A figure that opens is underlined (dotted) on hover, never link-blue (D17: the grid would be all blue). **Markup:** the treegrid is a `div` (the scroll region) around a `<table role="presentation">` whose rows and cells carry `row`, `columnheader` (with `aria-colspan` / `aria-rowspan`), `rowheader` and `gridcell`: the native `colspan` / `rowspan` draw the multi-row header, and jsx-a11y's strict config forbids an interactive role on `<table>` itself (no new lint exception). The hint ("Move between the figures with the arrow keys…") describes the grid. **Sticky (D21):** the `thead` carries `STICKY_HEAD` and `data-sticky-head` (the header rows move as one below the shell, `useStickyHead` on the region), the row headers `STICKY_START` on an opaque surface (`surface.raised`, the grand total's `surface.sunken`), the corner both and `data-sticky-start`, the region `STICKY_CLEARANCE`. The corner names the column fields (tertiary) over the row fields ("Region / Product line"). Groups: the first level open by default (`defaultExpanded`, or controlled `expanded` / `onExpandedChange`), "Expand all" / "Collapse all" in the toolbar. **Phones:** the same grid, read in place — it scrolls sideways inside its card with the first column at the start (min 9rem), the page never does (D19); figures still open their records.
- **2026-10-16 — Export and drill-down are reported (P5.77).** `exportAction: { formats, application's formats; shown only when a value is chosen; the application makes the file (as a job, a toast). `onDrillDown(cell)`: the application opens the records — the examples use an end Drawer titled by what it lists, the figure as its bold `subject` ("Liman 4 · 5120 Material · Sep 2026 · Amount", D22), with a DataTable (cards on phones) of the latest ten and the application's count.
- **2026-10-16 — Pivot examples (P5.77, group BR).** Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o.'s **cost analysis** (Analytics → Cost analysis): sites and their cost accounts (5120 Material, 5130 Machinery and fuel, 5330 Subcontractors; illustrative chart) down, July–September across with the amount and the number of supplier invoices under each month, the totals; the saved view "By supplier" (Beton Mix d.o.o., Elektro Sistem d.o.o. and two invented suppliers). Pekara Zlatni klas's **sales analysis** (Sales → Sales analysis, Jovana Marković): its categories and products (the till's, group I) down, months across with revenue and pieces; the saved view "By product and shop" (its own shop and group AX's customer group Shops). A "Saved view" select in the pivot's toolbar ("Custom layout" when none matches). The figures were computed once outside the examples (as the application's) and written out in `data-BR.ts`; the screens look a layout's result up (`resultFor`) and filter the records behind a figure by the figure's members (`membersOf`) — they never add. This illustrative application has figures for the saved views only; any other layout shows "No figures for this layout" (said in the page's subtitle).
- **2026-10-16 — RuleBuilder: "When / If / Then" from the application's data (P5.78).** A new component (`components/rule-builder.tsx`, pure logic in `rule-builder-logic.ts`), because the library had nothing that builds a condition list: FilterBar filters one list and reports values, Diagram draws a process of steps, SettingsPage switches one setting. Three blocks, each a group named by its heading (h3 by default, `headingLevel`): **When** (one SelectField of the application's triggers, grouped), **If** (conditions joined by "All of these" / "Any of these" — the join chosen once there are two; a **group** is a sunken box with its own join, one level deep), **Then** (the actions in order, each a SelectField of the application's action kinds and its parameters' fields). A condition is a field, a test (operator) and a value; the value's field follows the field's kind (`text`, `number` → NumberField, `money` → MoneyField with the field's currency, `date` → DateField, `choice` → SelectField, searched from 11 options; parameters may also be `longText` → TextAreaField); a test with `noValue` ("is empty") takes none; the test is unavailable, with "Choose a field first.", until a field is chosen. Values are strings (decimal strings, YYYY-MM-DD, an option's value), `null` while not given. **Everything is data:** the triggers, the fields of the chosen trigger (the application passes them), the tests each field allows, the actions and their parameters. The builder reports the edited rule (`onChange`, a `RuleDraft`) and never evaluates or checks it: the application's problems come back as `problems` keyed `'trigger'`, `'conditions'`, `'actions'` or `ruleProblemKey(id, part)` ("c2.value", "a1.who") and stand under their fields (block problems under the block). The rule **in words** is the application's (`summary`): above the blocks on surface.sunken under "In words", `role="status"` (announced politely as it changes). **Keyboard, no dragging:** every item names itself ("Condition 2", "Group 1", "Group 1, condition 2", "Action 1") on its own line with its tools at the end — Move up, Move down (only where it can move) and Remove, 28px CompactIconButtons named "Move up: Condition 2". The focus follows each edit once the application passes the new rule back: a new item's first field; the moved item's button (the other one when it reached an end, `moveFocusTarget`); after a removal the item that takes its place, else the one before, else the list's Add button (`focusAfterRemove`). Removing a group's last condition removes the group. New ids from the draft (`nextRuleId`: "c4", "g2", "a3"). Changing a condition's field keeps its test only where the new field allows it and its value only for the same kind (and currency, and an offered choice); changing an action's kind empties its parameters. **Read-only** (`readOnly`, or no `onChange`) and **disabled** (`disabledReason`, shown above) show the same blocks as text, the values through the provider's `format` (`ruleValueText`; "—" when not given). Loading: three skeleton blocks. Phones (`layout`, default below 48em): every field on its own line; on a desktop a condition's three fields share a row from a 42rem container. Join words between items ("and" / "or") are text, not colour.
- **2026-10-16 — ValueComparison chooses the values to keep (P5.79).** Merging two records needs the records side by side and a choice per differing field: ValueComparison already is that table (and on phones one card per field, each value labelled with its source), so it takes two optional props instead of a new component: `chosen` (row id → the index of the source whose value is kept) and `onChoose(rowId, index)`. With `onChoose`, each differing row's values are **native radio buttons** (one group per row through `name`, so Tab enters the row once and the arrows move the choice; a table row cannot be a Radix radio group), drawn as the system's radio (20px, brand.solid with a dot, the focus ring), the whole cell the target; the kept value is the neutral selection (D17: surface.selected with the 3px border.selected bar, only the radio blue). A row still to choose stays on status.warning.bg with "Choose the value to keep" (icon and words); a chosen one says "Chosen" (or the application's `note`). The count reads "4 of 5 chosen" (`chosenCounts`). Rows the application does not mark as differing are not choices ("Same", or its note: "Both accounts are kept"). With `chosen` and no `onChoose` the choice is shown, not changed (a check before the kept value, "Chosen" for assistive technology) — the merge's confirmation and summary. On phones each differing field's values are a `radiogroup` of boxes (source above value), one per line. The application decides which record stays, what it preselects, whether the choice is complete and what the merge moves.
- **2026-10-16 — Automation rules are a list, a record and a log (P5.78).** Settings → Automation of Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o. (group BS, `screens-BS.tsx`, `data-BS.ts`): **Automation rules** (ListPage; views All / On / Off / Last run failed): the rule's name with the rule in words under it, what starts it, the last run with its result in words (Done / Failed / Not met), the runs in the last 30 days, and the state — a SwitchField named by the rule with "On" / "Off" written beside it (a switch's name stays the rule's, never its state); the row menu has Turn off / Turn on (also on phones, where the cards show the state as a badge). **A rule** (DetailPage, view and edit in one page, P4.9): the state badge, who changed it, key figures (runs in the last 30 days, failed, last run), the rule (RuleBuilder read-only, its words above), its runs (DataTable); when the last run failed a danger Alert with the application's message and next step above the runs; actions Turn off and Edit. Edit mode: the name and the RuleBuilder; the bottom bar Cancel, **Test run** (the application's answer on the latest records — "Would run" / "Would not run" with its reason, nothing done — as a section), Save (the application's problems under their fields and an error toast; or saved). **New rule** (RecordFormPage). **Run log** (ListPage; All runs / Failed): time, the rule and the record as links, the result, what happened in the application's words. Every rule, figure, word and check is data or the example playing the application (`bsSummary`, `bsProblems`).
- **2026-10-16 — Merging duplicates is choose, see, confirm, result (P5.79).** Master data → Possible duplicates (group BT, `screens-BT.tsx`, `data-BT.ts`): the pairs the application found (both records with their codes, why: "Same PIB 106543218", "Same barcode 8600981000101", when found, the state in words — To review, Merged, Not duplicates with who decided). **Merge partners / Merge items** (DetailPage): "Which record stays" (CandidateList, one choice, each record's reason and figure; the application proposes the older and preselects its values; choosing the other record takes the application's other preselection and counts); "Values to keep" (ValueComparison with `chosen` / `onChoose`, columns "Beton Mix d.o.o. (stays)" / "Beton-Mix doo (merged into it)"); "What will happen" (KeyValueList of the application's counts: documents and open items moved, bank accounts kept, the inbox's matching, the merged record closed with its code leading to the kept one). Actions: Not duplicates, then **Merge** (caution, the main action) unavailable with its reason until every differing field has a value ("Choose the value to keep for 1 more field."). Merge opens the **IrreversibleConfirmDialog**: the action as title, "Beton-Mix doo into Beton Mix d.o.o." as subject, the consequence, the values kept as a preview (ValueComparison `chosen` only), the merged record's code typed. **The result** is the kept record's page: a success Alert with who merged what and when, what moved, the values kept, the documents that moved here as links (invoice 2026-1187 in the document inbox; the cement's receipt and issue at Site Liman 4).
- **2026-10-16 — Scheduled reports are built from the library (P5.80, group BU).** Nothing new was needed. The schedules are ListPage + DataTable (views All / Active / Paused / Last run failed with counts): the report and its kind, the schedule in the application's words ("Every Monday at 07:00"), who gets it ("Nenad Kovačević", "2 people, 1 outside"), the format, the next run (the application's instant through `format.dateTime`, "Paused" in words while paused), the last run's state as a badge with its time, and a SwitchField per row ("Sending: <name>", the label for assistive technology) that pauses or resumes it; the row's menu has Edit and Pause / Resume. One schedule is DetailPage: Pause / Resume and Send now (neutral), Edit (the main one, last); key figures next run, last run, its state, recipients; sections Report (the report and each parameter's chosen value — ReportPage's parameters —, the format, what happens when there is nothing to send), Schedule (repeats, the time zone "Europe/Belgrade (CEST, UTC+02:00)", the application's next three runs, who paused it and why, who created it), Recipients (people with their role and address, outside addresses with "Outside the company · Knjigovodstvo Jelić"), Last runs (DataTable: when, Sent / Failed / Skipped, "1 of 1" delivered, the file and its size, the application's note; Download in the row's menu) and "What recipients get" (EmailPreview with the sample values filled in, D27). A failed last run stands first as a danger Alert with the application's message and neutral actions Send now and Edit (D23). **Send now** asks in a ConfirmDialog titled by the action with the schedule as its subject (D22) and says the schedule does not change; the run joins the list. A new or edited schedule is RecordFormPage: Report (name, the report, its parameters as SelectFields that reset to the report's defaults when the report changes), Schedule (Repeats from the application's list — every day / week / month / quarter —, On: a weekday whose name comes from the provider's locale, or a day 1–28 / the last day from the application's list; At: the application's half hours, searched from 11 options; the time zone and the next run read-only — the next run is the application's, "The application plans it when you save" after a change), Recipients (MultiSelectField of the company's people; MultiSelectField of outside addresses used before; "Add an outside address" with the application's check under the field and "Add address"), Delivery (format PDF / Excel / CSV and "When there is nothing to send" as RadioGroupFields with descriptions), E-mail (subject with `{{date}}` / `{{period}}`, message) and the Preview. **No date of a run is computed by the library or by the screens**: every next run and every state is data.
- **2026-10-16 — DashboardGrid: a dashboard the user arranges (P5.81).** New, because nothing arranged cards of different widths: Launchpad's editing moves and hides module cards of one size and links; DashboardPage lays out a fixed set (stats, then two columns); KanbanBoard moves cards between stages. `DashboardGrid` takes the application's `cards` (id, title, size, the sizes it allows, its content — StatCard, a chart, a SectionCard), the application's `sizes` (name and columns), `columns` (default 4) and `editing`, and reports every change with the new layout and what changed (`onLayoutChange(layout, { kind: 'move' | 'resize' | 'remove', … })`); the application keeps the draft, saves it on its Done, puts it back on Cancel and adds cards from its catalogue (`addCard`). Grid: `columns` from 62em, two from 36em, one on phones; a card takes its size's columns, at most the grid's (two in the two-column grid, one on phones); the browser places the cards in order, never "dense", so the reading order is the visual order; heights follow the content. View mode adds nothing around the cards. **Editing:** each card in a dashed border.strong frame (radius lg, 8px) with a toolbar over its content — the handle (GripVertical 28px, "Move: <title>", the instructions as its description), the title (sm semibold), the size button (the size's name and a chevron; a menu of the sizes the card allows as radio items with a check), the card's menu (Move earlier, Move later, Move to the start, Move to the end) and Remove (X, 28px); the content stays visible and inert. Remove asks nothing: the application's Cancel puts the card back. **Moving, three ways (WCAG 2.5.7):** drag ("Launchpad dragging is live": pointer events, a mouse after 4px, a touch after a 250ms press, the card lifts and follows the pointer, a neutral dashed placeholder of its size where it lands, the slot nearest its centre measured when the drag starts — right-to-left needs no mirroring —, Escape or a cancelled pointer puts it back); the handle (Space / Enter picks it up, the reading direction's forward arrow moves it one place later and the other earlier, ArrowUp / ArrowDown to the place of the card above or below as laid out — `gridPlacement` reproduces the browser's placement, `dashboardKeyTarget` picks the card sharing the most columns —, Home / End, Space / Enter drops, Escape cancels, Tab away puts it back; each step announced politely, "Revenue: position 2 of 7."); the card's menu. **Phones:** one column, every card full width, no handle and no dragging, no size button (every size is the full width there); the menu moves and Remove removes. Loading keeps each card's place with a skeleton; without cards the application's `empty` (default EmptyState "No cards on this dashboard."). Pure and tested: `moveCardTo`, `moveCardBy`, `resizeCard`, `removeCard`, `addCard`, `layoutOf`, `cardSpan`, `allowedSizes`, `gridPlacement`, `dashboardKeyTarget`.
- **2026-10-16 — The director's customizable overview (P5.81, group BV).** DashboardPage with DashboardGrid as its one child (`col-span-full`). The header: the layout as a SelectField ("My overview · Default", "Month end"), a "Layout" menu (Save as…, Rename…, Set as default, Delete…) and Customize; while customizing: Add card, Cancel, Done (the one primary button, last) and a subtitle that says how. Add card is LookupDialog over the application's catalogue (the cards not yet on the layout, searched by name or kind; a card is added at the end at its catalogue size). Save as and Rename are FileNameDialog (the application's check returns "A layout with this name exists. Choose another name."); Delete is DeleteConfirmDialog with the layout as its subject ("Only the layout is deleted, never the figures"); deleting the default makes the next one the default (the application's rule, said in the message). The cards show the figures the other examples show: open receivables and overdue more than 30 days (group X), the main cash desk against its limit (AM), the budget used and plan against actual by cost centre (AR), revenue by month (X), Residential building Liman 4's progress (AA), the overdue invoices as a table (X), Liman 4 by cost type (AR).
- **2026-10-16 — Two statuses join the examples' tone map (P5.80).** `Skipped` (a run with nothing to send) and `Paused` (a schedule paused on purpose) are neutral: they wait on no one. A report run that was sent keeps the map's `Sent` (info), as every sent thing does.

## AML compliance (P5.82–P5.88)

- **2026-10-16 — AML compliance is assembled, not built (P5.82–P5.84).** The client risk assessment, the client file and the screening are made of DetailPage, ListPage, WorklistPage, Questionnaire, ReasonConfirmDialog, DropdownMenu, KeyValueList, KeyFigures, DataTable, FilterBar, SidePanels, AttachmentList, HierarchyChart, MaskedValue, HistoryList, ValueComparison, StatusBadge, DueDate and Alert. Nothing was missing, so nothing was added. Every risk, factor, effect, point, score, band, review cycle, next review, share, document verdict, PEP status, list, entry, match score, comparison mark and consequence is the application's data; the screens and the library never score, match, rank or decide, they show the application's figures and words and report the user's decisions with the reason the application requires.
- **2026-10-16 — A risk is a word in a tone (P5.82).** Low, Medium and High stand as StatusBadges ("Medium risk") in success, warning and danger — the word always carries the meaning. A factor's effect is the application's word ("Higher risk" in warning, "Standard" and "Lower risk" neutral) beside its points as the application writes them ("+20", "0"); the factors' table ends with the application's score as its total row ("Score 40") — given, never summed. The score is written "40 of 100" with its band in the application's words ("Medium: 30–59 points").
- **2026-10-16 — An override keeps the assessment beside it (P5.82).** "Override risk" (a neutral DropdownMenu button) offers the levels other than the one in force ("Set to High"; "Back to Medium, the assessment's" when an override is in force); the choice is confirmed in ReasonConfirmDialog — title "Override risk", the client as `subject`, the assessment's result and the consequence in the message, the application's reasons (one required) and optional details, the caution family. The page then shows an "Override" section: by the assessment, set to, reason, set by and when, details; the history records the change (Risk: Medium → High). The assessment's own level is never hidden.
- **2026-10-16 — A review starts from the last answers (P5.82).** The risk review is the Questionnaire with the application's questions and branch (the owners above a holding are asked about only when a company owns the client), the last assessment's answers filled in to be confirmed or changed, the summary where any answer can be changed, and "Send for assessment"; the application's result opens on the assessment page.
- **2026-10-16 — Next review by DueDate, document validity by the application's verdict (P5.82, P5.83).** The next review is DueDate with `warningDays={30}` (its "N days overdue" reads right for a review). A document's validity is the application's verdict as AttachmentList's `flag` ("Expired" danger, "Expires soon" and "Older than 12 months" warning; nothing for a valid one) with "valid until …" or "issued …" in the row's detail — not DueDate, whose words are a payment's. The "Review due" and "Needs documents" views follow the application's flags (the file's state), not dates the screen compares.
- **2026-10-16 — Owners as a tree, beneficial owners as a list (P5.83).** HierarchyChart draws the client on top and each owner under what it owns, the share on the line (`lineLabel`); a person is marked "Beneficial owner" by the application's rule (its words, under the section's title), a PEP or a potential PEP match as a badge in words; owners the client has not disclosed are a vacant node with `vacantLabel` "Unknown owner". Under the chart a DataTable lists the beneficial owners with the share in the application's words ("Indirectly 70%"), country and PEP status.
- **2026-10-16 — Identity numbers are masked, a match's facts are not (P5.83, P5.84).** In the client file the representative's national ID number and date of birth are MaskedValues (the application's reasons and "Other", "Access is logged" with what is kept). In a screening match the date of birth is shown beside the listed one, because the decision rests on it and only the compliance officer reviews matches.
- **2026-10-16 — A screening match side by side (P5.84).** WorklistPage, one match at a time: the screened person or company with its client (a link to the file), the list with its version, the application's match score ("74 of 100"), the listed entry, then ValueComparison with the columns "Client's record" and the list's name, each line marked by the application (`differs`, `note`: "Same, without diacritics", "Different", "Not on the list") and "3 of 4 differ" above it, and the application's summary under it. While a match is undecided the detail starts with the confidentiality reminder (below). Decisions: "False positive…" (neutral, CircleSlash) and "True match…" (caution, ShieldAlert), neither filled — a match has no default answer; each asks ReasonConfirmDialog for the application's reasons; the true match's message is the application's consequence ("The owner becomes a politically exposed person: …"). Several matches can be marked false positive at once (BulkActionBar), never confirmed as true matches together. After a decision the next match opens; on a phone the list comes first and the decisions stand in the bottom bar.
- **2026-10-16 — The client must not be told (P5.84; for P5.85–P5.88).** Wherever a potential match, a suspicion or a report is shown, a warning Alert titled "Confidential" says in the application's words that the client must not be informed (`ConfidentialNote` in the examples' `aml-shared.tsx`): never colour alone, never only an icon.
- **2026-10-16 — Screening results per person and list (P5.84).** A client's screening page lists the client, its owners and its representative against every list (one column per list): "No match" in words, a decided match as its badge, an undecided one as "Potential match" with a "Review" link to it; the lists with their versions; the re-screening history (HistoryList, the application's runs as a system actor, the decisions as people's entries). "Screen again" only asks the application.
- **2026-10-21 — Monitoring alerts are a worklist, decided one by one (P5.85).** The alert queue is WorklistPage: each row names the rule that raised the alert, the client with its risk in force (a StatusBadge), the transactions' total as the application gives it (MoneyText), the alert's age in the application's words and the assignee; the detail holds the rule and what it watches (the application's threshold, in its words), the transactions that triggered it with the application's marks ("New counterparty", "Cash", "Just below the threshold") and the total it gives (`totals` of the DataTable — never summed), the client's profile (risk, file state, PEP, expected activity, source of funds, screening) and the alert's history (HistoryList). "Close…" asks for the reason the application requires (ReasonConfirmDialog, neutral; several alerts at once from the BulkActionBar with one reason); "Escalate to a case…" is a Dialog with the case to go to (the client's open cases, or "Open a new case"), the application's reasons and details, caution family — then the case opens. An unassigned alert offers "Assign to me". A rule's figures, thresholds and ages are the application's: the screens count rows, never amounts.
- **2026-10-21 — A case is a DocumentPage (P5.86).** The client is the counterparty; the key figures are the risk in force, when it was opened, who investigates and the application's total of the transactions under review; the lines are the transactions of the linked alerts; the sections are the timeline (StatusTimeline with the next step: who approves next, the report to prepare), the linked alerts, screening matches and report (RelatedDocuments), the documents (AttachmentList), the tasks (a DataTable: task, owner, state in words with the reason a blocked one waits) and the decision; the side panels are the notes (ActivityList with a note field), the client and the history. The case's own states are Under investigation → Decision proposed → Approved → Closed, no suspicion / Reported; the lifecycle bar and the timeline name the last step by the outcome. Every case page starts with the `ConfidentialNote` as DocumentPage's `banner`.
- **2026-10-21 — Four eyes as a SignerList (P5.86).** A decision is proposed by one person ("Propose decision" → "No suspicion…" / "Report to the authority…", each a ReasonConfirmDialog with the application's reasons and the reasoning as details) and approved by another: the proposer and the approver are a SignerList — the proposer "signed" at the proposal's time, the approver waiting, the current user's row with `signLabel="Approve"` and Decline (with the application's reasons; the case goes back to the investigation and keeps the declined proposal in its history). The proposer cannot approve: the approver is the other of the compliance officer and the deputy, and the rule is written beside the list ("Four eyes" Alert, neutral). Approving "no suspicion" closes the case; approving a report opens the report as a draft (P5.87) and the case waits as Approved until the report is sent, then it is Reported.
- **2026-10-21 — The report is a DefinedForm from the authority's definitions (P5.87).** The suspicious transaction report is the illustrative authority's form kept by the application as field definitions (sections, fields, options, indicator codes, conditions — a legal person has a tax number, a natural person a date of birth; "Stopped until" shows when the funds were stopped), drawn by DefinedForm with the values the application filled in from the firm's record and the case. The page is PageHeader + ConfidentialNote + the form, with the progress (StatusTimeline: Draft → In review → Approved → Submitted → Acknowledged, the next step and its action), who prepared and who reviews (never the same person), and the history beside it (a 320px column from `lg`; on a phone everything in one column, the actions in the bottom bar). "Send for review" runs the form's `check()`: the missing values are said under their fields in the library's words, and a toast only reports that the report is not complete. The reviewer approves or sends it back with a reason; "Submit to the authority…" confirms what happens (caution ConfirmDialog). After that the form is read-only and "What was sent" records the instant, who sent it, the channel, the reference, the acknowledgement and the files kept — the files are the application's, the library renders no document.
- **2026-10-21 — The overview counts nothing (P5.88).** The AML overview is a DashboardPage: the figures over all 214 clients are the application's (`OVERVIEW_FIGURES`); only the open alerts and cases of the session are counted as rows. The clients by risk are a DonutChart whose slices carry the states' tones (danger, warning, success) and are named in the legend and the centre; the reviews due by month a BarChart with "Overdue" highlighted; the ageing a stacked BarChart of alerts and cases; alerts raised and closed two series. The compliance officer and deputy stand in a SectionCard with the work waiting; the year's obligations are a SetupChecklist (done / to do / blocked with the reason). The obligations page (DetailPage, section bar) holds the officer and deputy with their appointments and when they were reported to the authority, the staff's training records (a DataTable; the state — Done / Due / Overdue — is the application's word), the internal procedures as an AttachmentList with their adoption and review dates (a flag "Review due" from the application), the retention rules as a KeyValueList and the records whose period ends as a table, and the audit trail as a HistoryList paged by the application ("Show more").
- **2026-10-21 — Where the confidentiality note stands (P5.85–P5.88).** The kyc helper's `ConfidentialNote` (a warning Alert titled "Confidential", the words the application's) opens every case page (DocumentPage `banner`), every report page (under the header) and the detail of an alert that is part of a case. An open alert carries no such note: it is not yet a suspicion; its dialogs say "The client is not told."
- **2026-10-21 — The monitored company (P5.85).** The transactions monitored are the ones the accounting firm books and handles for its clients: Adria Commodities d.o.o. (the invented metals wholesaler of data-aml) is the trading company whose payments abroad and round advances raise the alerts and the case; Kvadrat Gradnja d.o.o.'s alert is its receipt from Stanogradnja Plus d.o.o. for order NAR-2026-0024 (data-AV). No second shell or module was built: one AML module of Knjigovodstvo Jelić monitors its clients' transactions, as an obligated accounting firm does.

## Floorplans and the canonical examples (P5.89)

- **2026-10-23 — Seven floorplans, three shells (owner).** The examples had grown to almost three hundred screens; SAP repeats five or six floorplans, and so do we: F1 List (ListPage), F2 Record (DetailPage, RecordFormPage, SettingsPage), F3 Document (DocumentPage with the one line editor, EditableGrid), F4 Worklist (WorklistPage), F5 Overview and analysis (DashboardPage, ReportPage, StatutoryFormPage, Pivot), F6 Steps (FormWizard, ImportWizard, Questionnaire, PeriodicRunPage), F7 Special canvases (calendar, floor plan, Gantt, POS, diagram, map — only where a list or a form cannot do), inside AppShell, AuthShell or PortalShell. `docs/floorplans.md` says for each when to use it, its anatomy on a desktop and on a phone, where actions go, how editing works and its empty, loading and error states. Every template and component stays; nothing new was needed — the floorplans are the templates that already existed, named and ruled.
- **2026-10-23 — The canonical set (owner's list, no swap).** Twenty-six screens, each on a desktop and on a phone: Shell — Sign in, Home, Notifications, Not found (404), Employee portal; F1 — Invoice list, Customers (search all, bulk edit, the import entry); F2 — Employee record (view and edit), My profile; F3 — Invoice, Invoice draft, Journal entry, Decrease document; F4 — Supplier invoices to approve, Bank statement; F5 — Overview (dashboard), Trial balance, VAT return, Cost analysis (pivot); F6 — Customer import, Health, book an appointment, Payroll run; F7 — Doctor's calendar, Restaurant service (the floor plan with a table's tab), POS checkout, Project timeline. Each of the owner's choices already represents its floorplan, so none was swapped. The walk-through signs in and clicks through the kept screens.
- **2026-10-23 — One story file per floorplan.** The single 20,000-line `examples.stories.tsx` became `examples-0-shell.stories.tsx` … `examples-7-canvases.stories.tsx`, titled "Examples/Shell", "Examples/F1 List" … "Examples/F7 Canvases", so the sidebar is the floorplan list. Kept per screen: the desktop and the phone story, the interaction stories that test the screen (hidden, `'!dev'`), and a hidden static state only where it is the floorplan's own state (the journal entry not balanced, the bank statement's line in focus on a phone). The other intermediate states of the kept screens were dropped with their pictures: each is a state of a component whose own stories show it. The story ids changed, so every Examples picture was regenerated (the Baselines workflow). `scripts/static-stories.mjs` counts "Examples/…" titles as Examples (`isExampleTitle`, tested).
- **2026-10-23 — What was removed, and how.** Every other example screen, its stories, data files, routes and pictures: 136 files and about 115,000 lines of example code (49 files and about 15,000 lines remain), and 4,272 pictures. The kept files were pruned of the removed screens' routes, then of every declaration nothing referenced any more (repeated until stable), then of unused imports; typecheck and lint proved the result. The dataset checks (`dataset-checks.ts`) keep what the kept screens show: the cancelled and the decreased invoice in the list and the customers' balances, the overdue total, the booking's free times against the doctor's calendar, the till's sale, Bistro Dunav's floor and table 7's tab.
- **2026-10-23 — Components stay, with their own stories.** No component or template was removed, including those only the deleted examples used. Audit: every exported component is rendered in its own stories or in those of the template that composes it (LifecycleBar, PageHeader, BackButton, HighlightedText, MentionText, FileIcon, AskedQuestion, QuestionList, PrintIssuedLine and PrintPaymentDetails through DocumentPage, the templates, SearchResultList, MessageList, FileGrid, AssistantPanel and PrintDocument); the states the removed screens showed are the components' own (C4), so no state needed moving.

Only the example-only shortcuts to removed screens were taken out: a walk-through link in the booking's confirmation, "Open the link from the e-mail" in the forgotten-password screen, the doctor's calendar opening the deleted patient chart, the reception's links, and the command palette's entries for removed records (the palette now offers the kept screens). The invoice's "PDF" keeps its printout (`screens-print.tsx`), part of the Invoice screen.
