## Owner review fixes (P5.90)

Each item of the owner's review was fixed as a class: the rule, every component and screen it touches, and a check where one can be written.

- **2026-10-23 — One header band, no white gaps (P5.90 item 1).** The white stripes on the grey table headers (the invoice, the final and cancelled invoices, the bank statement's open items) were seams between layers: every header cell was its own sticky, `will-change-transform` layer, and adjacent layers at fractional positions (any table in automatic layout, any zoom or display scale other than 100%) left hairline gaps through which the white body showed. The sticky header is now the header group itself (`thead`, or the header row group's element) — one band on one layer, with the header's background (surface.sunken, or surface.raised for the schedules) — and the cells are plain cells; only the corner stays sticky at the start inside the band. A totals row is a sticky `tfoot` band the same way. Every table, grid and schedule follows: DataTable, EditableGrid, TreeTable, AttendanceGrid, ShiftPlanner, PivotGrid, StatutoryFormPage (ResourceSchedule, CalendarView and Gantt already moved one band). Separators stay token borders (border.default / border.subtle); nothing between header cells is the page background. A unit test checks that `STICKY_HEAD` stands only on the element marked `data-sticky-head` in each of them.
- **2026-10-23 — Sticky headers in pure CSS, glued at any speed (P5.90 item 8).** The header below the shell no longer follows the page by script (`useStickyHead` set `--liro-head-shift` once a frame after each scroll, so a fast scroll left it a frame behind). Considered: (a) a plain `position: sticky; top: var(--liro-shell-top)` when the table fits its width — not enough, most grids scroll sideways and their region is then a scroll container; (b) a CSS scroll-driven animation — chosen, for every grid. The region is a named view timeline (`view-timeline: --liro-sticky-region block`, `data-sticky-region` set by `useStickyHead`), its scrollport inset at the top by the shell's height (`view-timeline-inset: var(--liro-shell-top, 0px) 0px`); the header band (`liro-sticky-head`, part of `STICKY_HEAD`) runs `liro-head-follow` (`transform: translateY(0 → --liro-head-room)`, linear, fill both) on that timeline over `exit-crossing --liro-head-start` to `exit-crossing --liro-head-start + --liro-head-room`: it moves one pixel for each pixel the region's top has gone under the shell, from the region's top border, and stops at the last row. The animation runs with the scrolling itself, on the compositor: the header is where it belongs in the very next frame of any jump. `useStickyHead` keeps only measurements that change on resize (ResizeObserver: the header's height, the start and room, the first column's width for the keyboard clearance); no scroll listener, no requestAnimationFrame. Gantt's SVAR time scale joins the same rule (styles.css selects `.liro-gantt .wx-scale` too). Browsers without scroll-driven animations (Firefox today) keep the header at the region's top (`@supports (animation-timeline: view())`). Playwright's `animations: 'disabled'` cancels these animations for a picture (their end time is not a number), which is the unscrolled state the pictured stories show. Proof: `expectGluedWhileJumping` (sticky-story-helpers) scrolls the page in eight large jumps down and up without waiting and checks in the very next animation frame that the header's top is the shell's bottom — in DataTable "Thirty rows under the shell" (desktop) and its new phone story (390px frame), and in EditableGrid "Thirty lines under the shell"; `sticky-head.test.ts` checks the CSS and that the hook has no scroll listener.
- **2026-10-23 — Cards clip with `overflow: clip` (P5.90 item 8).** A box with `overflow: hidden` is a scroll container even when it never scrolls; between a grid's region and the page it would own the region's view timeline (and break any sticky element inside). SectionCard, FormSection, FormTabs, ListPage's card, RegisterPage's card and Pivot's card now clip with `overflow: clip` (the same rounded clipping, no scroll container). The rule for new containers of tables: clip, never hide.
- **2026-10-23 — The line editor: flush, one line per edge, one focus ring (P5.90 item 2).** EditableGrid is the one line editor of every document. In a card it is flush with the card's edges as every table (no 16px inner padding, no frame of its own inside the card's); on its own the region carries the frame, on surface.raised as a table card. Every cell draws its bottom and end line (separate borders, no spacing), the row's last cell none, so each line is drawn once and aligned through every row, the subtotal's rule is the line under the row before it, and the totals' 2px border.strong line replaces the last row's. Every row is 36px: a 28px field in 4px padding, values and the header on the same middle line. One focus style: the library's focus ring (2px border.focus, inset 2px) round the cell while its field has the focus; the field itself draws no ring of its own inside the cell (read-only and amount rings removed there; before, a 1px border.focus outline on surface.hover plus the field's ring). A button beside a field (a date's calendar) keeps its own ring and the cell then draws none, so there is never more than one.
- **2026-10-23 — The line editor on phones, rebuilt (P5.90 item 3).** One card per line: its title ("Line 3", `grid.line`; or the line type for a heading or text line) with a 36px remove button (Trash2), then its fields under their column labels — text and searches (and columns 160px or wider) across the card, short fields (numbers, units, tax categories) two to a row —, its values (the amount) as a label and a value, its notes. "Add line" (with its menu) under the cards, always shown; the totals and the footer (the journal's BalanceBar) in one place after it, in the flow. The old totals card sticky at the top of the lines covered the first lines while scrolling, left an empty block above them and stray labels; it is gone. Nothing overlaps, nothing is wider than the screen (stories check both).
- **2026-10-23 — Simple line editors: optional columns (P5.90 item 4).** By default a line editor shows only what every line needs (item, quantity, unit, price, VAT, amount) and "Add line"; the rarer line types (section heading, text line, discount line) were already the menu of "Add line ▾" (`addTypes`, SplitAction: the plain line is the button). Decided for the discount column: the grid shows it when it is used, the application does not have to say so — a column with `optional` is hidden until some line uses it (`used(row)`, by default a value in its cell, `cellHasValue`) or until the user chooses its `addLabel` ("Discount on a line") from "Add line ▾"; that column's cell on the line last worked on then takes the focus. An optional column without `addLabel` appears only when used (the invoice draft's revenue account, needed only by a one-off line). Helpers `shownColumns` and `cellHasValue` are exported and tested.
- **2026-10-23 — The invoice draft, simple by default (P5.90 item 4).** The draft to Bojović i sinovi d.o.o. starts with plain lines only (cement, armature, a fixed asset sold, three services, an empty line): no section headings, subtotals, text line or discount line in the default picture; they and a line's discount come from "Add line ▾". Its header gains **Date of supply** (datum prometa, 06.10.2026.) and **Place of issue** (Novi Sad), ChangeableValues as the number, issue date and due date. The line amount less a line's discount is computed in `data-D1.ts` (its percent of quantity × price, to the para, half up). The journal entry keeps its BalanceBar as its totals: at the end of the action bar on a desktop, in the one totals place after the lines on a phone.
- **2026-10-23 — Number keys and Enter in the Questionnaire (P5.90 item 10).** On a choice question, 1–9 choose the numbered option (the number already stood at each option's end, ShortcutHint's key) and Enter goes to the next question when the answer is valid; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter goes on from anywhere, also from a multi-line text box; Enter on a button presses it; digits type into a typing field. The rule is one pure function, `questionnaireKeyAction(key, target, choices, modifiers)` (exported, unit-tested), used by the form's own key handler. Two gaps closed: the keys also work while nothing on the page has the focus (the page has just opened, or the user clicked beside the question), when it is the page's only visible questionnaire — a document listener that never acts while another element has the focus; and a typed answer's field (date, number, amount, text) takes the focus when its question is shown after the first — the primitive focuses the question's fieldset (not in the tab order) and that focus moves on into the field — so "Enter, type, Enter" needs no Tab. The first question never steals the focus on page load. A radio already chosen is only focused by its number, a checkbox toggles.
- **2026-10-23 — The course outline can be collapsed (P5.90 item 11).** Desktop: one neutral button above the lesson, "Hide outline" / "Show outline" (PanelLeft, mirrored in right-to-left, `aria-pressed` while the outline is shown — DocumentPage's "Hide panels" pattern), in the same place in both states so the focus stays on it; collapsed, the lesson takes the whole width. `defaultOutlineCollapsed` opens it collapsed and `onOutlineCollapsedChange` reports the choice so the application can remember it (uncontrolled; the application has no reason to drive it). Phones keep the content first and the outline collapsed in a sheet from "Course outline". A lesson's content stays the application's `children`; the stories show the kinds a lesson holds — text as RichText (sanitized HTML), a picture with its alt text and caption, a BarChart, a DataTable, a video with a captions track, callouts as Alerts — and the page keeps pictures and videos within the lesson's width (`max-width: 100%`, height auto). RichText was not extended with images, tables or callouts: those are components of their own in the lesson's slot.
- **2026-10-23 — One time parser and TimeField (P5.90 item 12).** `parseTimeText(text, { seconds })` reads a time of day the quick way, as the date fields read "010326": "630", "0630", "6:30", "6.30", "6,30", "06h30" are 06:30, "1430" is 14:30, "7" is 07:00, "6:30 pm" is 18:30, Arabic-Indic digits are read; with `seconds` "630" is 06:30:00 and "63015" 06:30:15. Seconds typed into a field without them are not dropped silently (the text is unreadable). The value is "HH:MM" / "HH:MM:SS" on a 24-hour clock, unreadable text is null, never midnight. TimeField is DateField's typing without a calendar: read on leaving or Enter and shown again as the value (immediate feedback), unreadable text kept with `field.invalidTime` ("Enter a time, for example 0630 or 6:30") and `onValidityChange(false)`, `withSeconds`, left to right in every language, the phone's number pad (`inputmode="decimal"`: digits and a separator). `FormTimeField` binds it to React Hook Form. The library's only typed times were ClockRecordList's correction drawer, now two TimeFields (`parseClockTime` delegates to the parser; `clock.timeInvalid` is gone). The library has no date-time field; the starts of ResourceSchedule's "Move to…" and ShiftPlanner's templates are chosen from the axis's slots, not typed, and stay selects.
- **2026-10-23 — The agenda has no bullet dots (P5.90 item 15).** CalendarView's agenda and the month's day list show an event as its time, title and description, without the tone's dot. A toned event carries the 3px start bar of its blocks in the tone's fg (inset 4px top and bottom); a neutral event has no mark. The tone is never the only signal (the event's words carry the meaning).
- **2026-10-23 — The "now" line never covers text (P5.90 item 17).** NowMarker stays one neutral line with a dot from the application's `now` (D25). Each time grid draws it after its lines, slots and backgrounds and before its content, so the content covers the line, never the reverse: CalendarView between the slot grid and the events layer; ResourceSchedule before the rows (desktop) and before the bookings (phone), without its former `z-index: 1`; Timetable before the cell's lessons, the cell content and the period's label made positioned; Gantt under the bars (`.wx-bars` is layer 1 in `gantt.css`, the marker layer 0), so bar labels and milestone names stand over it. The dot stays at the line's edge.
- **2026-10-23 — Resource schedules on phones: today's lists (P5.90 item 19, the F7 phone rule).** `ResourceSchedule` takes `phoneLists`: the day's lists the application passes — `{ id, label, bookings, emptyText? }`, such as Arrivals, Departures and In house — and on a phone (below 48em or `layout="phone"`) shows them instead of any timeline: a search (`phoneSearchLabel`, default "Search") over each booking's title, description and row name, folded for case and accents ("dordevic" finds "Đorđević", `scheduleSearchMatches`, tested), a segmented control of the lists, each with its count, the counts following the search; the chosen list's bookings as rows of at least 56px — title, row and time (or the stay's days), description, a toned booking's 3px start bar — and a press opens the booking (`onSelect`, the application's Drawer). Which booking is in which list is the application's data; the component computes nothing. Empty list: its `emptyText` (default "None today"); no match: "Nothing matches “…”"; `loading`: skeleton rows. Without `phoneLists` a phone keeps the one-row view (a few doctors); desktops and tablets always keep the timeline.

- **2026-10-23 — The bank statement works auto first (P5.90 item 9).** Statement 188 opens as one compact table of its lines (No., counterparty, signed amount, what the line does in a few words, its state) instead of a worklist with one line always open. Four states in words: _Matched automatically_ (the Core's exact matches — amount and reference, a known fee, the salary batch and its taxes, an own-account transfer), _Suggestion_ (the Core's best guess, to check), _Needs you_ (nothing found) and _Done_. "Accept all exact matches (6)" is the main action while there are any (then "Post statement"), and takes them all in one press with Undo — no confirmation. Only a line that needs the user is opened: a press opens it in an end Drawer (the whole screen on a phone) with what it does in one sentence, "Why: …" in a short line, "Confirm and next" (which opens the next line that needs the user) and "Change"; the full choice (close open items, post to an account, split) and the bank's details (an Accordion, "From the bank") stay folded until asked for — a line with nothing found opens with the choice. "Leave for later" is gone: a line the user does not open simply stays "Needs you". On a phone the cards are ordered by attention (Needs you, Suggestion, Matched automatically, Done). No library change was needed: DataTable (pressable rows, cards), Drawer, Accordion, StatusBadge and toasts with Undo cover it, so WorklistPage was left alone; every state, match and figure is the application's data (data-bank.ts).
- **2026-10-23 — CatalogPicker: choosing from 50 to 1,500 items (P5.90 item 14).** Radio buttons do not scale past a dozen services; a select hides what each costs and who performs it. CatalogPicker is a dialog on a desktop (720px) and a full-screen sheet on phones (D19), from the top down: the search first (in every level, by name, detail, provider, keywords and the levels' names, accents folded — "cacak" finds "Čačak"), filter chips (the application's rules, `matches`; several pressed all apply; the neutral selection, D17), the application's sections at the top level ("Most chosen", "Your recent", "Recommended for you", "On discount"), the levels as a drill-down with "Back to …" and the level's name, and the items as cards in a listbox (name; detail and who provides it; the price through `format.money` with the price before a discount struck through and the discount in the application's words, or the application's words instead of a price — "Covered by health insurance"; an unavailable card focusable with its reason). One item: a press chooses it and closes (fewest steps). Several (`multiple`): presses toggle (a checkbox mark and the neutral selection), "Choose 2" confirms; whether two items combine is the application's answer — it gives the others an `unavailableReason` on `onSelectedChange` — never the picker's. Long lists show 40 cards and "Show more" (paged, not virtualised: a card's height follows its words; the search narrows first). Keyboard: the search has the focus on opening; in a list the arrows move by the measured columns from the leading edge (`launchpadArrowTarget`), Home / End, Enter or Space choose. Loading (skeleton cards), error with "Try again", an empty catalogue and "Nothing found" with "Clear search and filters". Its logic is pure and tested (`catalog-picker-logic.ts`). The booking example offers Dom zdravlja Novi Sad's 61 services in it; the doctor is asked only for the chosen doctor's own services.
- **2026-10-23 — Every tap of a till answers at once (P5.90 item 20).** A first-day waiter with fifty guests at the door must see that a tap counted, or taps again out of doubt. A pressed product tile and a pressed − / + are highlighted for 700ms (`FLASH_DURATION`), and a cart line that appears or whose quantity goes up is highlighted and scrolled into view in the cart's own scroll (`useGrowingLines`, `grownLines` compares decimal strings exactly); the highlight is the neutral selection surface (never blue, D17) and a colour change, not a movement, so it stays with reduced motion (only its fade goes). A device that can vibrate gives a 12ms pulse (`tapFeedback`, guarded: desktop browsers and iOS have no `navigator.vibrate`, and a refused vibration is ignored). Nothing flashes when a screen first appears, so pictures stay still. A tile also shows how many of it the order holds (`inOrder`, read as "2 in the order"), so the count goes up under the finger.
- **2026-10-23 — A phone till shows the products first (P5.90 item 20).** On a phone PosShell no longer opens on the cart with the products in a sheet: the products (the categories, a search and the items in one scrolling area) are the screen, and the order is a compact bar at the bottom — "Order · 3 items · 1.011,00 RSD" from the application's `orderSummary`, highlighted at each change — that expands into a bottom sheet (85% of the height) with the cart and its main action. A waiter taps items far more often than they read the cart. `productsOpen` / `defaultProductsOpen` / `onProductsOpenChange` became `orderOpen` / `defaultOrderOpen` / `onOrderOpenChange` (a breaking change in the alpha). ProductGrid gained `search` (a local filter of the products given, by name or detail, across every category, the chips set aside while searching) and `categoryIds` (a product under several chips: the application's "Most sold" first and chosen by default, its order the application's figures).
- **2026-10-23 — Orders go to the kitchen when the waiter leaves the table (P5.90 item 20).** Restaurant tills (Toast, Lightspeed, Square for restaurants) send on leaving the order screen ("send on exit") and hold a course on demand ("hold / fire"); a lone "Send order" button is the step a busy waiter forgets, and an order left unsent is the worst mistake a till allows. The tab now marks a new line "New · sent when you leave the table", sends the new lines by itself when the waiter goes back to the floor (reported as "Sent: 2 to the kitchen, 1 to the bar." on the floor), keeps "Send now (n)" for a rush, and lets a line be held for a later course (a switch in the line's dialog; marked "Held for later"; sent with "Send held (n)"). No timer sends after a pause: it would send while the waiter is still tapping the order; an application may add one. The sending itself is the application's — the screen reports what went where (`sendLines`).
- **2026-10-23 — One tap opens a table; no "Needs cleaning" by default (P5.90 item 20).** On Bistro Dunav's floor a tap on an occupied table opens its tab, a tap on a free table opens a new tab at once (the number of guests is not asked: it is optional, `Party.size`), and only a reserved table is chosen first to show its reservation and "Seat guests". This refines D29 ("a click on a record opens it in place"): the table's tab is the record, opened at once. "Needs cleaning" is not a restaurant state unless the application turns it on: a cleared table is free at once, with Undo; closing a paid tab frees the table; clearing a table whose tab still has something to pay is unavailable with the amount as the reason. The library's restaurant story data dropped the state too (FloorPlan's states were always data; there is no library default). Seating, clearing and removing a line offer Undo instead of a confirmation; the story that edited a floor plan at phone width was deleted (FloorPlan refuses edit mode on phones, now proved by `floor-plan-phone.test.tsx`).
- **2026-10-23 — Toasts in the domain screens (P5.90 item 21, examples).** In the bank statement, the booking, the restaurant and the tills every routine confirmation is a `notice.success` that closes by itself (Helper b's library change) and covers no action: a decided line, the exact matches accepted, a table seated or cleared, a line removed, the order sent — each with Undo where it can be taken back; errors stay as they were.

- **2026-10-23 — Phones: no box with its own scroll inside the page (P5.90 item 5).** On a phone every list, table and tree flows with the page: DataTable's cards ignore `maxHeight` (no inner scrollbar, no white gap under the totals — the payroll preview's case); with `virtualize` a long card list is still drawn only where it is in view, but against the page's own scroll (the closest scrolling ancestor, or the window: `useWindowVirtualizer` with a scroll margin), never a box of its own; a flat card list's totals end the card with no band under them; TreeView (and TreeTable's phone tree, FolderPicker's tree) and LegalText are not windowed below 48em even with `maxHeight`. Desktop keeps `maxHeight` / virtualization. WorklistPage already scrolls its panes only from 62em; popover and select lists keep their native scroll (D20). Why: a box inside a scrolling page is two scrolls under one finger, and its fixed height left white space under the content.
- **2026-10-23 — One rule for every row of tabs (P5.90 item 6).** A tab row never wraps and never hides tabs in "More" for lack of room: when its tabs do not fit it scrolls sideways (finger, focus; no scrollbar), each edge with more tabs past it fades out over 32px (`edgeFade`, a mask, so it fades into any surface), and the active tab is scrolled into view, clear of the fade, when the row is first drawn and whenever it changes (`useTabRow`, `tab-row.tsx`). AppShell's module tabs, page Tabs (now one line, `flex-nowrap`; they wrapped before), FormTabs, PortalShell's section tabs, SectionBar and ListPage's saved views follow it. Saved views keep "More" after the fifth view: that is how many views a list shows on desktop, not an overflow rule; phones keep the one "View: …" select. Chosen over "More" for every row because the scroll keeps every tab one tap away and needs no measuring of which tabs fit; the fade says the row goes on. Focus rings of tabs are drawn inside the tab (`focus-visible:-outline-offset-2`) so the row's sideways scroll never clips them.
- **2026-10-23 — Long or unbroken text wraps, everywhere (P5.90 item 7).** The two text utilities every component uses for its text blocks, `bidi-content` (TEXT_DIRECTION) and `bidi-isolate` (TEXT_ISOLATE), now also set `overflow-wrap: break-word`, so an IBAN, a URL or a sixty-letter word breaks inside its box instead of running past it — in fields' hints and errors, KeyValueList values, cards' titles, dialogs, toasts, headings and table cells. `break-word`, not `anywhere`: a table's column still sizes by its longest word (the table scrolls sideways in its own box rather than squeezing words mid-letter), and flex rows keep their natural widths. Where a flex item could not shrink below the word, `min-w-0` is added (StatusBadge's label, FieldMessage); dialog and alert-dialog titles and descriptions (short, never table-sized) use `overflow-wrap: anywhere` with `min-w-0`, so an unbroken title never widens a phone's sheet. StatusBadge no longer forces one line: it stays on one line while it fits and wraps inside the badge only when wider than the room there. Stories "Unbroken text, phone width" (TextField, Cards, Dialog, StatusBadge; the Toast's long story) carry an IBAN, a URL and a long word (`UNBROKEN` in field-story-data) and are checked by the phone-overflow test.
- **2026-10-23 — A file that cannot be read shows its error, never its content (P5.90 item 7).** ImportWizard's `fileError` (the application's words) is the unreadable-file state: under the drop zone with its icon; while it is set the file's summary (name and what was read) is not shown and Next is unavailable until another file is read. The customer import example reads a file as the application would: a text CSV whose first row names at least two `;`-separated columns; a binary or damaged file (control characters, the replacement character) or a text without columns gives "… could not be read: …" in words (`readImportFile`, data-E.ts) and no columns — the bytes are never shown.
- **2026-10-23 — Empty states have their own space (P5.90 item 13).** EmptyState (and ErrorState) carries its vertical space: 32px above and below, 24px when `compact`. The places that show it add no vertical padding of their own (DataTable keeps only 16px at the sides, TreeView, TreeTable, SearchResultList, SlotPicker, ShiftPlanner, GazetteIssues, CartPanel, MyShifts, Pivot, LegalSearchPage, NotificationsPage, FileBrowser, HierarchyChart had 0 to 48px each), so "nothing here", "no results" and "could not load" look the same in a card, a table, a panel and a list, and never stand against a card's top edge. A one-line "None" inside a side panel's list stays a quiet line of text in the panel's padding; a full empty state is EmptyState.
- **2026-10-23 — The sensitive reveal dialog's note is one quiet line (P5.90 item 16).** MaskedValue's dialog: the question stands 8px above its options (a radio group's options now stand 8px under their question everywhere, a single control keeps 4px), and "Access is logged. Your name, the time and the reason are recorded." is one line of 12px secondary text directly above the buttons, without icon or box (the owner's latest decision; it replaces the P5.28 neutral Alert with ScrollText). `masked.loggedTitle` is now "Access is logged." (with its full stop), followed by `logNote` / `masked.logged`.
- **2026-10-23 — A field's hint is under its control (P5.90 item 18).** Field's order is label, control, then the description (hint), then the error or the disabled reason — never a hint between the label and the control — so fields side by side in a row keep their controls on one line whether or not one has a hint (the POS refund's "ID type" / "Buyer ID": the ID's "9 digits" pushed its input down). The control stands 4px under the label; the hint and the messages 5px under the control, 4px apart. Every field on Field (TextField, SelectField, MoneyField, NumberField, DateField, BuyerField's parts …) and CodeInput follow; EditableGrid still hides a cell field's hint and messages (`[data-field-messages]`). BuyerField's own description stays under its legend: it is about the whole group, above the row.
- **2026-10-23 — Toasts never block (P5.90 item 21).** The rule, for the library and for every example (helper d applies it to groups H, I, K and bank):
  1. A **routine save** (a draft, a setting, a form the user stays on) is answered inline and quietly: `SaveStatus` ("Saving…", then "Saved" with a check in status.success.fg, 12px) beside the action that saved, until the next edit sets it back to 'idle'; a failed save is the application's words in the same place (`role="alert"`). No toast.
  2. A **reversible action** (approve, move, delete with the Core's undo) is never confirmed beforehand: it happens, and a success toast says so with **Undo** (`action`); the toast stays 8 s.
  3. A **toast** reports an outcome elsewhere or out of view ("Payroll posted", "Request sent to …", "Signed out"). Success and info close by themselves after 4 s and have **no close button**; a success or info toast without an action lets clicks through (`pointer-events: none`), so it never covers anything usable. A warning closes after 6 s with a close button; an error stays until closed (Appendix B.8). A loading toast waits for its update.
  4. Toasts stand above every bar at the bottom: AppShell's and PortalShell's bottom bars and WorklistPage's detail bar (`--liro-shell-bottom`), and a page's sticky bottom bars — FormActions' / a record's edit bar, the wizard's Back / Next row on phones, an application's own (`useBottomBar`, which publishes `--liro-bottom-bars`).
  5. Never a toast for: a field's problem (under the field), a decision (ConfirmDialog), a lasting state (Alert, Banner), a download (the browser shows it), or what to do next (D23).
     In the examples: the journal entry's "Save draft" shows "Saved" beside the button (screens-F); the Gantt's moved dates offer Undo (screens-AA); posted / sent / signed-out outcomes stay success toasts, which now close by themselves.

## P5.90 follow-ups (P5.91)

- **2026-10-23 — The till's renamed props are told in the release notes (owner).** P5.90 turned PosShell's phone layout round (products first, the order as a bar that opens a sheet), so `productsOpen` / `defaultProductsOpen` / `onProductsOpenChange` became `orderOpen` / `defaultOrderOpen` / `onOrderOpenChange` with `orderSummary`. No alias for the old names: their meaning is inverted (open meant the products, now it means the order), so an alias would open the wrong thing. No repository uses them (this one, and `liro-bridge`, which does not use `@veljaos/ui`); the changesets of P5.90 and P5.91 carry the rename and the migration into the changelog.
- **2026-10-23 — A sticky first column never loses a row's line (owner).** A table's first column stands on a compositing layer of its own (P5.28, P5.29: without it its text was antialiased one way or the other from run to run). With `will-change: transform` that layer kept its row's fractional place — rows are fractional, 45.9px at the 1.45 line height of Appendix A — and where the next row's cell rounded the other way, its opaque background covered the row's line: in the invoice list between rows 3 and 4, in the bank statement between rows 2 and 3, and in Pivot, the statutory form, the trial balance and the VAT return; 104 lines in 134 tables, measured by screenshots of every table story in both directions in the pinned Chromium. Tried: dropping the layer (the line returns, the flaky pictures with it); drawing each row's line above the next cell, on the layer on top (30 lines still missing); a `translateZ(0)` layer (1 left, the same on `main`: a table without a line there). `STICKY_START` and `STICKY_START_AFTER_SELECT` are now `[transform:translateZ(0)]`: still one layer per cell, placed on whole pixels. Every grid with a sticky first column uses the two constants (a unit test checks it), so DataTable, EditableGrid, AttendanceGrid, ShiftPlanner, ResourceSchedule, Pivot and StatutoryFormPage all follow; their pictures change once. Changing the line height to whole pixels was not done: it is Appendix A's type scale, the owner's.
- **2026-10-23 — A faint change is not a "changed" picture (P5.91).** The visual comparison counts a pixel as different only past Playwright's colour threshold (0.2), and a 1px border.default line on white is under it: the left-to-right pictures with the missing line passed against the fixed code, and the Baselines workflow (`--update-snapshots=changed`) did not rewrite them. The pictures of every story with a table's sticky first column (the Examples, DataTable, EditableGrid, AttendanceGrid, ShiftPlanner, ResourceSchedule, Pivot, the templates that hold them) were regenerated with `--update-snapshots=all` in the pinned image, so the baselines show the lines. The threshold stays: lowering it would make antialiasing noise fail the suite; a fix of a faint look regenerates its pictures this way.

## Templates consolidated to the core (P5.92)

- **2026-10-27 — About eighteen page templates (owner).** A template is a floorplan's frame, not a domain's page. The ones kept: the shells (AppShell for everyone inside a company, AuthShell for signing in, PortalShell for people outside, PosShell for the till) and Launchpad (the home); ListPage and RegisterPage (F1: a register's numbering and locked periods are not a list's); DetailPage, RecordFormPage and SettingsPage (F2: view and edit, create with a guard, save per row); DocumentPage (F3); WorklistPage (F4); DashboardPage, ReportPage and StatutoryFormPage (F5: an official form's grid is not a report); PeriodicRunPage (F6: lock, steps, checks, preview, post); StatusPage and NotificationsPage (every application has them); PrintPage and PrintDocument (the sheet and the one business document). A domain page is a composition of these with the components, written in `docs/recipes.md` "Pages composed from the core templates"; the components stay, with their own stories.
- **2026-10-27 — The domain templates removed (owner).** LegalActPage → DocumentPage with LegalText, LegalContents and useLegalPanels; LegalSearchPage → ListPage with FilterBar's tree filter and SearchResultList (`snippetFromRanges` moved to the search helpers; `snippetText` duplicated `highlightText` and `gazetteNumbers` was the template's own, both removed); CoursePage, ArticlePage and AskPage → one reading page (DetailPage, a reading-width section, PageContents or the outline in the side column), no new template because a reading page needs nothing DetailPage lacks; PickList and StockCount → WorklistPage / ListPage inside `density="touch"` with ScanField and QuantityStepper (`warehouse-logic` with them); PaymentOrderForm → RecordFormPage, its paper form a JSON layout; SigningPage → DetailPage (or DocumentPage) with the preview first and SignerList in the side column, first on phones — the Employee portal example composes it so; FileBrowser → ListPage with FileGrid, FileDetails and the dialogs (`file-browser-logic` stays). Their 123 message keys went with them; three older unused keys (`ips.problem`, `queue.waiting`, `swap.shift`) are left for a later cleanup. Alpha breaking change, told in the changeset.
- _[Superseded by P5.95: printed documents are liro-folio's PDFs, and the print parts left the library]_ **2026-10-27 — Printouts are JSON definitions (owner).** PrintCertificate, PrintGradeReport, PrintFinding and PrintLegalAct are removed: liro-folio renders a document's layout from a JSON definition using the print parts (`PrintPage`, `PrintTitle`, `PrintDetails`, `PrintTable`, `PrintSection`, `PrintSignatures`, `PrintAmountDueLine`, `PrintPaymentDetails`, `PrintIssuedLine`), which stay exported. The library keeps PrintDocument as the business document every application prints; the Serbian formal acts are the next round's.
- **2026-10-27 — Four to six sidebar stories per template (owner).** Each kept template shows its default, empty, loading, error and phone stories and the one that matters most (where the template has the state; a shell or a printout has fewer); Arabic, Japanese, long text, interaction and intermediate states carry `'!dev'`, so the story, accessibility and visual tests still run them. ListPage got Loading, Empty and Error stories composed from DataTable's skeletons and empty state and ErrorState in the card.

## The owner's review, round 4 (P5.93)

- **2026-10-27 — One non-editable state for fields: read only, in the old disabled look (P5.93 item 1, the owner's firm decision).** Every field and editor (Field and every *Field, CheckboxField / SwitchField / RadioGroupField, ComboboxField, MultiSelectField, LookupField, the date, period, month, time, number and money fields, PasswordField, CodeInput, BuyerField, QuantityStepper, ScanField, MentionCombobox, RichTextField, NumericKeypad, PlanComparison, SlotPicker, DefinedForm, EditableGrid's cells and the `@veljaos/ui/form` bindings) has one state for a value that cannot be changed: `readOnly`. `disabled` and `disabledReason` are gone from `FieldBaseProps` (alpha breaking change). It replaces the 2026-09-25 decision "Read-only is text, not disabled": read only now LOOKS like the old disabled field — surface.disabled background, a border.default line — but the value stays in text.primary, so it is readable; it is focusable (focus ring, border unchanged), selectable and copyable, announced as read-only (native `readonly` on inputs, `aria-readonly` on checkboxes, switches, radio groups and the non-input boxes, the title "Read-only"). One shared class set: `READ_ONLY` (inputs and boxes) and `READ_ONLY_CHOICE` (checkboxes, radios, switches, through a `readOnly` prop on the primitives that sets `data-readonly`) in `primitives/classes.ts`; `ReadOnlyBox` (field.tsx) for a value that is not one line of text (MultiSelectField's pills); EditableGrid draws a read-only cell grey as a whole (styles.css). A read-only checkbox, radio or switch keeps its state drawn (the check, the dot, the thumb's side in text.secondary on the grey) and ignores a press or Space. No hint and no placeholder in read only; an empty value shows "—" (`READ_ONLY_EMPTY`, the placeholder of an input). The error, when the application gives one, still shows.
- **2026-10-27 — A read-only field shows no reason (P5.93 item 1).** The old "disabled with a visible reason" under a field is gone with the disabled state; in the spirit of "no helper text in read only" a read-only field says nothing under itself. When the application must say why something cannot be changed, it says it once where the page needs it (an Alert or Banner above the form, a section's line, AttendanceGrid's lock line). Where a choice that cannot be made is a matter of its own, the component keeps its own words: PermissionMatrix's phone cell (read-only checkbox and the matrix's reason under it, as the desktop cell's tooltip), SeatingChart's "This table is full." instead of a dead seat select, RuleBuilder's test select shown only once the field is chosen (the message `rule.fieldFirst` is removed). A choice inside a field that does not apply (a radio's, a select's or a combobox's option `disabled`) stays: it is an option, not the field's state.
- **2026-10-27 — Actions keep "unavailable with a reason"; forms around one action take `unavailableReason` (P5.93 item 1).** Buttons and actions are not fields. A component whose field exists only to start one action — AssistantComposer, MessageComposer, ReplyComposer, EmailFirstForm, NewsletterSignup, SatisfactionRating — replaces `disabled` + `disabledReason` with `unavailableReason`: the field is read only, the action unavailable, and the reason stands in words under it (FieldMessage, linked by aria-describedby to the action). FileDropzone is an action, not a value: `unavailableReason` draws the zone grey, keeps "Choose files" focusable (aria-disabled), ignores drops and says why under the zone; it has no read-only state.
- **2026-10-27 — While an action runs, fields are read only (P5.93 item 1).** The "Notify …" checkboxes of ConfirmDialog and ChangeConfirmDialog, RecoveryCodes' "I have saved these codes" while the codes load, and FileNameDialog's name while it saves were disabled; they are read only now (`NotifyChoices` `readOnly`).
- **2026-10-27 — Skeletons are text.primary at 10% (P5.93 item 2).** A skeleton of surface.disabled vanished on surface.sunken (both gray-2 in light), so RecoveryCodes' loading codes, and every skeleton on a sunken area, looked blank. The Skeleton primitive now fills with `bg-current/10` over `text-primary`: on a raised surface it is the same grey as before, and it stays visible on sunken, selected and dark surfaces. No new token.
- **2026-10-27 — Every loading state is visible; every empty state says something useful (P5.93 item 2).** AreaMap and Diagram write their loading words ("Loading the map", "Loading the diagram") over the skeleton of their canvas. LinkSuggestions without suggestions shows its box with the title and one quiet line (`messages['suggestions.empty']`, or `emptyText`). HierarchyChart's empty chart is an EmptyState with the application's words (`empty`) and first step (`emptyAction`), and its tools (search, fit, "Show only this unit", the path) are not drawn while it has no nodes (loading, failed, empty). - **2026-10-27 — A refusal is not an error (P5.93 item 10).** MaskedValue's "Refused" (`error` outside the dialog) and "Not allowed" (`notAllowedReason`) keep a KeyValueList row's shape — the label at the start, the mask and "Show" at the end — with one neutral line of secondary text under the value (no red, no error icon), which describes "Show". The code is a `role="region"` named by its title (or `label`, default "Code"), always `dir="ltr"`, a tab stop only while it scrolls (measured, as DataTable's area). **Highlighting** is a subpath of its own, `@veljaos/ui/code` (tsup entry `code`, `exports["./code"]`), so the main bundle never loads Shiki: `<CodeHighlighting>` gives every CodeBlock inside it `highlightCode` through a context (`CodeHighlighterProvider` in the main entry, which also lets an application pass another highlighter); outside it the code is plain text. `highlightCode` uses Shiki's tokenizer `@shikijs/primitive`, its JavaScript regular-expression engine `@shikijs/engine-javascript` (`forgiving`; no WebAssembly — `@shikijs/engine-oniguruma` is not installed) and `@shikijs/langs`, each language a dynamic import loaded on first use (a curated list of 22: bash, csharp, css, dockerfile, dotenv, go, graphql, html, http, ini, java, javascript, json, jsonc, jsx, kotlin, powershell, python, sql, tsx, typescript, xml, with aliases; YAML and TOML left out — their TextMate grammars carry no licence); code over 100,000 characters and lines over 2,000 are not tokenized. **Colours: the Liro code theme.** No Shiki theme is shipped; `LIRO_CODE_THEME` maps TextMate scopes to CSS variables (`var(--liro-code-keyword)` …), `tokensFromShiki` keeps only those names as a `CodeTokenKind` (any other colour is dropped), and styles.css ("Code") sets each variable from a Liro meaning per theme: comment and punctuation text.secondary, keyword family.document.fg, string family.positive.fg, constant (numbers, booleans, attributes) family.caution.fg, entity (functions, types, tags, JSON keys) family.verify.fg, link text.link, inserted / deleted / invalid status fg; the ANSI colours from the status and family fg and bg. No blue in syntax (D17). Every one measured ≥ 4.5:1 with contrast.ts on surface.sunken and on the success, danger and warning backgrounds over it, in both themes. The stories wait for `data-ready` (highlighting is asynchronous). Versions: `@shikijs/primitive`, `@shikijs/engine-javascript` and `@shikijs/langs` 4.5.0 (MIT, the npm `latest`, published 2026-10-01), bringing `@shikijs/types` 4.5.0, `@shikijs/vscode-textmate` 10.1.0, oniguruma-to-es 4.3.6, oniguruma-parser 0.12.2, regex 6.1.0, regex-recursion 6.0.2, regex-utilities 2.3.0 (MIT) and `@types/hast` 3.0.5 / `@types/unist` 3.0.3 (types only); not the `shiki` package (it brings the WebAssembly engine and every theme). Notices: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md "Shiki and its dependencies", with the grammars' own MIT notices (VS Code, dotenv, GraphQL, REST Client, Kotlin). The consumer check renders a highlighted CodeBlock from the packed subpath (`apps/consumer-check/src/CodeExample.tsx`).

- **2026-10-27 — The assistant's work display: Trace and its patterns (P5.93 item 49, owner).** After shadcn/ui's Trace and AI Elements (chain of thought, plan, queue, reasoning, sources, subagent, task), one row in our design (`components/trace.tsx`, pure rules in `trace-logic.ts`, tested): an icon, a one-line title in the application's words (wrapping, never cut), an optional description (a count, a duration) and a status — done (default; past tense; the title and icon text.secondary, calm), running (present tense; the title shimmers through an alpha mask so its colour and contrast stay — the `liro-shimmer` utility in styles.css; with reduced motion no shimmer and the spinner ring), pending (text.tertiary, an empty circle), error (the failure in words, a danger CircleX). Changes of status are announced politely, once each (the last changed step's title; never every token), with state adjusted while rendering. **Patterns**, each one calm line until opened: `Reasoning` ("Thinking…" → "Thought for 5 s" from the application's duration; open while thinking, closed when done unless the user toggled it — the user's choice wins from then on), `ChainOfThought` (a summary that opens into steps; status from the steps unless given), `Plan` ("2 of 5 done", announced as it changes), `Queue` (to do / completed, each with its count), `Task` (steps as they happen; opens and closes as Reasoning), `Subagent` (the agent's name and duration as the description, its steps and result) and `Sources` ("Used 4 records"; the same id or address once; record icons; external links marked). Counting steps is not a business figure (as Questionnaire's "3 of 7 answered"); every word is the application's or a provider message (`trace.*`). AssistantAnswer gains `work` (the patterns above the blocks; while thinking they replace "Thinking…"), and its sources block is now the Sources row ("Used 2 records") instead of an always-open numbered list — one calm line by default (P5.89 principle 1). Shown in "Components/Assistant/Trace" (its own story file), AssistantAnswer "With its work" and AssistantPanel "With its work". Nothing calls a model.

- **2026-10-27 — Dragging items between lists, one shared mechanism (P5.93 items 45, 46).** `useListDrag` (`components/use-list-drag.ts`, logic `list-drag-logic.ts`, tested) drags an item between lists stacked on a page or within one: the lists are elements marked `data-drop-zone`, their items `data-drop-item`, measured when the drag starts (so right to left needs no mirroring). It follows the dragging rule ("Launchpad dragging is live"): pointer events, a mouse after 4px, a touch after a 250ms press without moving more than 8px, the page does not scroll under a touch drag, Escape or a cancelled pointer puts it back. The look is the light variant of the rule (as ShiftPlanner's): the item lifts (shadow lg, border.strong, the raised layer) and follows the pointer; nothing slides; the list it would land in takes surface.selected and a 2px border.strong line marks the place — neutral, never blue. The landing place is the list under the pointer among those that take the item (else the nearest), after every other item whose centre is above the pointer (`listDropTarget`); a drop that changes nothing reports nothing (`dropMoves`). Dragging is always a shortcut: every user of it has a menu (and so a keyboard) way, and announces each move.

The old `{ join, conditions, actions }` is the first branch (migration note in the changeset). The logic grew: `addRuleBranch`, `addRuleOtherwise`, `moveRuleItemTo` (where a drag lands), `RULE_OTHERWISE` (Else's id for `addRuleAction` and `removeRuleItem`); `addRuleCondition`, `addRuleGroup`, `addRuleAction` and `setRuleJoin` take a branch's (or group's) id, default the first branch; `rulePlace` reports `branchId` and a 'branches' list; the If block never moves or goes; `moveFocusTarget` was removed (no move buttons any more). The library still evaluates nothing.

# Decisions of helper h (P5.93 items 43 and 44)

- **2026-10-27 — Seven new charts in `@veljaos/ui/charts` (P5.93 item 44, owner).** CandlestickChart, FunnelChart, ScatterChart, Heatmap, SankeyChart, MatrixChart and Treemap stand in the charts' own card (`ChartCard`: title, description, `controls`, "Show as table", the loading skeleton, `chart.noData`, the error with Retry, `defaultView`) and use the charts' tooltip body (`ChartTooltipContent`) and legend; values stay decimal strings, numbers only to draw (D4); every figure a person reads is written through `format`. **Recharts where it has the chart** (Funnel, Scatter, Sankey, Treemap, each drawn with our own shapes); **our own SVG** for Candlestick, Heatmap and Matrix (Recharts has none). No new dependency.
  1. **One keyboard and tooltip layer for marks reached one by one** (`charts/item-plot.tsx`, `ItemPlot`): every mark carries `data-chart-item`; the plot is one Tab stop (`role="application"`, named by the title, described by `chart.itemKeys`), the chart's own key function moves between the marks (a sequence — `sequenceKeyTarget`, the arrows with the screen, ArrowDown forward, Home / End — or a grid — `gridKeyTarget`, Home / End a row's ends, Ctrl/Cmd+Home / End the grid's); the reached mark is measured from the DOM, shows its tooltip, takes the focus ring round it and is announced once (a polite status); Escape hides; the pointer shows the same tooltip over a mark. The role, the tab index and the listeners are set on the element in an effect (as MapCanvas does), because jsx-a11y strict counts `application` as non-interactive. Recharts' own accessibility layer is off on these charts (`accessibilityLayer={false}`), so there is one Tab stop.
  2. **Measured in pixels.** The plot measures its width (ResizeObserver; a moment below 16px — a full-page screenshot — keeps the last layout) and lays the marks out from the start (`physicalX`: mirrored in right-to-left for the charts whose axis is time or a scale: the candles' days, the heatmap's hours, the matrix's impact, the Sankey's flow, the treemap's blocks; the funnel is symmetric; the scatter's axes are Recharts' reversed axes). The plot's frame is left to right; the tooltip and the hidden texts keep the page's direction. SVG text carries no `direction` attribute (in SVG it turns `text-anchor` around — the right-to-left Sankey's names stood on the wrong side); `unicode-bidi: plaintext` keeps Arabic in order.
  3. **Text is HTML where it can wrap:** the value axis and the category labels of the candlestick, the heatmap's and the matrix's row and column names, and the funnel's stage names (a column at the start: name, then the value · the application's share) are HTML beside the plot (`charts/axes.tsx`), never cut. The funnel first wrote its names on raised tags inside the stages; a tag covered a narrow stage whole (the shapes looked like slivers), so the names moved to the start column.
  4. **CandlestickChart (exchange rate):** one meaning, the main blue; a rising candle (the close at or above the open, compared exactly as decimal strings, `candleRises`) is hollow, a falling one filled — the shape says the direction, the legend names it (`chart.rising`, `chart.falling`). A rate rising is neither good nor bad, so no green or red. Bodies 60% of their band, 16px at most, 1px at least; a period without its four prices is a gap. Round ticks from `niceTicks` (1, 2, 2.5, 5 × 10ⁿ), written short (`shortTick`); the prices in full in the tooltip (`chart.open`, `chart.high`, `chart.low`, `chart.close`) and the table.
  5. **FunnelChart (CRM conversion):** every stage the main blue (a stage that means a state takes its tone — "Won" success in the story), 2px of the card between stages; widths follow the values (drawing only); the conversion is the application's `share`, named by `shareLabel`.
  6. **ScatterChart (price vs margin, optional bubbles):** series with the charts' palette rule (one blue, a second grey, three or more only with `palette="categorical"`); each axis named and written as an amount, a percentage (`format.percent`) or a number (`ScatterAxis`); points a 75% fill with a 1px line of the card; `size` makes bubbles whose area follows the value (4–20px, `scatterRadius`); axes from `niceTicks` (Recharts' "auto" domain gave steps of 950); the keys walk the points by x, then y (`scatterOrder`).
  7. **Heatmap (sales by weekday × hour):** the RegionChart rule — the application's `breaks` cut the values into at most five steps compared exactly (D4), one meaning in shades (main or neutral, 25–100%), a missing value hatched "No data", never 0; the legend writes the ranges through `format` (`map.stepBelow` / `stepBetween` / `stepFrom`) or the application's `stepLabels`. The steps, shades and ranges moved from `map/map-logic.ts` to `charts/steps.ts` (`valueStep`, `stepCount`, `stepRanges`, `stepShade`, `MAX_STEPS`); map-logic re-exports them under their old names (`regionStep` …), so nothing changes for applications; a sixth break no longer makes a sixth step. The legend and the hatch are `charts/step-legend.tsx`.
  8. **MatrixChart (risk matrix likelihood × impact):** the application's levels with status tones (a state: the tones' `bg`, `border` and `fg`), the level of every cell the application's (`cellLevels`), items placed by row and column; each cell writes its count, the tooltip lists the first six and "+N more" (`chart.more`), the table names every item with the level; the scales named (`rowLabel`, `columnLabel`).
  9. **SankeyChart (cash flow):** nodes main blue (a node that means a state takes its tone), flows a grey wash (`chart.comparison` at 40%, 70% under the pointer); a node's total is the application's `value`, never added; names beside their nodes toward the inside on a halo of the card, written only where they fit the room between the columns (`sankeyLabelRoom`, halved where two columns' names face each other) — never cut, the tooltip and the table say every one (on a phone most names of a three-column flow are left out); the flow mirrored in right-to-left. The table lists the flows (`chart.from`, `chart.to`). Flows must not loop (Recharts' layout).
  10. **Treemap (expenses by account group):** without groups every block the main blue; with groups (one level, `children`, the group's total the application's) each group a categorical hue named in the legend — the groups are the categories, so the categorical palette is the default there; names on a raised tag only where they fit whole (`textWidth`, CJK as 1em); the table lists the groups with their totals and the blocks under them.
  - Messages (new, "P5.93 (h)"): `chart.itemKeys`, `chart.open`, `chart.high`, `chart.low`, `chart.close`, `chart.rising`, `chart.falling`, `chart.cellName`, `chart.flow`, `chart.from`, `chart.to`, `chart.none`, `chart.more`. `ValuesTable` gained `writeSeries` (a series already written, such as a share).
  - Tested: `plot-logic.test.ts` (keys in both directions, ticks, candles, grids, scatter order and radius, the trapezoid, the Sankey's data, columns and label room, treemap leaves, the steps) and `item-charts.test.tsx` (legends and tables of every chart); every new story in the story, phone-overflow and accessibility specs in the four modes (574 passed).

- **2026-10-27 — Maps of Serbia shipped with `@veljaos/ui/map` (P5.93 item 43, owner).** `loadSerbiaBoundaries(level)` loads one level on first use — `region` (the five statistical regions of NSTJ level 2, 8 KB), `district` (the 24 districts and the City of Belgrade with their ISO 3166-2:RS codes, and the province, 17 KB) or `municipality` (the 145 cities and municipalities and the province, 51 KB) — each a separate chunk (`dist/regions-*.js`, `districts-*.js`, `municipalities-*.js`, imported dynamically by `dist/map.js`; no Recharts in the map subpath). An area has `id`, `name` (Serbian, Latin script, with its diacritics — the source's ASCII names were corrected by hand), `nameEn`, `parent` (a district's region, a municipality's district, computed by largest overlap) and for municipalities `kind` (city / municipality / province); `serbiaChildren(areas, parentId)` is the drill-down's next step. The data are TopoJSON (quantized to 10,000 steps) in TypeScript modules as one string each, read by a small TopoJSON reader of our own (`map/topology.ts`, tested), so the package needs no `topojson-client`.
  1. **Source: geoBoundaries gbOpen, build of 12 December 2023 (commit 9469f09): SRB ADM1 and ADM2 (OpenStreetMap, ODbL 1.0) and XKX ADM0 (OpenStreetMap; geoBoundaries lists it as CC BY-SA 2.0) for the outline of Kosovo and Metohija.** Both allow commercial use; never GADM. The derived data are under the ODbL (notice in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, "Boundaries of Serbia"; the files' headers say it); **the attribution must be shown with the map**: `SERBIA_BOUNDARIES_ATTRIBUTION` ("© OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), via geoBoundaries"), given by the loader and written under the map by RegionChart's new `attribution` prop (MapCanvas `attribution`, after a base map's). Processing in a scratch directory, not in the repository's scripts: mapshaper 0.6.113 (a tool only, MPL-2.0; nothing of it ships) merged the layers, cleaned slivers and gaps between the two sources (snap 0.002°, gaps under 20 km²), dissolved the districts into regions, simplified (weighted Visvalingam, 8% of the points, shapes kept) and quantized.
  2. **Kosovo and Metohija, per D31 and P5.31a.** It is drawn within Serbia's area, never as a country. Inside Serbia's own division it appears as Serbian law names it: the **Region Kosovo i Metohija** among the five statistical regions (NSTJ), and the **Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija** (`RS-KM`) among the districts and the cities and municipalities. Its five districts (Kosovski, Pećki, Prizrenski, Kosovskomitrovački, Kosovskopomoravski; ISO RS-25 … RS-29) and its municipalities as Serbian law defines them have no open boundary data — the open data follow the post-1999 division, which Serbia does not recognise and which would draw borders and names D31 forbids — so the province is one area at those levels; an application with the official geometry passes its own. The unit test checks Priština, Prizren, Peć, Kosovska Mitrovica and Gnjilane inside the province's area at every level. **For the owner to confirm:** the province as one area at district and municipality level, and its name in the data.
  3. **Map charts under Charts.** The RegionChart stories moved from "Components/Map/Region chart" to "Charts/Map/Region chart" (their pictures are renamed); the maps of Serbia are "Charts/Map/Serbia": by region, by district with the sales offices as bubbles, by city and municipality, drill-down (choosing an area opens the level under it; "Back to regions" / "Back to districts" in the header), "Show as table", phone width, Serbian names, Arabic, Japanese. Kosovo and Metohija is hatched "No data" in the stories (the invented company has no sales recorded there).
  4. **MapCanvas no longer projects before Leaflet has a view** (`hasView`): a RegionChart remounted with new areas (the drill-down) threw "Set map center and zoom first" from its tooltip and labels; found by the drill-down's interaction story.
- **2026-10-28 — Kosovo and Metohija on the package's maps of Serbia (P5.93 item 43, lead).** The open boundary data draw the post-1999 division, which the Republic of Serbia does not recognise; no open source draws the province's districts and municipalities as Serbian law defines them. The package therefore shows the Region Kosovo and Metohija among the five statistical regions and the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija as one area among the districts and among the cities and municipalities, named as Serbian law names it and inside Serbia's outline (D31). An application with official boundaries passes its own geometry.
- **2026-10-28 — The new charts take the interactive header too (P5.93 items 42, 44, lead).** The seven charts of item 44 were written beside item 42's `toggle`; they now pass it to the card as every other chart does.

## The owner's review, round 5 (P5.94)

The owner's fifth review (2026-10-29): twenty findings, each fixed as a class under the two principles (simplicity first; ease sells). Items 4 and 9 were regressions, so each has an automated check now.

- **2026-10-29 — A handled key stops where it was handled (P5.94 item 9, regression).** "Press 1, then Enter does not go on": the Questionnaire chose the option, but the key went on to the page, and Storybook's own shortcut "1" (focus the sidebar) took the focus, so Enter never reached the question. An application's own shortcuts would do the same. Every page-wide key the library handles now stops there (`stopPropagation` after `preventDefault`): the Questionnaire's number keys and Enter, the Launchpad's 1–9 and the command palette's Ctrl/Cmd+K, the last two listening on the document instead of the window. The "Number keys, interaction" story now stands in for a page shortcut that steals the focus on the digits and Enter, and still lands on question 2.
- **2026-10-29 — A button's or a label's word never breaks inside (P5.94 item 4, regression).** "Vouche r" in the payment dialog: the label carried `overflow-wrap: break-word` (from `bidi-content`/`bidi-isolate`, P5.90) in a three-column grid narrower than the word. One rule in `styles.css`, unlayered so it wins: inside a button, a tab, a menu item, a legend and a field label (one that does not wrap its control) words wrap only between words. Body text still breaks an unbroken IBAN or URL. Where a word cannot fit, the place gives it room or shortens it: the ways to pay wrap as whole buttons (on a phone the icon above the label) and a label wider than a whole row ends in "…" with the whole name in the library's Tooltip, only when it is cut (`FittedLabel`, internal). Checked in every story and mode: `tests/stories.spec.ts` measures each word inside buttons, tabs, menu items and labels (a word on two lines fails) and each button's text (running out of its box fails) — a protected change, merged by the owner. A field label or a legend whose one word is wider than its whole line (an 80-letter German word) ends that line in "…" (`text-overflow: ellipsis` with `overflow-x: clip`), so the page never scrolls sideways (D19); the accessible name keeps all of it. `brokenWords` skips text that is not drawn (a floor plan label left out with `visibility: hidden`).
- **2026-10-29 — A sale paid in parts, by any ways in any order (P5.94 item 5).** With `onAddPart` every way can take a part, so the default ways are Cash and Card (no "Split" way). The parts are a list — the way, the amount and its state ("Paid"; "Approved" for a card or an instant payment, `PaymentPart.state`) — and the remaining amount always stands beside the amount due. The keypad holds this part's amount; cash and the plain ways add it ("Add this payment"); a card takes one part at a time: "Pay 500,00 RSD by card" sends it (`onCardStart(amount)`), the terminal waits (Cancel cancels the terminal's request), approved — the application adds the part and lowers the remaining amount — or declined: the amount stays for "Try again" or another way, nothing is lost. Only cash gives change; any other part is at most the remaining amount and the way's own `maxAmount` (a voucher's value, with `maxReason`), compared exactly as decimal strings (`partOverLimit`, tested): over it, the button is unavailable with the reason under it. "Complete payment" waits with "Still to pay: …" while something remains. Cancelling after an approved part asks in the dialog, without a second dialog: "Cancelling reverses the approved payments: Card 500,00 RSD." with "Keep paying" (focused) and "Cancel payment"; Escape keeps paying; the reversal is the application's (`onCancel`). An approved part has no remove button: cancelling reverses it. The dialog still fits without scrolling: on a phone the parts are one-line chips (the way, the amount, a check for an approval; the card or voucher detail in the tooltip), the list's "Paid so far" is its accessible name, and the keypad has no Clear row (Backspace stays; "Exact amount" and the quick amounts replace the amount in one press). The dialog's own "Still to pay" describes "Complete payment" for assistive technology only, since the remaining amount stands at the top.

The value cell is a column now, so the row's baseline is always the value's first line whatever the value holds, and a note under the value never moves the label. MaskedValue's "Not allowed" keeps "Show" unavailable (aria-disabled, focusable) with its reason — the owner's answer. A scan of every story checks key/value rows.
